nodes.title: Trace recognition in dimension two over F₂
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and V,W finite-dimensional semisimple representations of Γ of the same dimension d. If Γ is a group, k=F₂ and d=2, equality of trace functions still implies V≅W.
hypotheses: Let k be a field and V,W finite-dimensional semisimple representations of Γ of the same dimension d.
proofSteps: The case k = F_2, d = 2, Γ a group: the only character Γ → F_2^× is trivial, so a semisimple representation of dimension 2 over F_2 is 1 ⊕ 1 (trace identically 0) or irreducible, with image in GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 the subgroup of order 3 or all of S_3; elements of order 3 have trace 1 and all other elements trace 0. If the image has order 3, the kernel is {g : tr = 0} and the representation is the unique irreducible 2-dimensional representation of the quotient of order 3. If the image is S_3, the set {g : tr = 0} is not a subgroup and the representation is absolutely irreducible, hence determined by its trace: the traces determine the kernel of k[Γ] → End_k(V) through the nondegenerate trace form of the matrix algebra (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible (iii)). So the trace function determines the representation in every case.
acceptance: The group hypothesis matters: for the idempotent monoid {1,e}, e acting by id and by zero on F₂² gives semisimple nonisomorphic modules of equal trace.

nodes.title: Residue field of Q̄_ℓ is an algebraic closure
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪. The field κ has characteristic ℓ, is algebraic over F_ℓ and is algebraically closed. Consequently κ≅AlgebraicClosure(F_ℓ), noncanonically.
hypotheses: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪.
proofSteps: O is a valuation ring of the field Q̄_ℓ with maximal ideal 𝔪, because the norm is multiplicative and nonarchimedean (mathlib:PadicAlgCl.normedField, mathlib:PadicAlgCl.isNonarchimedean); so κ is a field, and ‖ℓ‖ = 1/ℓ < 1 (mathlib:PadicAlgCl.valuation_p) gives characteristic ℓ.

κ is algebraic over F_ℓ: an element α of O is algebraic over Q_ℓ, and its norm is the spectral value of its minimal polynomial f over Q_ℓ (mathlib:PadicAlgCl.spectralNorm_eq), the maximum of ‖c_i‖^{1/(d−i)} over the coefficients c_i of f; so ‖α‖ ≤ 1 forces f ∈ Z_ℓ[X]. Reducing f(α) = 0 modulo 𝔪 shows that the class of α is a root of the monic polynomial f mod ℓ ∈ F_ℓ[X].

κ is algebraically closed: a monic polynomial over κ lifts to a monic f ∈ O[X]; Q̄_ℓ is algebraically closed (mathlib:PadicAlgCl is an algebraic closure), so f has a root α, which is integral over the valuation ring O and therefore lies in O (valuation rings are integrally closed); its class is a root of the given polynomial.
acceptance: The isomorphism with the chosen AlgebraicClosure(F_ℓ) is not canonical; κ itself is the canonical residue field.

nodes.title: Reduction of prime-to-ℓ roots of unity
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪. For m≥1 prime to ℓ, reduction induces a group isomorphism μ_m(Q̄_ℓ)≃μ_m(κ).
hypotheses: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪.
proofSteps: (b): the roots of X^m − 1 in Q̄_ℓ have norm 1 and lie in O. Reduction is injective on them: if ζ ≠ 1, ζ^m = 1 and ζ ≡ 1 mod 𝔪, then 0 = 1 + ζ + ⋯ + ζ^{m−1} ≡ m mod 𝔪, but m is a unit of O. Both groups have exactly m elements (Q̄_ℓ and κ are algebraically closed and m is invertible in both), so reduction is bijective.
acceptance: For m=ℓ every ℓ-th root of unity reduces to 1, so the prime-to-ℓ hypothesis is essential.

nodes.title: Finite residue fields inside the residue of Q̄_ℓ
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪. For each coefficient field E⊂Q̄_ℓ reduction embeds k_E into κ; these images cover κ. If q is an ℓ-power, the unique subfield of κ with q elements is contained in k_E for E=Q_ℓ(μ_{q−1}).
hypotheses: Let ℓ be prime, Q̄_ℓ=PadicAlgCl ℓ, O={x:‖x‖≤1}, 𝔪={x:‖x‖<1}, and κ=O/𝔪.
proofSteps: (c): E ∩ 𝔪 is the maximal ideal of the valuation ring E ∩ O of E, so k_E → κ is an injective homomorphism of fields; every element of O lies in a coefficient field, so κ is the union of the images. A subfield of κ with q elements consists of 0 and the (q−1)-th roots of unity of κ, which by (b) are the reductions of the (q−1)-th roots of unity of Q̄_ℓ, elements of Q_ℓ(μ_{q−1}) ∩ O.
acceptance: The zero element and the reductions of μ_{q−1} give all q elements, including q=2.

nodes.title: Reduction of an integral model and the residual semisimplification
nodes.statement: (a) General reduction: for a ContinuousRep (M, ρ) of Γ over a topological local ring A whose maximal ideal m_A is open (k_A := A/m_A discrete), M ⊗_A k_A is a ContinuousRep over k_A with charpoly ρ̄(g) = charpoly ρ(g) mod m_A and det ρ̄ = det ρ mod m_A. (b) For a coefficient field E (O_E, ϖ, k_E) and an integral model Λ of a ContinuousRep V over E (R01.1/integral-model), the reduction is ρ̄_Λ := Λ/ϖΛ = Λ ⊗_{O_E} k_E, a ContinuousRep of Γ over the finite field k_E with finite image; in a basis of Λ, ρ̄_Λ = ρ mod ϖ : Γ → GL_n(k_E). Its semisimplification ρ̄_Λ^ss is the residual semisimplification attached to Λ. (c) Over Q̄_ℓ: for V over Q̄_ℓ, choose E with V ≅ V_E ⊗ Q̄_ℓ (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field) and an integral model Λ of V_E, and put ρ̄ := (ρ̄_Λ ⊗_{k_E} F̄_ℓ)^ss, a semisimple ContinuousRep over F̄_ℓ (discrete), F̄_ℓ the residue field of Q̄_ℓ. Compatibilities: reduction commutes with coefficient extension E ⊂ E′ (Λ ⊗ O_{E′} reduces to ρ̄_Λ ⊗ k_{E′}), with direct sums, tensor products, duals (Λ^∨/ϖΛ^∨ ≅ (Λ/ϖΛ)^∨), twists and restriction. The reduction ρ̄_Λ itself depends on Λ; its semisimplification does not (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence).
hypotheses: m_A open in A, so the residue field is discrete and the reduction has open kernel.
E a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field k_E.
Q̄_ℓ case: the residue field of the valuation ring of Q̄_ℓ is an algebraic closure F̄_ℓ of F_ℓ (R01.1/residue-field-of-the-algebraic-closure-of-q-ell).
proofSteps: (a) M ⊗_A k_A is finite projective (free) over k_A; joint continuity holds because ϖ- or m_A-adic neighbourhoods are open, so the action on M/m_A M factors through an open subgroup (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients). Characteristic polynomials and determinants commute with the ring homomorphism A → k_A (R01.1/coefficient-extension).
(b) is (a) for A = O_E and M = Λ; finiteness of the image from R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients since k_E is finite.

(c) uses R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field for E, R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices for Λ, and R01.1/semisimplification over F̄_ℓ. The embedding k_E → F̄_ℓ, and the fact that the residue field F̄_ℓ of the valuation ring of PadicAlgCl ℓ is an algebraic closure of F_ℓ (so that it can be identified with the AlgebraicClosure (ZMod ℓ) of R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), are R01.1/residue-field-of-the-algebraic-closure-of-q-ell.
Compatibilities with operations: (Λ ⊗ Λ′)/ϖ = Λ/ϖ ⊗ Λ′/ϖ, Hom_{O_E}(Λ, O_E)/ϖ = Hom_{k_E}(Λ/ϖ, k_E) since Λ is free; restriction and twists are evident.
acceptance: Reduction of Z_ℓ(1) is μ_ℓ(F̄) with the mod ℓ cyclotomic character ω̄ = χ_ℓ mod ℓ.
For Z_ℓ acting on Q_ℓ² by (1 a; 0 1), Λ_0 = Z_ℓ² reduces to the nontrivial (1 ā; 0 1) and Λ_1 = Z_ℓ e_1 ⊕ ℓZ_ℓ e_2 to the trivial representation; both have semisimplification 1 ⊕ 1.

nodes.title: Semisimplified reduction is independent of lattice
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep. For two integral models Λ,Λ′ of V, (Λ/ϖΛ)^ss≅(Λ′/ϖΛ′)^ss over k_E.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep.
proofSteps: Second proof of (b), independent of R01.1/brauer-nesbitt: after a homothety assume Λ′ ⊂ Λ, and take a ≥ 0 with ϖ^aΛ ⊂ Λ′. The lattices Λ_i := Λ′ + ϖ^iΛ (0 ≤ i ≤ a) are Γ-stable, Λ_0 = Λ, Λ_a = Λ′ and ϖΛ_i ⊂ Λ_{i+1} ⊂ Λ_i. For Γ-stable lattices with ϖΛ ⊂ Λ′ ⊂ Λ one has [Λ/ϖΛ] = [Λ/Λ′] + [Λ′/ϖΛ] and [Λ′/ϖΛ′] = [Λ′/ϖΛ] + [ϖΛ/ϖΛ′] in the Grothendieck group of finite-length k_E[Γ]-modules, and ϖΛ/ϖΛ′ ≅ Λ/Λ′ by multiplication by ϖ. So Λ/ϖΛ and Λ′/ϖΛ′ have the same composition factors with multiplicities (additivity of Jordan–Hölder multiplicities in short exact sequences of k_E[Γ]-modules of finite length, tauceti:TauCeti.jordanHolderMultiplicity_eq_add_of_exact), that is, isomorphic semisimplifications. This uses only R01.1/integral-model and R01.1/semisimplification.
acceptance: Distinct stable lattices can have split and nonsplit reductions with the same two composition factors; the unsimplified reductions need not agree.

nodes.title: Residual reduction is independent of coefficient descent
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep. For V over Q̄_ℓ, choose any coefficient descent V_E and integral model Λ. The isomorphism class of ((Λ/ϖΛ)⊗_{k_E}κ)^ss is independent of E, of the descent and of Λ.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep.
proofSteps: Use R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field to descend V. Two descents and their Q̄_ℓ-linear comparison descend to a common coefficient field by R01.1/descent-of-qlbar-representations. Base change an integral model to its integer ring; its reduction is the corresponding residue-field base change by R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification. The common-field lattices have isomorphic semisimplified reductions by R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence, and R01.1/semisimple-representations-over-perfect-fields permits scalar extension of a semisimple representation over the finite residue field.
acceptance: A ramified enlargement changes the uniformiser but not the residual isomorphism class over κ.

nodes.title: Finite-image and polynomial properties of residual reduction
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep. The residual representation over κ is continuous, semisimple, has finite image and is defined over a finite field. For every g its characteristic polynomial is the reduction of that of V; its isomorphism class depends only on these polynomials.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with ring O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue k_E, and V a finite-dimensional ContinuousRep.
proofSteps: Choose one descent and model, whose finite residue field and jointly continuous reduction give finite image by R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients. R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field gives the same assertion over κ; semisimplification preserves characteristic polynomials by R01.1/semisimplification. Compare polynomials by R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification and conclude uniqueness by R01.1/brauer-nesbitt. Choice-independence is R01.1/residual-representation-well-defined.
acceptance: For the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character the residual polynomial is X−χ̄_ℓ(g).

nodes.title: Twisting coefficients by field automorphisms; the residual coefficient Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative topological ring, σ a continuous ring automorphism of A, and (M, ρ) a ContinuousRep of Γ over A. The coefficient twist is ρ^σ := baseChange σ M (R01.1/coefficient-extension); in framed form ρ^σ(g) = σ(ρ(g)) entrywise. It satisfies ρ^{id} = ρ, (ρ^τ)^σ ≅ ρ^{στ}, charpoly ρ^σ(g) = σ(charpoly ρ(g)), det ρ^σ = σ ∘ det ρ, and commutes with ⊕, ⊗, duals, twists and restriction. (a) Residual coefficient Frobenius: for A = F̄_p or a finite field k (discrete) and σ = Frob_p : x ↦ x^p (Mathlib frobeniusEquiv), ρ̄^{(p)} := ρ̄^{Frob_p}; for k = F_p it is ρ̄ itself. (b) Galois conjugation of ℓ-adic coefficients: for γ ∈ G_{Q_ℓ} = Gal(Q̄_ℓ/Q_ℓ) (continuous on Q̄_ℓ) and V over Q̄_ℓ, V^γ is a ContinuousRep; if V = V_E ⊗ Q̄_ℓ with integral model Λ then γ(Λ) is an integral model of V^γ over O_{γE}, and the residual representations satisfy ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V)^{γ̄}, where γ̄ ∈ Gal(F̄_ℓ/F_ℓ) is the image of γ. Consequently: (i) if γ lies in the inertia subgroup I_{Q_ℓ} (γ̄ = 1), then ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V); (ii) if γ is a lift of arithmetic Frobenius (γ̄ = Frob_ℓ), then ρ̄(V^γ) ≅ ρ̄(V)^{(ℓ)}, independently of the chosen lift. This twists the coefficients; it is not restriction of the Galois representation along a Frobenius element of the base field.
hypotheses: σ continuous (automatic for automorphisms of a discrete field and for G_{Q_ℓ} acting on Q̄_ℓ).
In (b), the surjection G_{Q_ℓ} → Gal(F̄_ℓ/F_ℓ), its kernel I_{Q_ℓ} and arithmetic Frobenius lifts are those of Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2 and 4.
Arbitrary Frobenius lifts are NOT inertia: (i) and (ii) differ unless ρ̄ is defined over F_ℓ.
proofSteps: Twist = base change along σ: R01.1/coefficient-extension, with the functoriality isomorphisms there; charpoly and det by the same compatibilities.
(a) mathlib:frobeniusEquiv gives the automorphism x ↦ x^p of the perfect field F̄_p (or k); it fixes F_p pointwise.

(b) γ is an isometry of Q̄_ℓ, so it maps O_E to O_{γE} and the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal, inducing γ̄ on residue fields; γ(Λ) is stable under ρ^γ(Γ) and (γΛ)/ϖ(γΛ) ≅ (Λ/ϖΛ)^{γ̄}. The action of G_{Q_ℓ} on the residue field and its kernel come from Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2 and 4 (stage prerequisites, with requests).

(i) γ̄ = 1 gives the claim after semisimplification (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence); (ii) two Frobenius lifts differ by inertia, so their residual twists agree, both being Frob_ℓ-twists.
acceptance: For a character χ̄ : Γ → F_{p²}^× of order p² − 1, χ̄^{(p)} = χ̄^p ≠ χ̄; for χ̄ with values in F_p^×, χ̄^{(p)} = χ̄.
Newton–Thorne (1.1), for 0 < r < p: Sym^{p+r−1} r̄ ≅^{ss} ((det r̄)^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1} r̄) ⊕ (r̄^{(p)} ⊗ Sym^{r−1} r̄), where the second summand uses the residual coefficient Frobenius of this node.

nodes.title: Teichmüller lifts of residual characters
nodes.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field (a coefficient field) with residue field k_E of cardinality q, and teichmuller E : k_E^× →* O_E^× the Teichmüller lift (Tau Ceti), the unique multiplicative section of reduction with values in μ_{q−1}(O_E). For a continuous character ψ̄ : Γ → k_E^× (k_E discrete), its Teichmüller lift is [ψ̄] := teichmuller E ∘ ψ̄ : Γ → O_E^×. Then [ψ̄] is a continuous character of finite order equal to the order of ψ̄ (dividing q − 1), [ψ̄] mod ϖ = ψ̄, and [ψ̄] is the unique lift of ψ̄ with values in μ_{q−1}(O_E) (equivalently, of finite order prime to the residue characteristic of E); [ψ̄φ̄] = [ψ̄][φ̄], [ψ̄⁻¹] = [ψ̄]⁻¹, [1] = 1; for E ⊂ E′ the Teichmüller lift over E′ restricts to the one over E on k_E^×, so [ψ̄] is independent of the coefficient field. For ψ̄ : Γ → F̄_ℓ^× (discrete), [ψ̄] is defined through any finite subfield containing the image (R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), with values in Q̄_ℓ^×. Example: ω := [ω̄] for the mod p cyclotomic character ω̄ = χ_p mod p, and for p odd χ_p = ω · ⟨χ_p⟩ with ⟨χ_p⟩ := χ_p ω⁻¹ valued in 1 + pZ_p.
hypotheses: E nonarchimedean local field; k_E finite of cardinality q.
ψ̄ continuous for the discrete topology on k_E^× (open kernel).
proofSteps: Definition and section property: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller with tauceti:TauCeti.residue_teichmuller; values in μ_{q−1}: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller_pow.
Continuity: ψ̄ has open kernel (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients), and ker[ψ̄] = ker ψ̄ because teichmuller E is injective (tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller_injective).
Uniqueness among (q−1)-torsion lifts: tauceti:TauCeti.eq_teichmuller applied pointwise (a lift χ with χ^{q−1} = 1 and χ mod ϖ = ψ̄).

Compatibility with E ⊂ E′: the Teichmüller lift over E′ of α ∈ k_E^× is a (q′−1)-torsion lift of α; since α^{q−1} = 1 and reduction is injective on prime-to-p roots of unity, it equals the E-lift (uniqueness again).
As a ContinuousRep: ofCharacter [ψ̄] (R01.1/continuous-representation); its reduction is ofCharacter ψ̄ (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification).

F̄_ℓ-valued characters: the image of ψ̄ lies in a finite subfield k of F̄_ℓ with q elements (R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field with n = 1). With F̄_ℓ the residue field of Q̄_ℓ, k lies in the residue field of the coefficient field E := Q_ℓ(μ_{q−1}) (R01.1/residue-field-of-the-algebraic-closure-of-q-ell (c)), and [ψ̄] := teichmuller E ∘ ψ̄; equivalently [ψ̄](g) is the unique (q−1)-th root of unity of Q̄_ℓ whose reduction is ψ̄(g) (part (b) of that lemma). It does not depend on E by the compatibility for E ⊂ E′.
acceptance: The Teichmüller lift of the mod p cyclotomic character of G_Q is the finite-order character ω : G_Q → Z_p^× through Gal(Q(μ_p)/Q) with ω ≡ χ_p mod p.
The Teichmüller lift of the trivial character is trivial.

nodes.title: Ribet's lemma: a lattice with nonsplit reduction
nodes.statement: Let E be a coefficient field (Ribet: K finite over Q_p) with O_E, uniformiser ϖ and residue field k, Γ a group, and V a two-dimensional E-representation of Γ that is irreducible over E and leaves some lattice stable (e.g. Γ profinite and V a ContinuousRep). Suppose the reductions of V are reducible over k, so their semisimplifications are φ_1 ⊕ φ_2 for characters φ_1, φ_2 : Γ → k^× (independent of the lattice by R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence, applied to the closure of ρ(Γ) in GL(V), which is compact because Γ stabilises a lattice, R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices (b)). Then there is a Γ-stable lattice L ⊂ V whose reduction is of the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) and is not semisimple, i.e. a nonsplit extension 0 → φ_1 → L/ϖL → φ_2 → 0. By symmetry there is also a stable lattice with nonsplit reduction (φ_2 *; 0 φ_1).
hypotheses: dim V = 2 and V irreducible over E; the conclusion is false for V = ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 reducible.

The reductions are reducible over the residue field k itself (otherwise first extend E by an unramified extension, which is allowed only if V stays irreducible over the larger field, for instance if V is absolutely irreducible).
Completeness of O_E is used (the limit lattice).
proofSteps: Choose a stable lattice and an O_E-basis, so ρ : Γ → GL_2(O_E) (R01.1/integral-model, R01.1/framed-representation); after conjugating by (0 1; 1 0) and by P = diag(1, ϖ) as needed, the reduction has the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) (Ribet: if it is (φ_1 0; * φ_2), divide upper-right entries by ϖ and multiply lower-left ones using P(a ϖb; c d)P⁻¹ = (a b; ϖc d)).

Suppose, for contradiction, that every lattice whose reduction is of the form (φ_1 *; 0 φ_2) has semisimple reduction. Ribet constructs inductively M_i = (1 t_i; 0 1) such that M_iρ(Γ)M_i⁻¹ has lower-left entries divisible by ϖ and upper-right entries divisible by ϖ^i: conjugating by P^i reduces to the hypothesis, the diagonalising matrix U = (1 u; 0 1) of the semisimple reduction gives t_{i+1} = t_i + ϖ^i u.
t_i converges in O_E (completeness), and M = (1 t; 0 1) with t = lim t_i makes all upper-right entries of Mρ(Γ)M⁻¹ zero, so ρ is reducible over E — a contradiction.
The second assertion follows by exchanging the roles of φ_1 and φ_2 (conjugating by (0 1; 1 0)).
acceptance: For V = ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 a sum of two characters Γ → O_E^× with distinct reductions (for example Γ = Ẑ, or Γ = Z/2 with ℓ odd, ψ_1 = 1 and ψ_2 the sign character; Γ = Z_ℓ is excluded, because a character of a pro-ℓ group has trivial reduction), every stable lattice is ϖ^aO e_1 ⊕ ϖ^bO e_2 (for g with ψ̄_1(g) ≠ ψ̄_2(g) the projectors (ρ(g) − ψ_j(g))/(ψ_i(g) − ψ_j(g)) preserve it) and every reduction is split: irreducibility is necessary.

Ribet's application: for p | B_k, the p-adic representation attached to a cusp form congruent to an Eisenstein series has reducible reductions with characters 1 and χ^{k−1}, and Proposition 2.1 produces ρ̄ = (1 *; 0 χ^{k−1}) nonsplit (Ribet 1976, Theorem 1.3).

nodes.title: Stable lattices are unique up to homothety
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible. All integral models of V are ϖ^jΛ₀ for one integral model Λ₀ and integers j.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible.
proofSteps: (a) Given integral models Λ, Λ′, rescale Λ′ so that Λ′ ⊂ Λ and Λ′ ⊄ ϖΛ. The image of Λ′ in Λ/ϖΛ is a nonzero Γ-stable subspace, hence everything by residual irreducibility; so Λ′ + ϖΛ = Λ and Λ′ = Λ by Nakayama (R01.1/integral-model).
acceptance: Irreducibility of the residual representation over k_E suffices; absolute irreducibility is stronger than required.

nodes.title: A self-dual integral model after rescaling the pairing
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible. For a perfect symmetric or alternating E-pairing with ⟨ρ(g)x,ρ(g)y⟩=μ(g)⟨x,y⟩, where μ:Γ→Eˣ is continuous, μ is O_Eˣ-valued and some stable lattice is self-dual for c⟨,⟩ with c∈{1,ϖ}.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible.
proofSteps: (b) µ(Γ) is compact in E^×, hence contained in O_E^× (its valuation is a compact subgroup of Z). For an integral model Λ, the orthogonal Λ^⊥ := {x ∈ V : ⟨x, Λ⟩ ⊂ O_E} is an integral model (the dual lattice transported along the perfect pairing; Γ-stable because µ is unit-valued), so Λ^⊥ = ϖ^mΛ by (a). Replacing Λ by ϖ^jΛ changes m by −2j; if m is odd replace ⟨ , ⟩ by ϖ⟨ , ⟩. Then Λ^⊥ = Λ, i.e. the pairing is perfect on Λ.
acceptance: If Λ⊥=ϖ^mΛ, rescaling Λ by ϖ^j changes m to m−2j; odd m requires multiplying the form by ϖ.

nodes.title: Integral symplectic coordinates
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible. In the alternating case, dim_E V=2g and the stable self-dual lattice has an O_E-symplectic basis. Thus the E-valued representation is GSp_{2g}(E)-conjugate to a continuous O_E-valued symplectic-similitude representation with multiplier μ.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E a coefficient field with uniformiser ϖ, and V a ContinuousRep whose residual representation over k_E is irreducible.
proofSteps: (c) A perfect alternating form on a free module over the local ring O_E has a symplectic basis: choose x with ⟨x, y⟩ ∈ O_E^× for some y (perfectness), split off the hyperbolic plane O_E x ⊕ O_E y and induct on the orthogonal complement; the matrix of ρ(g) in this basis lies in GSp_{2g}(O_E) with multiplier µ(g).
This fills the step used without proof by Calegari–Geraghty on p. 843 (recorded as ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E101).
acceptance: The symplectic-basis induction works at ℓ=2 because the form is alternating, not merely skew-symmetric.

nodes.title: Semisimple restriction to a normal subgroup
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k. If H is normal and V is semisimple over Γ, then Res_H V is semisimple in every characteristic.
hypotheses: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k.
proofSteps: Decompose V as a finite direct sum of irreducibles using R01.1/semisimplification. Each restricts semisimply by tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype; sum the restricted decompositions. No invertibility hypothesis on [Γ:H] is used.
acceptance: This applies in characteristic p even when p divides [Γ:H].

nodes.title: Clifford isotypic decomposition over an arbitrary field
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k. If H is normal and V is irreducible over Γ, then Res_H V≅(W₁⊕⋯⊕Wₜ)^{⊕e}, where the Wᵢ are the distinct Γ-conjugates of any one simple constituent and all multiplicities are equal; t is the index of its open isomorphism-class stabiliser.
hypotheses: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k.
proofSteps: R01.1/clifford-restriction-semisimple supplies semisimplicity. The sum of Γ-translates of any H-constituent is Γ-stable and nonzero, hence all of V. Conjugation permutes the H-isotypic components transitively. Because its maps are linear isomorphisms, the dimensions of the corresponding multiplicity modules over the isomorphic constituent endomorphism division rings agree, so their natural-number multiplicities agree. The stabiliser contains H and is open.
acceptance: No splitting-field or Maschke hypothesis is imposed; multiplicity is not silently replaced by a k-Hom dimension.

nodes.title: Averaging detects semisimplicity
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k. If [Γ:H] is invertible in k and Res_H V is semisimple, then V is semisimple.
hypotheses: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k.
proofSteps: (b): given a Γ-stable W ⊂ V, choose an H-equivariant projection p : V → W (Res_H V semisimple) and put p′ := [Γ : H]⁻¹ Σ_{gH ∈ Γ/H} ρ(g) p ρ(g)⁻¹; each summand depends only on the coset gH because p is H-equivariant, and p′ is a Γ-equivariant projection onto W, so W has a Γ-stable complement (mathlib:Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation is the complemented-lattice condition).
acceptance: The two-dimensional unipotent C_p-module in characteristic p restricts semisimply to 1 but is not semisimple over C_p.

nodes.title: Induction preserves semisimplicity with invertible core index
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Γ profinite, H an open subgroup, N its open normal core, and all representations finite-dimensional ContinuousReps over k. If [Γ:N] is invertible in k and U is semisimple over H, then Ind_H^Γ U is semisimple.

nodes.title: Integral models for reductive-group representations
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Ĝ a split connected reductive group scheme over Z, and Γ profinite. Every continuous ρ:Γ→Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) is Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugate into Ĝ(O_E) for some coefficient field E. No restriction on ℓ is imposed.
hypotheses: Let ℓ be prime, Ĝ a split connected reductive group scheme over Z, and Γ profinite.
proofSteps: Baire step: fix a closed embedding Ĝ ↪ GL_N over Z; it gives Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) its topology and Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) ∩ GL_N(E) = Ĝ(E). ρ(Γ) is compact, and R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field applied to Γ → GL_N(Q̄_ℓ) (closed subgroups ρ(Γ) ∩ Ĝ(E), countably many E) gives ρ(Γ) ⊂ Ĝ(E) for a coefficient field E.

Bruhat–Tits step (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2): ρ(Γ) lies in Ĝ(E)^0 (all characters O_E^×-valued, by compactness), acts on the building B(DĜ, E) of the derived group with bounded orbits, hence fixes a point; maximal compact subgroups of Ĝ(E)^0 are stabilisers of centroids of facets, and the hyperspecial point x_0 has stabiliser Ĝ(O_E).

Larsen's lemma (Larsen 1995, Lemma 2.4, recorded as a gap): there are a totally ramified E′/E and a ρ(Γ)-stable point x with i_{E,E′}(x) hyperspecial in B(DĜ, E′). Hyperspecial vertices are conjugate under Ĝ^ad(E′); lifting the conjugating element to Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) gives (i).
acceptance: For Ĝ=GL_n this follows from stable lattices without the building or pseudocharacter gaps; the general statement retains Larsen Lemma 2.4 as a gap.

nodes.title: Choice-independent reductive residual representation
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Ĝ a split connected reductive group scheme over Z, and Γ profinite. The Ĝ-completely reducible semisimplification of any integral conjugate reduced into Ĝ(F̄_ℓ) is continuous and independent of all choices up to Ĝ(F̄_ℓ)-conjugacy.

Lafforgue) — gap.

nodes.title: Reductive integral models specialise to GL_n
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, Ĝ a split connected reductive group scheme over Z, and Γ profinite. For Ĝ=GL_n the integral conjugates are framed stable lattices, complete reducibility is ordinary semisimplicity, and the reductive residual isomorphism class is the residual class from R01.1/residual-representation-well-defined.

nodes.title: Decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at a place of a number field
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, F̄ = AlgebraicClosure F, G_F = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F with its Krull topology, and O_{F̄} the integral closure of O_F in F̄, on which G_F acts. For a finite place v of F (v : HeightOneSpectrum O_F) let F_v = v.adicCompletion F, k_v its residue field, q_v = #k_v, F̄_v = AlgebraicClosure F_v and G_{F_v} = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F_v. A place of F̄ above v is a maximal ideal w̄ of O_{F̄} with w̄ ∩ O_F = v. Define the decomposition group D_{w̄} = MulAction.stabilizer G_F w̄, the inertia group I_{w̄} = Ideal.inertia G_F w̄ = {σ ∈ G_F : σx − x ∈ w̄ for all x ∈ O_{F̄}} (a subgroup of D_{w̄}), and the wild inertia group P_{w̄} ⊂ I_{w̄} as the largest closed normal pro-p subgroup of I_{w̄}, p the residue characteristic of v (by (ii) it is the image of P_{F_v} and the unique pro-p Sylow subgroup of I_{w̄}). For every field embedding ι : F̄ → F̄_v over F → F_v, let ι^* : G_{F_v} → G_F, τ ↦ ι^{-1} ∘ τ ∘ ι (Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.mapOfAlgebra F F_v for the algebra structure AlgebraicClosure F → AlgebraicClosure F_v given by ι; Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map (algebraMap F F_v) is the special case of the embedding chosen by IsAlgClosed.lift and cannot be given a prescribed ι). G_F = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F is a plain definition, so its action on F̄, on O_{F̄} and on the ideals of O_{F̄} is declared by this node (transported from AlgebraicClosure F ≃ₐ[F] AlgebraicClosure F), and let w̄(ι) be the place of F̄ pulled back from the maximal ideal of the integral closure of O_{F_v} in F̄_v. Then: (i) ι^* is a continuous injective group homomorphism and a homeomorphism onto its image, which is the closed subgroup D_{w̄(ι)}; (ii) ι^* maps the inertia group I_{F_v} = Gal(F̄_v/F_v^{ur}) and the wild inertia group P_{F_v} of Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 onto I_{w̄(ι)} and P_{w̄(ι)}, and induces D_{w̄}/I_{w̄} ≅ Gal(k̄_v/k_v) ≅ Ẑ; (iii) every place above v is w̄(ι) for some ι; for σ ∈ G_F, w̄(ι∘σ) = σ^{-1}w̄(ι) and (ι∘σ)^* = σ^{-1}·ι^*(−)·σ; two embeddings with the same place differ by an element τ_0 of G_{F_v} (ι' = τ_0∘ι), and then ι'^* = ι^* ∘ (conjugation by τ_0^{-1}); hence D_{σw̄} = σD_{w̄}σ^{-1}, I_{σw̄} = σI_{w̄}σ^{-1}, and the conjugacy classes of these subgroups depend only on v; (iv) the arithmetic Frobenius lifts at w̄ are the σ ∈ D_{w̄} with IsArithFrobAt O_F σ w̄ (σx ≡ x^{q_v} mod w̄ for x ∈ O_{F̄}); they exist and form one coset of I_{w̄} in D_{w̄}, and Frob_{σw̄} = σ Frob_{w̄} σ^{-1} modulo I_{σw̄}; geometric Frobenius lifts are their inverses; (v) for a finite Galois subextension L/F with w = w̄ ∩ O_L, the restriction of D_{w̄} to L is the stabilizer of w in Gal(L/F), and G_{F_v} → Gal(L/F) through ι^* is the composite of restriction G_{F_v} → Gal(L_w/F_v) with the inverse of the bijection decompositionHom of Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6. At a real place v, an embedding ι : F̄ → C over the real embedding gives D = {1, c_ι} with c_ι = ι^{-1}∘(complex conjugation)∘ι, an element of order 2, and changing ι conjugates c_ι in G_F.
hypotheses: F is a number field; v is a finite place for (i)–(v) and a real place for the last sentence
the embedding ι is a choice: Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map documents that it depends on an arbitrary embedding of algebraic closures, and only conjugacy classes are canonical
inertia is defined globally through the action on O_{F̄} and locally as Gal(F̄_v/F_v^{ur}); statement (ii) is the comparison
proofSteps: Continuity and the homomorphism property are Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.mapOfAlgebra for the algebra structure given by ι (Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map is used only for the comparison in the unit test localEmbeddingMap_eq_map). F_v = v.adicCompletion F is a nonarchimedean local field by Tau Ceti's isNonarchimedeanLocalField_adicCompletion (finite residue field), so the local objects I_{F_v}, P_{F_v} of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 apply to it.
Injectivity: F̄_v = F_v·ι(F̄) by algebraic-closure-of-a-completion-is-generated-by-the-global-closure, so an F_v-automorphism fixing ι(F̄) is the identity.

Image: ι^*τ preserves the pulled-back valuation, hence stabilises w̄(ι). Conversely, for each finite Galois L/F the restriction of D_{w̄} to L is the stabilizer of w, and NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6 shows decompositionHom is a bijection onto Gal(L_w/F_v); compactness of G_{F_v} and the inverse limit over L give surjectivity onto D_{w̄}. The image of a compact group in a Hausdorff group is closed, and a continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.

Inertia: τ ∈ G_{F_v} acts trivially on the residue field of F̄_v iff ι^*τ acts trivially on O_{F̄}/w̄, since the residue field of F̄_v is the algebraic closure of k_v and equals O_{F̄}/w̄ via ι. Wild inertia is the pro-p Sylow subgroup of inertia on both sides (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4).

Change of ι: direct computation of ι'^{-1}∘τ∘ι'; transitivity of G_F on places above v follows from transitivity of Gal(L/F) on the primes of L above v at every finite Galois level (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2) and compactness.

Frobenius lifts: for a finite Galois L/F inside F̄, Tau Ceti's NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt gives a Frobenius element at w̄ ∩ O_L (Mathlib's IsArithFrobAt.exists_of_isInvariant underlies it), and IsArithFrobAt.restrictNormal (stated for an arbitrary normal M/F inside any L, so it applies to L = F̄) shows that the restrictions of an arithmetic Frobenius lift at w̄ are Frobenius elements at every finite level, compatibly; the sets of Frobenius elements at w̄ ∩ O_L form an inverse system of nonempty finite sets, so a lift in G_F exists by compactness. IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia shows two lifts differ by inertia and IsArithFrobAt.conj gives the conjugation rule (Deligne 3.12 works with exactly this choice of a place of F̄ above v).
acceptance: For F = Q, v = p and L = Q(i): the image of D_{w̄} in Gal(Q(i)/Q) is trivial when p ≡ 1 mod 4 and is the whole group when p ≡ 3 mod 4 or p = 2, and the image of I_{w̄} is nontrivial only for p = 2.

For F = Q and two embeddings ι, ι' = ι∘σ, the subgroups ι^*(G_{Q_p}) and ι'^*(G_{Q_p}) are conjugate by σ and need not be equal: for p = 5 and L = Q(2^{1/3}, ζ_3) their images in Gal(L/Q) ≅ S_3 are the subgroups of order 2 generated by a transposition and by its conjugate under the image of σ, which differ when σ maps to a 3-cycle; so the decomposition group is not a normal subgroup. (That the two subgroups differ for every σ ∉ D_{w̄(ι)} is also true, but it is F. K. Schmidt's theorem that decomposition groups of distinct primes of F̄ intersect trivially, which this node does not prove and no consumer uses.)
The restriction of D_{w̄} to a finite Galois L/F agrees with MulAction.stabilizer (L ≃ₐ[F] L) w used by Tau Ceti's Ideal.zpowers_eq_stabilizer_of_isArithFrobAt at unramified w.

nodes.title: The algebraic closure of F_v is generated by F_v and the algebraic closure of F
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, v a finite place, F_v = v.adicCompletion F, F̄ = AlgebraicClosure F, F̄_v = AlgebraicClosure F_v and ι : F̄ → F̄_v a field embedding over F → F_v. Then F̄_v = F_v·ι(F̄): the intermediate field of F̄_v/F_v generated by ι(F̄) is F̄_v. Consequences: (a) an F_v-automorphism of F̄_v that fixes ι(F̄) pointwise is the identity; (b) every finite extension of F_v inside F̄_v is F_v(ι(β)) for some β ∈ F̄, hence is the completion of the number field F(β) at the place induced by ι.
hypotheses: F is a number field and v a finite place; the argument uses only that F is dense in F_v, that F_v is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, and that the characteristic is 0 (separability of minimal polynomials)
ι is an arbitrary embedding over F → F_v; its image is the algebraic closure of F in F̄_v
proofSteps: Norms: F_v is complete for a rank-one discrete valuation; with the normed-field structure Valued.toNormedField (the one used in the proof of Tau Ceti's isNonarchimedeanLocalField_adicCompletion) it is a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field, and F̄_v carries the spectral norm (Mathlib's spectralNorm, a normed-field structure extending the norm of F_v). Mathlib's instance IsKrasner.of_completeSpace then gives IsKrasner F_v F̄_v.

Approximation: let α ∈ F̄_v, with minimal polynomial f over F_v of degree n and roots α = α_1, …, α_n in F̄_v (distinct: characteristic 0); let δ = min_{i ≥ 2} ‖α − α_i‖ > 0 (any δ > 0 if n = 1). F is dense in F_v, so there is a monic g ∈ F[X] of degree n whose coefficients are so close to those of f that ‖g(α)‖ = ‖(g − f)(α)‖ < δ^n. Writing g = ∏_j (X − β_j) in F̄_v we get ∏_j ‖α − β_j‖ < δ^n, so some root β of g has ‖α − β‖ < δ.

Krasner: Mathlib's IsKrasner.krasner, with x = α and y = β (the minimal polynomial of α is separable and splits in F̄_v, β is integral over F_v as a root of the monic g, and ‖α − β‖ < ‖α − α'‖ for every conjugate α' ≠ α), gives α ∈ F_v⟮β⟯.

β is algebraic over F, and ι(F̄) is an algebraically closed subfield of F̄_v containing the image of F, so g splits in ι(F̄) and all its roots in F̄_v, in particular β, lie in ι(F̄). Hence α ∈ F_v(ι(F̄)). (Mathlib's proof of IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange carries out the same approximation.)

Consequences: (a) such an automorphism fixes F_v(ι(F̄)) = F̄_v. (b) A finite extension of F_v in F̄_v is F_v(α) for some α (primitive element, characteristic 0); with β as above, F_v(α) ⊂ F_v(β) and [F_v(β) : F_v] ≤ n = [F_v(α) : F_v], so F_v(α) = F_v(β) with β ∈ ι(F̄).
acceptance: For F = Q and v = p odd: the unramified quadratic extension of Q_p is Q_p(√a) for any integer a that is not a square modulo p, an element of ι(Q̄).
Statement (a) is the injectivity of ι^* : G_{F_v} → G_F in decomposition-group-at-a-place (i).

nodes.title: Restriction of a global representation to a decomposition group, and its independence of the embedding
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_F → Aut_A(M) be a continuous representation (R01.1 carrier: M finite projective over a topological coefficient ring A with the module topology, jointly continuous action) of the absolute Galois group of a number field F, and v a finite place. For an embedding ι : F̄ → F̄_v over F → F_v (decomposition-group-at-a-place) define the local restriction ρ_ι := ρ ∘ ι^* : G_{F_v} → Aut_A(M), a continuous representation of G_{F_v} (restriction along the continuous homomorphism ι^*, R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist). Independence: (a) for σ ∈ G_F, ρ(σ) is an isomorphism of G_{F_v}-representations (M, ρ_{ι∘σ}) → (M, ρ_ι); (b) for τ_0 ∈ G_{F_v}, ρ_ι(τ_0) is an isomorphism (M, ρ_{τ_0∘ι}) → (M, ρ_ι); since any two embeddings are related by (a) and (b), the isomorphism class of ρ|_{G_{F_v}} := [ρ_ι] depends only on ρ and v. For two embeddings ι, ι' the isomorphism (M, ρ_{ι'}) → (M, ρ_ι) obtained by composing (a) and (b) is ρ(g) with g = ι^{-1}∘ι' ∈ G_F (ι and ι' have the same image, the algebraic closure of F in F̄_v, and τ_0∘ι∘σ = ι∘(ι^*(τ_0)σ)); it depends only on (ι, ι'), not on the factorisation ι' = τ_0∘ι∘σ, and these isomorphisms compose (ρ(g)ρ(g') = ρ(gg')). It is in general not the identity of M, and ρ_ι and ρ_{ι'} are in general different homomorphisms on the same module; other isomorphisms ρ_{ι'} ≅ ρ_ι differ from it by automorphisms of ρ_ι (the commutant of ρ(D_{w̄(ι)})). The restriction is compatible with the R01.1 operations: (ρ ⊗ ρ')_ι = ρ_ι ⊗ ρ'_ι, (ρ^∨)_ι = (ρ_ι)^∨, (ρ ⊗ χ)_ι = ρ_ι ⊗ χ_ι, coefficient extension along A → B, and for L/F finite and w̄ above w | v, (ρ|_{G_L})_{ι} = (ρ_ι)|_{G_{L_w}}; for induction from an open G_L, (Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ρ)_ι ≅ ⊕_{w | v} Ind_{G_{L_w}}^{G_{F_v}} (ρ_{ι_w}) (R01.1/mackey-decomposition with D = ι^*(G_{F_v}), double cosets G_L\G_F/D ↔ places w of L above v). For ρ with finite image and kernel field K_ρ (finite Galois over F), ρ_ι factors through an injective homomorphism Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) → Aut_A(M), 𝔭 = w̄(ι) ∩ O_{K_ρ}, carrying the inertia and wild inertia subgroups of Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) onto ρ(I_{w̄}) and ρ(P_{w̄}).
hypotheses: F is a number field and v a finite place; the same construction applies at real places with D = {1, c_ι}
A, M as in R01.1 (finite projective M with the module topology)

independence is up to the isomorphism ρ(ι^{-1}∘ι'), which is not the identity of M; statements that depend on the isomorphism (for example extension classes compared at two places above v) must carry ι
proofSteps: Continuity: composite of the continuous action map with ι^* × id (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist).
(a): ρ_{ι∘σ}(τ) = ρ(σ^{-1}ι^*(τ)σ) = ρ(σ)^{-1}ρ_ι(τ)ρ(σ) by decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii); (b) likewise with τ_0.
Any two embeddings ι, ι' satisfy ι' = τ_0∘ι∘σ for some σ ∈ G_F, τ_0 ∈ G_{F_v}: choose σ with w̄(ι') = σ^{-1}w̄(ι) by transitivity, then use decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii).

Operations commute with restriction along a group homomorphism by definition; the induction formula is R01.1/mackey-decomposition for the closed subgroup D_{w̄} and open G_L, with the double cosets identified with places of L above v (finite level: NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5).

Finite image: ρ factors through Gal(K_ρ/F), ι^* restricted to Gal(K_{ρ,𝔭}/F_v) is decompositionHom^{-1} (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 5.6), injective; the inertia statement is decomposition-group-at-a-place (ii) at finite level.
acceptance: For the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ of G_Q and p ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ ∘ ι^* is the cyclotomic character of G_{Q_p}, for every ι (the restriction of a character does not depend on ι at all, since conjugation acts trivially on an abelian target).

For ρ = Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} 1 and p ≡ 1 mod 4 the restriction ρ_ι is the trivial two-dimensional representation, while for p ≡ 3 mod 4 it is Ind_{G_{Q_{p²}}}^{G_{Q_p}} 1, which is 1 ⊕ (unramified quadratic character) when 2 is invertible in A (over A = F_2 or Z_2 it is the regular representation of Z/2, not a direct sum of two characters), matching the Mackey formula with two places, respectively one place, above p.

uses.how: loc_v : H^r(G_S, M) → H^r(K_v, M) is restriction along G_v → G_S, with invariance under changing the embedding
identifies ρ̄|_{D_p} with an injective Gal(K_𝔭/Q_p) → GL_2(F) carrying inertia and wild inertia to their images
local Weil–Deligne data are computed from local restrictions of twists, restrictions and inductions
local conductors are invariants of ρ|_{G_{F_v}}
V_v is the restriction of V to the decomposition group of a chosen place of K̄ above v

nodes.title: Unramified and tamely ramified representations, and the ramification set
nodes.statement: Local: for K a nonarchimedean local field with inertia I_K and wild inertia P_K (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4) and a continuous representation ρ of G_K (or of the Weil group W_K) on M, ρ is unramified if ρ(I_K) = 1 and tamely ramified if ρ(P_K) = 1. Global: for ρ a continuous representation of G_F (F a number field) and v a finite place, ρ is unramified at v if ρ(I_{w̄}) = 1 for one, equivalently every, place w̄ of F̄ above v (equivalently ρ_ι is unramified for one, equivalently every, ι). Ram(ρ) is the set of finite places at which ρ is ramified; for p a prime, Ram^{(p)}(ρ) = Ram(ρ) minus the places above p (the set S(r̄) of CG20 when F = Q). ρ is unramified outside a set S of places if Ram(ρ) ⊂ S; equivalently ρ factors through G_{F,S} = Gal(F_S/F), F_S the maximal extension of F in F̄ unramified at every finite place outside S, with no condition at the archimedean places (this is the usual F_S when S contains the archimedean places). If ρ has open kernel (for Hausdorff A this means that the continuous ρ has finite image; in particular if A is finite discrete), Ram(ρ) is the finite set of places ramified in the kernel field K_ρ, that is Tau Ceti's NumberField.Chebotarev.ramifiedPrimes F K_ρ (a Finset of height-one primes of O_F, which the library already has; the node adds only the identification with Ram(ρ)); for ℓ-adic ρ finiteness of Ram(ρ) is a hypothesis and is carried explicitly by consumers.
hypotheses: unramifiedness at v is independent of w̄ because the I_{w̄} for w̄ | v are conjugate in G_F
Ram(ρ) contains only finite places; real places are handled by complex conjugation (R01.4, G7)
Ram(ρ) need not be finite without a hypothesis; finiteness is automatic only for finite image
proofSteps: Independence of w̄: decomposition-group-at-a-place (iii).
Factorisation through G_{F,S}: the closed normal subgroup generated by the I_{w̄}, v ∉ S, is the kernel of G_F → G_{F,S}; ρ kills it iff ρ is unramified outside S.

Finite image: ρ factors through Gal(K_ρ/F) (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients) and is unramified at v iff the inertia group at a prime of K_ρ above v is trivial, i.e. iff K_ρ/F is unramified at v (Tau Ceti Ideal.isUnramifiedAt_iff_inertia_eq_bot); the set of such v is NumberField.Chebotarev.ramifiedPrimes F K_ρ, a Finset.
acceptance: Ram(χ_ℓ) is the set of places above ℓ, for F = Q and any prime ℓ.
For E/Q with split multiplicative reduction at p and ℓ ≠ p with ℓ | v_p(q_E), the residual E[ℓ] is unramified at p while V_ℓE is ramified at p: unramifiedness of ρ̄ does not imply that of ρ.

S(r̄) is the set of primes away from p at which r̄ is ramified

nodes.title: The Frobenius characteristic polynomial P_v(ρ, X) at an unramified place
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative coefficient ring, ρ : G_F → Aut_A(M) continuous with M finite free of rank n over A (over the local coefficient rings of R01.1 every finite projective module is free; in general P_v is defined Zariski-locally on A and glues), and v a finite place at which ρ is unramified. P_v(ρ, X) := LinearMap.charpoly(ρ(Frob_{w̄})) = det(X − ρ(Frob_{w̄}) | M) ∈ A[X], where Frob_{w̄} is any ARITHMETIC Frobenius lift at any place w̄ above v (σx ≡ x^{q_v} mod w̄). It is well defined: lifts at one w̄ differ by elements of I_{w̄}, which act trivially, and lifts at σw̄ are conjugate by σ. Its trace tr ρ(Frob_v) and determinant det ρ(Frob_v) are coefficients up to sign. The geometric variant is P_v^{geom}(ρ, X) := det(X − ρ(Frob_{w̄}^{-1})) = P_v(ρ^∨, X), and the local Euler factor at an unramified v is L_v(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Frob_{w̄}^{-1})) = X^n·P_v(ρ^∨, X^{-1}) = Polynomial.reverse (P_v(ρ^∨, X)).
hypotheses: ρ unramified at v
arithmetic Frobenius (x ↦ x^{q_v}), following the plan; consumers using geometric-Frobenius polynomials (WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.1) use P_v^{geom} = P_v(ρ^∨, −)
M free of finite rank (charpoly is defined for finite free modules)
proofSteps: Independence of the lift: decomposition-group-at-a-place (iv) and unramifiedness (Mathlib IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia).

Independence of w̄: conjugate endomorphisms have equal characteristic polynomials (LinearMap.charpoly is invariant under conjugation; LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix compares with Matrix.charpoly in any basis).

Geometric variant: ρ^∨(g) is the transpose-inverse of ρ(g), so det(X − ρ^∨(Frob)) = det(X − ρ(Frob)^{-1}); reversing gives the Euler-factor identity (Polynomial.reverse, using that the constant term det(−ρ(Frob)) is a unit).
acceptance: P_v(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v for v ∤ ℓ, and P_v^{geom}(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v^{-1}.
For an elliptic curve E/Q with good reduction at p ≠ ℓ, P_p(V_ℓE, X) = X² − a_pX + p (R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial), and L_p(V_ℓE^∨, X) = 1 − a_pX + pX².

nodes.title: Unramified characters λ(α) with prescribed Frobenius value, and the geometric variant
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, R a topological commutative ring and α ∈ R^×. λ(α) : G_K → R^× is the continuous homomorphism, trivial on I_K, with λ(α)(Frob) = α for one (equivalently every) arithmetic Frobenius lift Frob, when such a homomorphism exists (CG18). It exists iff the homomorphism Z → R^×, n ↦ α^n, extends to a continuous homomorphism Ẑ = Gal(K^{ur}/K) → R^×; the extension, hence λ(α), is unique when R is Hausdorff, which is assumed from here on. A necessary condition is that n ↦ α^n is continuous for the profinite topology of Z; it is also sufficient when the closure of α^Z in R^× is complete (for instance compact), but not in general: for R = Z_ℓ ∩ Q̄ with the ℓ-adic topology and α = 1 + ℓ, n ↦ α^n is continuous for the profinite topology and the only candidate extension x ↦ (1 + ℓ)^x takes values outside R. Sufficient: the closure of α^Z in R^× is a profinite group, e.g. R^× profinite, as for R a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field, R = O_E, or R finite discrete; then λ(α) = (lift of n ↦ α^n to the profinite completion of Z) ∘ (G_K ↠ Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ). For R = E finite over Q_ℓ, λ(α) exists iff α ∈ O_E^×; for R = C (complex topology) iff α is a root of unity. The geometric variant (CG20) λ^{geom}(γ) sends a geometric Frobenius to γ: λ^{geom}(γ) = λ(γ^{-1}). On the Weil group no condition is needed: λ_W(α)(w) = α^{weilDegree(w)} defines an unramified character W_K → R^× for every α ∈ R^×, and λ_W(α) extends to G_K iff λ(α) exists. For a number field F and finite place v, λ_v(α) denotes λ(α) on G_{F_v}, transported to D_{w̄} by ι^*.
hypotheses: arithmetic normalisation for λ (CG18), geometric for λ^{geom} (CG20); the two differ by inversion
existence is a condition on α and the topology of R, not automatic
R is Hausdorff (needed for uniqueness of λ(α); every coefficient ring of R01.1 is)
proofSteps: G_K/I_K ≅ Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ with Frob ↦ 1 (LocalFieldsRamification layers 2 and 4). Here Ẑ is Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.completion (GrpCat.of (Multiplicative ℤ)), with eta the canonical map from ℤ and denseRange its density.

If the closure H of α^Z is profinite, Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.lift extends n ↦ α^n to Ẑ → H, and lift_eta gives λ(α)(Frob) = α; uniqueness is lift_unique (Z is dense in Ẑ, ProfiniteCompletion.denseRange). Mathlib's lift is bundled and universe-monomorphic: H has to be a ProfiniteGrp in the universe of ℤ (Type 0), so for a coefficient ring in a higher universe the node passes through a ULift or constructs the extension directly from density and completeness of H.

Necessity: a continuous extension restricts to the profinite topology on Z. For R = E: the image of the compact group Ẑ is bounded, forcing |α| = 1; conversely O_E^× is profinite. For R = C: a continuous homomorphism from a profinite group to C^× has finite image (C^× has no small subgroups), so α has finite order.
The Weil-group version uses W_K/I_K ≅ Z via weilDegree (ClassFieldTheory layer 9) and needs no extension.
acceptance: For ℓ ≠ p and K/Q_p finite, λ(q) : G_K → Z_ℓ^× equals the restriction of the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character χ_ℓ to G_K.
λ(ℓ) : G_K → Q_ℓ^× does not exist, while λ_W(ℓ) : W_K → Q_ℓ^× does.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic cyclotomic character, Dirichlet characters as Galois characters, and their Frobenius values
nodes.statement: (a) For a field F of characteristic ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ : G_F → Z_ℓ^× is Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter (AlgebraicClosure F) ℓ composed with G_F → RingAut(F̄); it is continuous (cyclotomicCharacter.continuous) and σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} for ζ ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}(F̄) (cyclotomicCharacter.spec); its reduction mod ℓ^n is modularCyclotomicCharacter; Z_ℓ(1) of R01.1/tate-twist is A = Z_ℓ with this action. (b) For K a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p ≠ ℓ, χ_ℓ|_{G_K} is unramified with χ_ℓ(Frob) = q for arithmetic Frobenius, i.e. χ_ℓ|_{G_K} = λ(q); for F a number field and v ∤ ℓ finite, χ_ℓ is unramified at v and P_v(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q_v. (c) For N ≥ 1 and a Dirichlet character ε : (Z/N)^× → R^× (Mathlib DirichletCharacter R N on units), ε_Gal := ε ∘ galEquivZMod ∘ (restriction G_Q → Gal(Q(ζ_N)/Q)) is a continuous finite-order character of G_Q (any topology on R); it is unramified at every p ∤ N with ε_Gal(Frob_p) = ε(p mod N) for arithmetic Frobenius, Ram(ε_Gal) is the set of primes dividing the conductor of ε, and ε_Gal(c) = ε(−1) for complex conjugation c. Characters induced from divisors of N give the same Galois character. (d) Every finite-order character G_Q → R^× with open kernel (in particular every continuous character with finite image when R is Hausdorff) is ε_Gal for a unique primitive ε (Kronecker–Weber, Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 13). A continuous character of finite order has finite image when R^× has only finitely many elements of each finite order (for instance when R is a domain), but not in general: for R = F_2[[t]][η]/(η²), a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field F_2, the subgroup 1 + ηF_2[[t]] of R^× is an infinite profinite group of exponent 2, isomorphic to ∏_N Z/2; G_Q maps continuously onto it through Gal(Q(√p : p prime)/Q) ≅ ∏_p Z/2, and the resulting continuous character of order 2 has infinite image, so its kernel is not open and it is not ε_Gal for any Dirichlet character ε. (e) The mod-p cyclotomic character χ̄_p = χ_p mod p equals ε_Gal for ε = (Z/p)^× → F_p^× the identity; its Teichmüller lift ω_p : G_Q → Z_p^× (R01.1/teichmuller-lift-of-a-residual-character) satisfies χ_p = ω_p·⟨χ_p⟩ with ⟨χ_p⟩ valued in 1 + pZ_p (1 + 4Z_2 for p = 2, where ω_2 is taken modulo 4).
hypotheses: χ_ℓ is valued in Z_ℓ^× and is trivial when F̄ lacks ℓ-power roots of unity (never for char F ≠ ℓ)
arithmetic Frobenius throughout; the Hodge–Tate weight of χ_p (+1 in the plan, −1 in CG20) is PadicHodgeTheory's convention, not fixed here
for p = 2 the Teichmüller decomposition uses (Z/4)^× (the torsion of Z_2^× is {±1})
proofSteps: (a) is Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter with spec, toZModPow and continuous. cyclotomicCharacter.spec and cyclotomicCharacter.toZModPow carry the instance hypothesis [∀ i, HasEnoughRootsOfUnity L (ℓ ^ i)]; for L = AlgebraicClosure F and ℓ ≠ char F Mathlib provides it, which is why (a) assumes char F ≠ ℓ. 'Its reduction mod ℓ^n is modularCyclotomicCharacter' is the theorem cyclotomicCharacter.toZModPow, not part of the definition.

(b): an arithmetic Frobenius lift acts on μ_{ℓ^n} ⊂ O_{K̄}^× by ζ ↦ ζ' with ζ' ≡ ζ^q mod the maximal ideal; reduction is injective on μ_{ℓ^n} for ℓ ≠ p, so ζ' = ζ^q; inertia acts trivially because the extension K(μ_{ℓ^∞})/K is unramified (LocalFieldsRamification layer 2).

(c): galEquivZMod_apply_of_pow_eq gives σ(ζ) = ζ^{a(σ)}. For p ∤ N and a prime P of Q(ζ_N) above p, Mathlib's galEquivZMod_stabilizer says that galEquivZMod maps the decomposition group of P onto the subgroup of (Z/N)^× generated by p; the node adds that the Frobenius element itself maps to p (it acts as ζ ↦ ζ^p modulo P and reduction is injective on μ_N for p ∤ N; this is the cyclotomic example of NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2), so ε_Gal(Frob_p) = ε(p). Change of level is Mathlib's galEquivZMod_restrictNormal_apply. Complex conjugation inverts ζ, so ε_Gal(c) = ε(−1); Q(ζ_N)/Q is ramified exactly at p | N, and ε_Gal is ramified at p iff ε is not trivial on the p-part, i.e. iff p divides the conductor.
(d) is Kronecker–Weber with the identification of Gal(Q^{ab}/Q) with Ẑ^× through cyclotomicCharacter.

(e): ω_p is the Teichmüller lift of χ̄_p in the sense of R01.1/teichmuller-lift-of-a-residual-character for the coefficient field E = Q_p. Tau Ceti's teichmuller Q_p is a homomorphism 𝓀[Q_p]^× → 𝒪[Q_p]^×, so the node supplies three things that the library does not state: the identifications 𝒪[Q_p] = Z_p and 𝓀[Q_p] = Z/p as rings (they occur only inside the proof of Padic.natCard_residueField in Tau Ceti); the splitting Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p), deduced from TauCeti.residue_teichmuller (the Teichmüller map is a section of reduction, and the kernel of reduction on units is 1 + pZ_p); and, for p = 2, the character ω_2 := χ_2 mod 4 : G_Q → {±1} ⊂ Z_2^×, constructed directly, because teichmuller Q_2 is trivial (𝓀[Q_2]^× is trivial).
acceptance: For the character ε = χ_{−4} of (Z/4)^×: ε_Gal(Frob_p) = (−1)^{(p−1)/2} for odd p, ε_Gal(c) = −1, and ε_Gal is the character of Q(i)/Q.
χ_ℓ(Frob_p) = p for every prime p ≠ ℓ, and χ_ℓ is ramified at ℓ with χ_ℓ(I_ℓ) = Z_ℓ^×.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic tame character t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of characteristic p and cardinality q, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Let θ : I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1) = lim_{p ∤ m} μ_m(K̄) be the tame character of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 and Z_ℓ(1) = lim_n μ_{ℓ^n}(K̄) (R01.1/tate-twist). Define t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1) as θ composed with the projection to the ℓ-component; explicitly t_ℓ(σ) = (σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n})_n for a uniformiser π and a compatible system of roots. Then: (i) t_ℓ is a continuous surjective homomorphism, independent of π and the roots, trivial on P_K; (ii) Kummer reductions: t_ℓ mod ℓ^n is σ ↦ σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n} ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}; (iii) equivariance: t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)·t_ℓ(σ) for w ∈ G_K, σ ∈ I_K; for w ∈ W_K this is q^{weilDegree(w)}·t_ℓ(σ); (iv) every continuous homomorphism from I_K (or from an open subgroup J of I_K) to a pro-ℓ group factors through t_ℓ (through t_ℓ|_J); in particular I_K has exactly one quotient of order ℓ, namely t_ℓ mod ℓ : I_K ↠ μ_ℓ; (v) for L/K finite with ramification index e, t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L}; (vi) a trivialisation T : Z_ℓ(1) ≅ Z_ℓ (a choice of compatible primitive ℓ^n-th roots of unity) gives T∘t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ, and changing T multiplies it by a unit of Z_ℓ. t_ℓ does not extend to a homomorphism on G_K or W_K (by (iii) such an extension would be invariant under conjugation by Frobenius, which multiplies t_ℓ by q ≠ 1).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p
K has finite residue field (a nonarchimedean local field); the construction for henselian traits with other residue fields stays with LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0
t_ℓ is a character of inertia only
proofSteps: (i)–(ii): LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 (the tame character, its independence of choices, its finite-level form) followed by the projection Ẑ^{(p')}(1) → Z_ℓ(1).

(iii): the G_K-equivariance statement of layer 4 (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with χ_ℓ from cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters; on W_K, χ_ℓ(w) = q^{weilDegree w} because χ_ℓ = λ(q) on G_K.

(iv): a pro-ℓ quotient kills the pro-p group P_K and factors through the abelian group I_K/P_K ≅ ∏_{ℓ' ≠ p} Z_{ℓ'}(1), whose maximal pro-ℓ quotient is the ℓ-factor; the order-ℓ quotients correspond to Hom(Z_ℓ(1), Z/ℓ), a line over F_ℓ.
(v): with π_K = u·π_L^e, σ ∈ I_L fixes the ℓ^n-th roots of the unit u (they generate an unramified extension), so σ(π_K^{1/ℓ^n})/π_K^{1/ℓ^n} = (σ(π_L^{1/ℓ^n})/π_L^{1/ℓ^n})^e.
acceptance: For K = Q_p and σ ∈ I with σ(p^{1/ℓ}) = ζ_ℓ p^{1/ℓ}, t_ℓ(σ) ≡ ζ_ℓ in μ_ℓ.

For K = Q_2 and ℓ = 3, the unique quotient of order 3 of I_2 is t_3 mod 3 : I_2 ↠ μ_3, through which every unipotent action of I_2 on an F_3-vector space of dimension at most 3 factors (a unipotent u with (u − 1)³ = 0 has u³ = 1 in characteristic 3); in particular every two-dimensional one (ClassicalSerreModularity R33.3 at (q, N) = (3, 2)). In dimension 4 the Jordan block of size 4 over F_3 has order 9 and gives a unipotent action of I_2 through t_3 mod 9 that does not factor through t_3 mod 3.

nodes.title: Tame inertia, the level of a character, and the fundamental characters of levels one and two
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of characteristic p, I_K ⊃ P_K and I_t = I_K/P_K (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4), k̄ the residue field of K̄. For n ≥ 1 and Q = p^n, the fundamental character of level n is θ_{Q−1} : I_t → μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× ⊂ k̄^× (reduction modulo the maximal ideal), σ ↦ σ(π^{1/(Q−1)})/π^{1/(Q−1)}, independent of the uniformiser and the root; the fundamental characters of level n are its n conjugates θ_{Q−1}^{p^i}, 0 ≤ i < n, and, for a field k_1 of characteristic p, a character I_t → k_1^× is fundamental of level n if it is θ_{Q−1} followed by an embedding F_Q ↪ k_1. These induce I_t ≅ lim F_{p^n}^× (transition maps the norms). A character of I_t is of level n if it factors through F_{p^n}^× (via θ_{p^n−1}) and through no F_{p^m}^× with m a proper divisor of n. Conjugation by an arithmetic Frobenius lift s acts on I_t by u ↦ u^{#k}, so θ(sus^{-1}) = θ(u)^{#k} for every fundamental character θ. For K = Q_p: the level-1 fundamental character is ω = θ_{p−1} = χ̄_p|_{I}; the two level-2 fundamental characters ψ = ω_2, ψ' = ω_2^p satisfy ψψ' = ω_2^{p+1} = ω; for a finite extension K/Q_p with ramification index e, χ̄_p|_{I_K} = θ_{p−1}^e. The residual character ω_{p,2}, its Teichmüller lift [ω_{p,2}] := teichmuller(Q_{p²}) ∘ ω_{p,2} : I_t → μ_{p²−1}(𝒪[Q_{p²}]) ⊂ 𝒪[Q_{p²}]^× (TauCeti.teichmuller for the unramified quadratic extension Q_{p²} of Q_p; 𝒪[Q_{p²}] is the ring of Witt vectors W(F_{p²}), an identification the library does not contain and this node does not need) and its ℓ-adic incarnations are three distinct declarations, although the sources use one symbol.
hypotheses: level is a property of a character of I_t, not of a representation of G_K
the level-1/level-2 dichotomy is specific to dimension two (tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations)
the comparison with local class field theory has a sign: Serre 1972 Proposition 3 shows the tame character and the reciprocity map on units are opposite
proofSteps: θ_{Q−1} is the Q−1 component of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4's tame character I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1), read in the residue field. The reduction μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× is obtained from TauCeti.rootsOfUnityEquivResidueFieldUnits, which is stated for a nonarchimedean local field and the exponent #𝓀 − 1: apply it to an unramified extension K_Q of K inside K̄ whose residue field contains F_Q (LocalFieldsRamification layer 2) and note that μ_{Q−1}(K̄) = μ_{Q−1}(K_Q), because X^{Q−1} − 1 already splits in K_Q. The inverse limit statement is Serre 1972 Proposition 2.
Conjugation: layer 4's equivariance (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with the cyclotomic character of an arithmetic Frobenius acting on prime-to-p roots of unity by the #k-th power.
ω = θ_{p−1} on I_{Q_p}: K(μ_p) = K((−p)^{1/(p−1)}) and (ζ^a − 1)/(ζ − 1) ≡ a modulo the maximal ideal (Serre 1972 Proposition 8, recorded there as the e-th power for ramification index e).
ψψ' = ψ^{1+p} = θ_{p²−1}^{(p²−1)/(p−1)} = θ_{p−1} by the norm compatibility of the θ's.
acceptance: The product of the two level-2 fundamental characters of I_{Q_p} is the restriction of the mod-p cyclotomic character.
On an explicit supersingular elliptic curve over Q_p with good reduction (p odd), the tame characters of E[p] are the two level-2 fundamental characters (Serre 1972 1.11; R01.6 supplies the curve).

nodes.title: Semisimple residual local representations are tame; levels and induced representations in dimension two
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, k_1 a field of characteristic p with the discrete topology and ρ̄ : G_K → GL(V) a continuous representation on a finite-dimensional k_1-vector space. (a) If ρ̄ is semisimple then ρ̄(P_K) = 1; hence for any ρ̄, P_K acts trivially on the semisimplification V^{ss} (R01.1/semisimplification) and I_K acts on V^{ss} through I_t; ρ̄(I_t) is cyclic of order prime to p, and over k̄_1 the action of I_t on V^{ss} is a sum of characters, each a product of powers of fundamental characters, the multiset of which is stable under χ ↦ χ^{#k}. (b) (K = Q_p, dim V = 2, k_1 = F̄_p) The two characters φ, φ' of I_t on V^{ss} are of level 1 or 2; if of level 2 they are conjugate: φ' = φ^p, φ = φ'^p, φ ≠ φ'. (c) If φ, φ' are of level 2, V is irreducible; conversely an irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ has level 2. (d) Let Q_{p²} ⊂ Q̄_p be the unramified quadratic extension and χ : G_{Q_{p²}} → F̄_p^× continuous with χ|_{I} = ω_2^j. Then ind(χ) := Ind_{G_{Q_{p²}}}^{G_{Q_p}} χ restricted to I_{Q_p} is ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj}, and ind(χ) is irreducible iff (p+1) ∤ j; every irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ is of this form. When (p+1) | j, χ extends to a character χ̃ of G_{Q_p} and ind(χ) ≅ χ̃ ⊗ Ind_{G_{Q_{p²}}}^{G_{Q_p}} 1; for p odd this is χ̃ ⊕ χ̃η with η the unramified quadratic character, and for p = 2 it is a non-split extension of χ̃ by χ̃ (the regular representation of Z/2 in characteristic 2, where η is trivial), with semisimplification χ̃ ⊕ χ̃.
hypotheses: k_1 has characteristic p equal to the residue characteristic (residual representations at p)
semisimplicity in (a) is with respect to G_K; P_K need not act trivially on V itself
(b)–(d) are two-dimensional statements over Q_p; for K with residue field F_{p^f} the Frobenius acts by the p^f-th power
proofSteps: (a) Serre 1972 Proposition 4: ρ̄(P_K) is a finite p-group (open kernel), its invariants V' ≠ 0 form a G_K-stable subspace because P_K is normal; semisimplicity and induction on dimension give ρ̄(P_K) = 1. Then I_t acts through a finite cyclic group of order prime to p (I_t is procyclic of order prime to p), hence diagonalisably over k̄_1, through characters which are powers of fundamental characters (tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters); stability under the #k-th power is conjugation by a Frobenius lift.

(b) Serre 1987 Proposition 1: conjugation by a Frobenius lift s satisfies sus^{-1} ≡ u^p mod I_p, so {φ, φ'} is stable under the p-th power; either both are fixed (level 1) or they are swapped (level 2).

(c) Serre 1987 2.2: a stable line would give a character of I_t extending to G_p, hence of level 1. Conversely let ρ̄ be irreducible (hence semisimple, so (a) applies) with φ, φ' of level 1: if φ = φ', twisting by a power of χ̄_p extending φ makes ρ̄ unramified, with procyclic image, hence reducible over F̄_p; if φ ≠ φ', conjugation by a Frobenius lift maps the φ-eigenline of I_t to the φ^{1/p} = φ eigenline, so both eigenlines are G_p-stable; either way ρ̄ is reducible.

(d) Mackey: Res_I Ind χ = χ|_I ⊕ χ^s|_I with s a Frobenius lift, and χ^s|_I = ω_2^{pj} by the conjugation rule; irreducibility holds iff χ ≠ χ^s, by a direct argument valid in every characteristic: Res_{G_{Q_{p²}}} ind(χ) = χ ⊕ χ^s (Mackey for the normal subgroup G_{Q_{p²}}), and a G_{Q_p}-stable line is G_{Q_{p²}}-stable, so if χ ≠ χ^s it is the χ- or the χ^s-eigenline, and s exchanges these two, so there is none; if χ = χ^s then χ extends to χ̃ (G_{Q_p}/G_{Q_{p²}} is cyclic and F̄_p^× is divisible), and ind(χ) = χ̃ ⊗ ind(1) contains the line χ̃ ⊗ (constant functions). Finally χ ≠ χ^s iff ω_2^j ≠ ω_2^{pj} on I, because χ/χ^s is trivial at s², a Frobenius lift of Q_{p²}, so it is trivial as soon as it is unramified; i.e. iff (p² − 1) ∤ j(p − 1), i.e. (p+1) ∤ j. If (p+1) | j then ω_2^j = ω^{j/(p+1)} on I and χ = ω^{j/(p+1)}μ with μ unramified, which extends. Every irreducible ρ̄ has level 2 by (c), so I_t acts by ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj} with distinct characters; the Frobenius of Q_{p²} acts on I_t by the p²-th power and fixes both, so G_{Q_{p²}} preserves the two eigenlines, ρ̄|_{G_{Q_{p²}}} = χ ⊕ χ^s, and Frobenius reciprocity gives ρ̄ ≅ ind(χ).
acceptance: For 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, ind(ω_2^{k−1}) is irreducible (1 ≤ k − 1 ≤ p < p + 1), as used by OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5.
For p = 3 and j = 4, ω_2^4 = ω on I and ind(χ) is reducible.

nodes.title: The exponential of nilpotent elements and the logarithm of unipotent elements are inverse to each other
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring that is a Q-algebra (not necessarily commutative). For a nilpotent N ∈ A let exp(N) = Σ_{i ≥ 0} N^i/i! (Mathlib's IsNilpotent.exp, a finite sum), and for u ∈ A with u − 1 nilpotent (u unipotent) let log(u) = Σ_{i ≥ 1} (−1)^{i+1}(u − 1)^i/i (a finite sum). Then: (i) exp(N) is unipotent and log(u) is nilpotent; (ii) log(exp(N)) = N and exp(log(u)) = u, so exp and log are mutually inverse bijections between the nilpotent and the unipotent elements of A, and exp is injective on nilpotent elements; (iii) for a ring homomorphism f : A → B of Q-algebras, f(log u) = log(f u) and f(exp N) = exp(f N); in particular log(aua^{-1}) = a·log(u)·a^{-1} and exp(aNa^{-1}) = a·exp(N)·a^{-1} for a ∈ A^×; (iv) exp(mN) = exp(N)^m and log(u^m) = m·log(u) for m ∈ Z, and for m ≥ 1 the element exp(m^{-1}·log u) is the unique unipotent m-th root of u; it is a polynomial in u with rational coefficients; (v) if E is a finite extension of Q_ℓ, V a finite-dimensional E-vector space and h : Z_ℓ → GL(V) a continuous homomorphism with h(1) unipotent, then h(x) = exp(x·log h(1)) for every x ∈ Z_ℓ.
hypotheses: A is a Q-algebra: the denominators i! and i are needed; no commutativity is assumed

Mathlib has IsNilpotent.exp with its functional equation for commuting nilpotent elements, its units and its naturality; it has no logarithm of unipotent elements and no statement that exp is injective or surjective onto unipotent elements; that is what this node adds
no convergence is involved: all sums are finite
proofSteps: (i): exp(N) − 1 is nilpotent by Mathlib's IsNilpotent.isNilpotent_exp_sub_one; log(u) is (u − 1) times a polynomial in u − 1, hence nilpotent.

Reduction to the commutative case: N, exp(N) and log(exp N) lie in the commutative subring Q[N], and u, log u, exp(log u) in Q[u]; so for (ii) one may assume A commutative, with N^k = 0 (resp. (u − 1)^k = 0) and all sums stopping at k − 1.

log(exp N) = N: in A[t] put Y(t) = exp(tN) − 1 = Σ_{1 ≤ i < k} t^iN^i/i! and G(t) = L(Y(t)), where L(Y) = Σ_{1 ≤ i < k} (−1)^{i+1}Y^i/i. Then dY/dt = N(1 + Y) (the missing term is a multiple of N^k = 0) and L'(Y)(1 + Y) = 1 − (−Y)^{k−1}, so dG/dt = N − N(−Y)^{k−1} = N, because Y is divisible by N. As G(0) = 0 and A is a Q-algebra, G(t) = tN (a polynomial over a Q-algebra is determined by its derivative and constant term); evaluate at t = 1.

exp(log u) = u: with Y = u − 1, Y^k = 0, put Λ(t) = L(tY) and H(t) = E(Λ(t)), E(Z) = Σ_{i < k} Z^i/i!. Then (1 + tY)·dΛ/dt = Y(1 − (−tY)^{k−1}) = Y, and dH/dt = (E(Λ) − Λ^{k−1}/(k−1)!)·dΛ/dt with Λ^{k−1}·dΛ/dt a multiple of Y^k = 0; so (1 + tY)·dH/dt = Y·H. The polynomial 1 + tY satisfies the same equation and has the same value 1 at t = 0, and it is a unit of A[t]; the quotient H/(1 + tY) has derivative 0 and value 1 at 0, hence H = 1 + tY; evaluate at t = 1.

(iii): log and exp are polynomial expressions with rational coefficients, so they commute with homomorphisms of Q-algebras (for exp this is Mathlib's IsNilpotent.map_exp); conjugation by a unit is such a homomorphism.

(iv): exp(mN) = exp(N)^m for m ≥ 0 by IsNilpotent.exp_add_of_commute and induction, and for m < 0 because exp(−N) is the inverse of exp(N) (same lemma with exp(0) = 1; this is how IsNilpotent.isUnit_exp is proved). Applying log to exp(m·log u) = u^m gives log(u^m) = m·log u. If v is unipotent with v^m = u then m·log v = log u, so v = exp(m^{-1}·log u): existence, uniqueness, and v ∈ Q[u].

(v): x ↦ exp(x·log h(1)) = Σ_i x^i(log h(1))^i/i! is a polynomial function of x ∈ Z_ℓ ⊂ E, hence continuous; it agrees with h on the natural numbers by (iv); N is dense in Z_ℓ and GL(V) is Hausdorff, so the two continuous maps agree.
acceptance: For N with N³ = 0: exp(N) = 1 + N + N²/2 and log(1 + N + N²/2) = (N + N²/2) − (N + N²/2)²/2 = N.
For the Jordan block u = 1 + N, N³ = 0: log u = N − N²/2 and exp(N − N²/2) = 1 + (N − N²/2) + N²/2 = u; the unipotent square root of u is exp((N − N²/2)/2) = 1 + N/2 − N²/8.

nodes.title: Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem (arithmetic quasi-unipotence)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q, q = p^f, W_K its Weil group with the Weil topology (ClassFieldTheory layer 9), ℓ ≠ p a prime, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ, V a finite-dimensional E-vector space and ρ : W_K → GL(V) continuous for the Weil topology and the ℓ-adic topology (for instance the restriction of a continuous representation of G_K). Then there is a unique nilpotent N ∈ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(Z_ℓ(1), End_E V) = End(V)(−1) and an open subgroup J ⊂ I_K such that ρ(σ) = exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) for all σ ∈ J (exp of a nilpotent endomorphism, a finite sum). Moreover ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) for w ∈ W_K, x ∈ Z_ℓ(1); after a trivialisation T of Z_ℓ(1), N' := N(T^{-1}1) satisfies ρ(w)N'ρ(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N', i.e. ρ(Φ)N'ρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN' for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and ρ(F)N'ρ(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N' for a geometric one. Consequences: every ρ(σ), σ ∈ I_K, is quasi-unipotent (eigenvalues roots of unity); ρ(I_K) is finite iff N = 0; N is the same for ρ and for every restriction ρ|_{W_L}, L/K finite, up to the factor e(L/K) of t_ℓ (N_L = e·N_K); coefficients in Q̄_ℓ are covered after descent to a finite E (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field).
hypotheses: ℓ different from the residue characteristic p

finite residue field: the argument uses that Frobenius multiplies t_ℓ by q, which is not a root of unity; for K = C((t)) the character σ ↦ (1+ℓ)^{T(t_ℓ(σ))} of I_K = G_K is continuous and not quasi-unipotent, so the statement fails for algebraically closed residue fields (where LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1 supplies the geometric theorem)
quasi-unipotence holds on an open subgroup only; ρ need not be unipotent on I_K
N is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' depends on T and is multiplied by a^{-1} when T is replaced by aT (N(x) = T(x)·N' for x ∈ Z_ℓ(1))
only finite residue fields are treated; the general hypothesis of Serre–Tate (no finite extension of the residue field contains all ℓ-power roots of unity) is not covered by this node
proofSteps: Deligne states the theorem as 8.2 for a nonarchimedean local field (finite residue field) and E_λ finite over Q_ℓ, and refers to Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties (his [13]), for the proof; the argument below is the standard one and is complete for finite residue fields.

Lattice: ρ(I_K) is compact, so it stabilises an O_E-lattice (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices); J := ρ|_{I_K}^{-1}(1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E)) is open in I_K and ρ(J) is a closed subgroup of the pro-ℓ group 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E).

Factorisation: by ell-adic-tame-character (iv), ρ|_J = h ∘ t_ℓ|_J for a continuous homomorphism h : t_ℓ(J) → 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E); t_ℓ(J) = ℓ^m Z_ℓ(1) is free of rank one over Z_ℓ; fix a generator γ_0 and put g = h(γ_0).

Unipotence: let Φ be an arithmetic Frobenius lift and J' = J ∩ Φ^{-1}JΦ, open in J, so t_ℓ(J') = ℓ^kt_ℓ(J) for some k ≥ 0. Take σ ∈ J' with t_ℓ(σ) = ℓ^kγ_0. Then ρ(σ) = g^{ℓ^k} and, since t_ℓ(ΦσΦ^{-1}) = q·t_ℓ(σ) (ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), ρ(Φ)g^{ℓ^k}ρ(Φ)^{-1} = h(qℓ^kγ_0) = (g^{ℓ^k})^q. So the eigenvalues of g' := g^{ℓ^k} (in an algebraic closure of E, with multiplicity) are permuted by λ ↦ λ^q; each satisfies λ^{q^r} = λ for some r ≥ 1, hence is a root of unity. They are ≡ 1 modulo ℓ² in the ring of integers, and a root of unity ζ ≡ 1 mod ℓ² is 1: if ζ ≠ 1 has order m prime to ℓ, then 1 − ζ divides m = ∏_{0 < j < m}(1 − ζ^j) and is an ℓ-adic unit; if ℓ divides the order, a power ζ' of order ℓ has v(ζ' − 1) = v(ℓ)/(ℓ − 1) < 2v(ℓ), although ζ' ≡ 1 mod ℓ². So g' is unipotent. This is the only place where the finite residue field is used: q is an integer ≥ 2.

Definition of N: Z_ℓ(1) ⊗ Q is the line Q_ℓ·γ_0; put N(a·ℓ^kγ_0) := a·log(g') for a ∈ Q_ℓ, a nilpotent endomorphism for each a (nilpotent-exponential-and-unipotent-logarithm (i)), Z_ℓ-linear in the argument. For σ ∈ J' write t_ℓ(σ) = aℓ^kγ_0 with a ∈ Z_ℓ; then ρ(σ) = h(aℓ^kγ_0) = exp(a·log g') = exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) by nilpotent-exponential-and-unipotent-logarithm (v), applied to the continuous homomorphism a ↦ h(aℓ^kγ_0) of Z_ℓ. Here exp is the finite sum IsNilpotent.exp; no ℓ-adic series is used.

Conjugation: for w ∈ W_K and σ in the open subgroup J' ∩ w^{-1}J'w, exp(ρ(w)N(t_ℓ(σ))ρ(w)^{-1}) = ρ(wσw^{-1}) = exp(N(χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ))) (ell-adic-tame-character (iii) and (iii) of the logarithm node); both arguments are nilpotent, so they are equal by injectivity of exp, and Z_ℓ-linearity gives ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) for all x. (Nilpotence of N was obtained in the previous steps, not from this relation.)

Uniqueness: two pairs (N_1, J_1), (N_2, J_2) give exp(N_1(t_ℓ(σ))) = exp(N_2(t_ℓ(σ))) on J_1 ∩ J_2, hence N_1 = N_2 on the open subgroup t_ℓ(J_1 ∩ J_2) by injectivity of exp on nilpotent elements, and everywhere by linearity.

ρ(I_K) finite iff N = 0: if N = 0, ρ is trivial on the open subgroup J' of the compact group I_K; if ρ(I_K) is finite, exp(N(x)) has finite order m for x ∈ t_ℓ(J'), so exp(mN(x)) = 1 and N(x) = 0. Quasi-unipotence of every ρ(σ), σ ∈ I_K: a power of σ lies in J'.
acceptance: For the Tate curve E_q over K with v(q) > 0, the representation on V_ℓE_q has N ≠ 0 with image the line Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q, and ρ(I_K) is infinite.
For an abelian variety with potentially good reduction, or for any representation with finite image on inertia (e.g. a finite-order character), N = 0.
