nodes.title: Weil–Deligne representations of a local Weil group (arithmetic normalisation)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, W_K its Weil group with weilDegree : W_K → Z (kernel I_K, arithmetic Frobenius lifts of degree 1; ClassFieldTheory layer 9), and Ω a field of characteristic 0. A Weil–Deligne representation of W_K over Ω is a triple (V, r, N): V a finite-dimensional Ω-vector space, r : W_K → GL(V) a homomorphism whose restriction to I_K has open kernel (equivalently r is continuous for the discrete topology on GL(V)), and N ∈ End_Ω(V) nilpotent with r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N for all w ∈ W_K (Deligne (8.4.1.1)); equivalently r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N for a geometric lift F. Morphisms are Ω-linear maps f with f∘r(w) = r'(w)∘f and f∘N = N'∘f; they form an Ω-linear abelian category WD_Ω(K) with direct sums, tensor products (r⊗r', N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), internal Hom and duals (r^∨, −N^∨), determinant (det r, 0), coefficient extension Ω → Ω', restriction to W_L for L/K finite inside K̄ and induction from W_L: on Ind r = Ω[W_K] ⊗_{Ω[W_L]} V the monodromy is N_Ind(g ⊗ v) = q^{−weilDegree(g)}·(g ⊗ Nv) for g ∈ W_K (well defined because N r(h) = q^{−weilDegree(h)} r(h)N for h ∈ W_L; in the model of functions f : W_K → V with f(hw) = r(h)f(w) it is (N_Ind f)(w) = q^{weilDegree(w)}N(f(w))). Applying N on each coset summand without the power of q does not satisfy the relation unless the coset representatives lie in I_K. The unramified character ω : W_K → Ω^×, ω(w) = q^{weilDegree(w)} (ω(Φ) = q), corresponds to Deligne's ω_1 = ‖·‖ and to Q_ℓ(1); the special representation Sp(n) has basis e_0, …, e_{n−1}, r(w)e_i = ω(w)^i e_i and Ne_i = e_{i+1} (Ne_{n−1} = 0). The inertial type of (V, r, N) is r|_{I_K} up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: arithmetic normalisation (8.4.1.1); copying a geometric-Frobenius formula with q instead of q^{-1} gives the wrong objects
r is required to have open kernel on inertia; the ℓ-adic topology of Ω plays no role (Deligne 8.3–8.4: the description is independent of the topology of E_λ)
Ω has characteristic 0, needed for exp/log in the comparison with ℓ-adic representations
proofSteps: Category: kernels and cokernels of morphisms carry the restricted r and N, the relation is preserved; tensor products: r⊗r'(w)(N⊗1 + 1⊗N')r⊗r'(w)^{-1} = q^{deg w}(N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), and N⊗1 + 1⊗N' is nilpotent as a sum of commuting nilpotents.
Duals: with r^∨(w) the transpose of r(w)^{-1}, r^∨(w)X^∨r^∨(w)^{-1} = (r(w)Xr(w)^{-1})^∨ for X ∈ End V, so r^∨(w)(−N^∨)r^∨(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}(−N^∨).
Restriction to W_L: weilDegree_K = f(L/K)·weilDegree_L on W_L (ClassFieldTheory layer 9 weilDegree_weilTransfer) and q_L = q^{f(L/K)}, so the relation is preserved.
acceptance: Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N e_0 = e_1) satisfies the relation, and its kernel of N is the line on which arithmetic Frobenius acts by q, matching Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓ(E_q) for a Tate curve.
The pair (ω ⊕ 1, N e_0 = e_1), i.e. N lowering the ω-exponent, violates the relation: r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{-weilDegree(w)}N.

nodes.title: Rescaling the monodromy operator: (V, r, N) ≅ (V, r, aN) for a ≠ 0
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, Ω a field of characteristic 0 and (V, r, N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_K over Ω (weil-deligne-representation). For every a ∈ Ω^× there is A ∈ GL(V) that commutes with r(W_K) and satisfies A∘N = (aN)∘A; that is, A is an isomorphism of Weil–Deligne representations (V, r, N) → (V, r, aN). So the isomorphism class of (V, r, aN) does not depend on a ∈ Ω^×. For a = 0 and N ≠ 0 the two objects are not isomorphic.
hypotheses: a ≠ 0 (Deligne prints 'tout a ∈ E')

the proof uses that r(I_K) is finite (open kernel on the compact group I_K) and that q ≥ 2 is not a root of unity in Ω; without either the statement fails: if N commuted with r (the case 'q = 1') and r(F) = 1 + N on Ω², every A commuting with r(F) commutes with N
proofSteps: A central power of Frobenius: let F be a geometric Frobenius lift and I' = ker(r|_{I_K}), open in I_K and normal in W_K. Conjugation by F induces an automorphism of the finite group I_K/I'; if n is a multiple of its order then r(F)^n commutes with r(I_K), and it commutes with r(F), hence with r(W_K), which is generated by r(F) and r(I_K) (W_K/I_K ≅ Z, ClassFieldTheory layer 9).

Primary decomposition: factor the minimal polynomial of r(F)^n over Ω as ∏_α m_α, powers of distinct monic irreducible polynomials (α runs through the Galois-conjugacy classes of eigenvalues of r(F)^n in an algebraic closure), and put V^α = ker m_α(r(F)^n). By Mathlib's kernel decomposition (Polynomial.sup_ker_aeval_eq_ker_aeval_mul_of_coprime and Polynomial.disjoint_ker_aeval_of_isCoprime), V = ⊕_α V^α, and each V^α is r(W_K)-stable because r(F)^n is central.

N shifts the classes: r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N gives P(q^n·r(F)^n)∘N = N∘P(r(F)^n) for every polynomial P, so N maps ker m_α(r(F)^n) into ker m_α(q^nX)(r(F)^n) ⊂ V^{q^{-n}α} (zero if the class q^{-n}α does not occur).

The scalars: multiplication by q^{-n} has no periodic point on the set of Galois-conjugacy classes of nonzero algebraic elements (a class of degree d fixed by q^{-nj} would give q^{-njd} = 1 on taking norms, and q ≥ 2 in characteristic 0). So the finite set S of classes that occur is a disjoint union of chains α_0, q^{-n}α_0, …, q^{-nj}α_0, and λ : S → Ω^×, λ(q^{-ni}α_0) = a^i, satisfies λ(q^{-n}α) = a·λ(α) whenever α and q^{-n}α both lie in S.
A := ⊕_α λ(α)·id_{V^α} commutes with r(W_K) and, for v ∈ V^α, A(Nv) = λ(q^{-n}α)Nv = a·N(Av); A is invertible because a ≠ 0. For a = 0 an isomorphism would conjugate N to 0.
acceptance: Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, Ne_0 = e_1): n = 1, the classes are 1 (on e_0) and q^{-1} (on e_1) for a geometric Frobenius, λ(1) = 1, λ(q^{-1}) = a, A = diag(1, a), and A(Ne_0) = a·e_1 = (aN)(Ae_0).
Used with a = e(L/K) for restriction to W_L and with a ∈ Q_ℓ^× for the change of trivialisation of Q_ℓ(1) in grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor.

nodes.title: The Weil–Deligne representation of an ℓ-adic representation and its independence of choices
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ and (V, ρ) a continuous representation of W_K (or of G_K, restricted to W_K) on a finite-dimensional E-vector space, with monodromy N ∈ End(V)(−1) from grothendieck-quasi-unipotence. Choose a geometric Frobenius lift F ∈ W_K and an isomorphism T : Q_ℓ(1) → Q_ℓ (Deligne 8.4.2). Define WD_{F,T}(ρ) = (V, ρ', N') by ρ'(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)·exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) for n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K (every w ∈ W_K is uniquely F^nσ), and N' ∈ End(V) the image of N under T. Then (V, ρ', N') is a Weil–Deligne representation over E in the sense of weil-deligne-representation (ρ'|_{I_K} has open kernel and ρ'(w)N'ρ'(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N'), and its isomorphism class WD(ρ) depends only on ρ, not on F or T (Lemme 8.4.3): changing F to Fτ (τ ∈ I_K) conjugates ρ' by A = exp((q−1)^{-1}t_ℓ(τ)N), that is ρ'_{Fτ} = Aρ'_F A^{-1} (and changing F to τF conjugates by exp((1−q^{-1})^{-1}t_ℓ(τ)N), the coefficient printed by Deligne), and changing T to aT (a ∈ Q_ℓ^×) replaces N' by a^{-1}N' (T∘t_ℓ is multiplied by a and ρ(σ) = exp(T(t_ℓ(σ))·N') on J does not change; the source prints aN'), and (ρ', bN') is isomorphic to (ρ', N') for every b ∈ E^×. The construction is a functor from continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K to WD_E(K), it is exact, faithful, compatible with ⊗, duals, det, direct sums, twists (WD(ρ⊗χ) = WD(ρ)⊗WD(χ)), coefficient extension, restriction to W_L and induction from W_L, and with V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}; it induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K over E and isomorphism classes of Weil–Deligne representations over E (Deligne 8.3.7, in the form 8.4); a continuous representation of W_K extends continuously to G_K iff its image is bounded, i.e. iff the eigenvalues of ρ(Φ), Φ an arithmetic Frobenius lift, are ℓ-adic units (ρ(Φ)^Z is bounded exactly then, also when ρ(Φ) is not semisimple, because the powers of a unipotent matrix are ℓ-adically bounded).
hypotheses: λ must have residue characteristic different from that of K; this is the ℓ ≠ p hypothesis of the stage
the nilpotent N of Theorem 8.2 lies in End(V)(−1), i.e. it is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' of 8.4.2 depends on the choice of T, and changing T to aT replaces N' by a^{-1}N'
quasi-unipotence is only on a subgroup of finite index of inertia; ρ itself need not be unipotent on all of I
the construction 8.4.2 depends on choosing a GEOMETRIC Frobenius F and a trivialization T of Z_ℓ(1); Lemme 8.4.3 removes the dependence only up to isomorphism

Lemme 8.4.3 is proved in two steps: a change of F conjugates ρ' by an exponential of a multiple of N (the constants printed in the source are not right as they stand; the correct ones are in the statement), and a change of T to aT replaces N' by a^{-1}N' (printed as aN' in the source), which gives an isomorphic pair for every a ≠ 0 by the rescaling lemma (decompose V into the generalised eigenspaces V^α of a central power F^n, with N V^α ⊂ V^{q^{−n}α}; the source prints 'tout a ∈ E')
the bijection is for representations of W_K; Weil–Deligne representations whose Frobenius has non-unit eigenvalues come from representations of W_K that do not extend to G_K
proofSteps: Deligne states 8.2 as Grothendieck's theorem and refers to Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), his [13], for the proof; grothendieck-quasi-unipotence proves it for finite residue fields.

The exponent convention is fixed by the notation of 2.2.2–2.2.4: v' is reduction to Gal(k̄/k), whose Weil subgroup W(k̄/k) = Z is generated by the ARITHMETIC Frobenius φ, and F = φ^{-1} is the geometric Frobenius; so the displayed relation reads ρ(Φ)Nρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN for arithmetic Φ. This agrees with the stage text 'With arithmetic Frobenius the relation is r(F)Nr(F)^{-1}=qN'.

ρ' is a homomorphism because ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) and t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ) (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence, ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), so the correction factors exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) multiply compatibly; ρ' is trivial on the open J where ρ = exp(t_ℓN).

8.4.2 produces (ρ', N') from (V, ρ). Independence of F: (Fτ)^n = F^nσ_n with t_ℓ(σ_n) = ((q^n − 1)/(q − 1))t_ℓ(τ) (induction on n, using t_ℓ(F^{-1}σF) = q·t_ℓ(σ)), so ρ'_{Fτ}(w) = ρ'_F(w)exp(((q^n − 1)/(q − 1))t_ℓ(τ)N) for w ∈ F^{n}I_K, and this equals Aρ'_F(w)A^{-1} for A = exp((q − 1)^{-1}t_ℓ(τ)N) because ρ'_F(w)^{-1}Nρ'_F(w) = q^nN. Independence of T: rescaling-the-monodromy-operator. The bijection 8.3.7: ell-adic-representation-of-a-weil-deligne-representation constructs the inverse and shows that the two constructions have the same morphisms.

Compatibilities: N is unique, so the N of ρ⊗ρ' is N⊗1 + 1⊗N' and the N of ρ^∨ is −N^∨; restriction to W_L uses t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L} (ell-adic-tame-character (v)); induction: the monodromy of Ind ρ is the induced N because N is unique and Ind ρ restricted to an open subgroup of I_K is a sum of conjugates of ρ.
Invariants: σ ∈ I_K fixes v under ρ iff ρ'(σ)exp(t_ℓ(σ)N)v = v for all σ; taking σ ∈ J gives Nv = 0, and then ρ'(σ)v = v (Deligne 8.12, FSY §5.3.1).
acceptance: Check the conjugation relation against a chosen normalization by computing it for a Tate curve, where N is nonzero and the Frobenius eigenvalues differ by q: WD(V_ℓE_q) ≅ Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N ≠ 0), arithmetic Frobenius acting by q on ker N.

Check that the Frobenius semisimplification, the semisimplification and the full object are three different things by exhibiting a representation where they differ: V_ℓE_q ⊕ U with U unramified and Frobenius a nontrivial unipotent Jordan block (frobenius-semisimplification).
WD(Q_ℓ(1)) = (ω, 0) for ℓ ≠ p.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic representation of the Weil group attached to a Weil–Deligne representation
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ, F ∈ W_K a geometric Frobenius lift, T : Q_ℓ(1) → Q_ℓ an isomorphism and t := T∘t_ℓ : I_K → Q_ℓ. Let (V, r, N') be a Weil–Deligne representation of W_K over E. Then ρ(F^nσ) := r(F^nσ)·exp(t(σ)N') (n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K) is a homomorphism W_K → GL(V), continuous for the Weil topology and the ℓ-adic topology of GL(V); its monodromy operator in the sense of grothendieck-quasi-unipotence is the N with T(N) = N'; and ρ(F^nσ)·exp(−t(σ)N') = r(F^nσ). It is the only continuous representation of W_K on V with these two properties. A linear map V → V_1 commutes with ρ and ρ_1 if and only if it commutes with r, r_1 and with N', N'_1.
hypotheses: ℓ different from the residue characteristic
the representation obtained need not extend to G_K: it does if and only if the eigenvalues of r(F) are ℓ-adic units
F and T are fixed; the construction depends on them
proofSteps: Homomorphism: for w = F^nσ and w' = F^mτ, ww' = F^{n+m}(F^{-m}σF^m)τ and t(F^{-m}σF^m) = q^m·t(σ) (ell-adic-tame-character (iii), F geometric), so ρ(ww') = r(w)r(w')·exp(q^mt(σ)N')·exp(t(τ)N'). On the other hand ρ(w)ρ(w') = r(w)·exp(t(σ)N')·r(w')·exp(t(τ)N'), and exp(t(σ)N')·r(w') = r(w')·exp(q^mt(σ)N') because r(w')^{-1}N'r(w') = q^mN' (the relation of weil-deligne-representation for w' of degree −m, with nilpotent-exponential-and-unipotent-logarithm (iii)). Exponentials of multiples of N' multiply by IsNilpotent.exp_add_of_commute.

Continuity: on J = ker(r|_{I_K}), an open subgroup of W_K for the Weil topology, ρ(σ) = exp(t(σ)N') is a polynomial in the continuous function t; a homomorphism that is continuous on an open subgroup is continuous.

Monodromy: ρ(σ) = exp(t(σ)N') = exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) on J with N = T^{-1}(N'), so N is the monodromy operator of ρ by the uniqueness statement of grothendieck-quasi-unipotence; the identity ρ(F^nσ)exp(−t(σ)N') = r(F^nσ) is the definition.
Uniqueness: a representation ρ_1 with monodromy N and ρ_1(F^nσ)exp(−t(σ)N') = r(F^nσ) equals ρ on every F^nσ.

Morphisms: if f commutes with ρ and ρ_1 then exp(t(σ)N'_1)∘f = f∘exp(t(σ)N') for all σ in the open subgroup J ∩ J_1; both sides are polynomials in t(σ), which takes infinitely many values there, so the coefficients agree, and the linear one gives N'_1∘f = f∘N'; then f commutes with r(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)exp(−t(σ)N'). The converse is immediate from the formula.
acceptance: (ω, 0) gives the character w ↦ q^{weilDegree(w)}, the restriction of χ_ℓ to W_K (Q_ℓ(1)).
Sp(2) gives a representation with ρ(σ) = exp(t(σ)N) on all of I_K, the one of V_ℓ of a Tate curve with v(q_E) = 1 for a suitable T (weil-deligne-required-examples).
(λ_W(ℓ), 0) gives a continuous character of W_K with ρ(F) = ℓ^{-1}, which does not extend to G_K.

nodes.title: Frobenius semisimplification, semisimplification, and the three objects attached to a Weil–Deligne representation
nodes.statement: Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over a field Ω of characteristic 0 and F ∈ W_K a geometric Frobenius lift. Let r(F) = s·u be the multiplicative Jordan–Chevalley decomposition (s semisimple, u unipotent, commuting; Tau Ceti LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.jordanDecomposition, Ω perfect). Then u commutes with r(W_K) and with N (Deligne 8.5: u is a polynomial in r(F), a power r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) because F^m acts trivially on I_K modulo the open kernel of r, and N is an eigenvector of conjugation by r(F)); the Frobenius semisimplification is (V, r^{F-ss}, N) with r^{F-ss}(F^nσ) := r(F^nσ)u^{-n} (n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K) (Deligne (8.5.1)). It is a Weil–Deligne representation, independent of the choice of F, with r^{F-ss}(F) = s. (V, r, N) is Frobenius-semisimple if r = r^{F-ss}, equivalently if r(w) is semisimple for one (equivalently every) w ∈ W_K ∖ I_K. Three objects are distinguished: (1) the full (V, r, N); (2) its Frobenius semisimplification (V, r^{F-ss}, N), which keeps N; (3) its semisimplification in the abelian category WD_Ω(K), which is (V^{ss}, r^{ss}, 0): the simple objects have N = 0 because ker N is a sub-object, and r^{ss} is the semisimplification of r as a representation of W_K. On the Galois side, for an ℓ-adic ρ, WD(ρ^{ss}) is (3) for WD(ρ), whereas WD(ρ)^{F-ss} is (2). Every Frobenius-semisimple indecomposable Weil–Deligne representation over an algebraically closed Ω is r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) for an irreducible representation r_0 of W_K and n ≥ 1, and the decomposition of a Frobenius-semisimple object into such is unique up to order.
hypotheses: Ω of characteristic 0 (perfect, so the Jordan decomposition exists over Ω)
Frobenius semisimplification semisimplifies only Frobenius; it does not kill N and is not the semisimplification of the Weil–Deligne representation
the classification of indecomposables needs Ω algebraically closed
the classification of Frobenius-semisimple indecomposable objects (last sentence of the statement) is not established here: none of the cited sources states it, and it is recorded as a gap
proofSteps: Deligne 8.5, with Tau Ceti's multiplicative Jordan–Chevalley decomposition r(F) = s·u (jordanDecomposition_spec: s semisimple, u unipotent, commuting). (i) u commutes with everything that commutes with r(F) (commute_coe_unipotentPart_left_of_commute). (ii) For m with F^m acting trivially by conjugation on the finite group I_K/I' (I' the open kernel of r on I_K), r(F)^m is central in r(W_K); u^m is the unipotent part of r(F)^m (unipotentPart_mul_of_commute, by induction), so u^m commutes with r(W_K) by (i) applied to r(F)^m, and u = exp(m^{-1}·log(u^m)) is a polynomial in u^m (nilpotent-exponential-and-unipotent-logarithm, characteristic 0), hence u centralises r(W_K). (iii) N ∘ r(F) = (q·r(F)) ∘ N by the relation for a geometric F, so comp_unipotentPart_eq_of_comp_eq gives N ∘ u = unipotentPart(q·r(F)) ∘ N; the unipotent part of a nonzero scalar multiple of g is that of g (the scalar goes into the semisimple factor, by eq_jordanDecomposition_iff), so N ∘ u = u ∘ N.

r^{F-ss} is a homomorphism with the same restriction to I_K and the relation for N holds because u commutes with r(W_K) and with N. Independence of F: for σ ∈ I_K, r(Fσ)^m = r(F)^m·r(σ') with σ' ∈ I_K, and r(σ') has finite order k and commutes with the central r(F)^m, so r(Fσ)^{mk} = r(F)^{mk}; hence the unipotent parts of r(Fσ) and r(F) have the same mk-th power and are equal (unipotent m-th roots are unique in characteristic 0, by the logarithm), and u^n is the unipotent part of r(F^nσ) for every n and σ (Deligne 8.5: 'ρ'(w_1) et ρ'(w_2) ont une puissance commune').
Semisimplification: ker N is r-stable by the relation, so simple objects have N = 0; Jordan–Hölder in the finite-length category WD_Ω(K).

Classification: on an F-semisimple object, the monodromy filtration of N (the unique increasing filtration with N M_k ⊂ M_{k−2} and N^k : gr_k ≅ gr_{−k}) is r-stable with r(F) acting on the primitive parts; Deligne Proposition 8.9 uses the graded pieces; the decomposition r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) follows from the Jacobson–Morozov form of N (Ω characteristic 0).
acceptance: For V = Sp(2) ⊕ U, U two-dimensional unramified with r(F) a nontrivial unipotent Jordan block and N = 0 on U: the full object, its Frobenius semisimplification Sp(2) ⊕ 1² and its semisimplification (1 ⊕ ω ⊕ 1², 0) are pairwise non-isomorphic.
For WD(V_ℓA) of an abelian variety, the representation is already Frobenius-semisimple (Deligne Exemple 8.10).

nodes.title: The local Euler factor of a Weil–Deligne or ℓ-adic representation (geometric Frobenius)
nodes.statement: For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over Ω and an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ ∈ W_K (so that Φ^{-1} is a geometric lift), L(V, X) := det(1 − X·r(Φ^{-1}) | (ker N)^{r(I_K)}) ∈ Ω[X], a polynomial with constant term 1 and degree dim (ker N)^{I_K}, independent of Φ (inertia acts trivially on the invariants); for Ω = C, L(V, s) = L(V, q^{-s})^{-1}. In Deligne's notation (3.5.1) Z(V; t) = det(1 − Ft^d, V^I)^{-1} with F the geometric Frobenius and d = [k : F_p], so Z(V; t) = L(V, t^d)^{-1} and X = t^d = q^{-s}. For a continuous ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K or W_K (ℓ ≠ p), L(ρ, X) := det(1 − Xρ(Φ^{-1}) | V^{ρ(I_K)}) = L(WD(ρ), X) (Deligne 8.12). For F a number field, a finite place v and ρ a continuous representation of G_F over a field of characteristic 0 with v ∤ ℓ, L_v(ρ, X) := L(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}, X), independent of ι; if ρ is unramified at v, L_v(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Frob_v)^{-1}) = X^{dim V}·P_v(ρ^∨, X^{-1}). For a Tate module V_ℓA with H^1 = V_ℓA^∨: (V_ℓA^∨)^{I_v} is the dual of the coinvariants (V_ℓA)_{I_v}, so L_v(V_ℓA^∨, X) = det(1 − X·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with arithmetic Frob_v; this equals det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓA^{I_v}) when I_v acts through a finite quotient, but not in general (Tate curve: 1 − X from coinvariants, 1 − qX from invariants).
hypotheses: GEOMETRIC Frobenius in the Euler factor, arithmetic Frobenius in P_v; the two are related by duality
(ker N)^{I} on the Weil–Deligne side, V^{ρ(I)} on the Galois side; these agree by the Weil–Deligne functor
taking inertia invariants does not commute with reduction modulo ℓ, so L_v of a residual representation is not the reduction of L_v of a lift
proofSteps: Independence of Φ: two arithmetic (equivalently two geometric) lifts differ by an element of I_K, which acts trivially on (ker N)^{I_K}; (ker N)^{I_K} is r(W_K)-stable because I_K is normal and r(w) preserves ker N by the relation.
L(ρ) = L(WD(ρ)): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor gives V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}, and ρ' = ρ on it.
Unramified case: ρ(Frob^{-1}) acts on V and det(1 − Xρ(Frob)^{-1}) = X^n det(X^{-1} − ρ^∨(Frob)) by transposition (frobenius-characteristic-polynomial).
acceptance: L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X; for a Tate curve E_q over K, L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X and L(V_ℓE_q^∨, X) = 1 − X, the split multiplicative Euler factor.
For a ramified character χ (χ|_{I_K} ≠ 1), L(χ, X) = 1.

nodes.title: Local factors and Weil–Deligne representations of induced representations
nodes.statement: (a) Local: let L/K be a finite separable extension of nonarchimedean local fields with residue degree f, and (V, r, N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_L over Ω. Then L(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K}(V, r, N), X) = L((V, r, N), X^f), and for an ℓ-adic representation ρ of W_L (or G_L), WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ), so L(Ind ρ, X) = L(ρ, X^f). (b) Global: let L/F be a finite extension of number fields, ρ a continuous representation of G_L over a field of characteristic 0 and v a finite place of F with v ∤ ℓ. Then L_v(Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} L_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}). If ρ is unramified at every w | v and L/F is unramified at v, Ind ρ is unramified at v and P_v(Ind ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} P_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}).
hypotheses: L/F finite (open subgroup G_L), places w of L above v with residue degrees f(w|v)
for the P_v formula: L/F unramified at v and ρ unramified at all w | v; otherwise only the L-factor statement holds

Deligne states Proposition 3.8 for complex representations of the Weil group (no monodromy); part (a) is the same statement for Weil–Deligne representations over any field Ω of characteristic 0: the proof is algebraic, and for N ≠ 0 it is applied to the W_L-representation ker N, because ker of the induced monodromy is the induced representation of ker N
proofSteps: (a) Deligne Proposition 3.8(ii) with Lemme 3.9: inertia-invariants-of-an-induced-representation identifies (ker N_Ind)^{I_K} with ((ker N)^{I_L})^f, the geometric Frobenius of K acting as the cyclic block endomorphism built on the geometric Frobenius of L, and determinant-of-a-cyclic-block-endomorphism gives det(1 − X·F_K) = det(1 − X^f·F_L).
WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (compatibility with induction).
(b) local-restriction gives (Ind ρ)_ι ≅ ⊕_{w|v} Ind_{G_{L_w}}^{G_{F_v}} ρ_{ι_w} (Mackey); apply (a) to each summand with f = f(w|v) and multiplicativity of L on direct sums.
P_v formula: at unramified v, L_v = reverse of P_v of the dual; apply the L-formula to ρ^∨ (Ind commutes with duals) and reverse, using that reversal is multiplicative and X ↦ X^f commutes with it.
acceptance: For L = Q(i), F = Q, ρ = 1: P_p(Ind 1, X) = (X − 1)² for p ≡ 1 mod 4 and X² − 1 = (X − 1)(X + 1) for p ≡ 3 mod 4.
For K'/K unramified of degree f and ρ = 1, L(Ind 1, X) = 1 − X^f.

nodes.title: The determinant of a cyclic block endomorphism (Deligne, Lemme 3.9)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, V a finite free A-module, φ ∈ End_A(V) and n ≥ 1. Let φ_n be the endomorphism of V^n = V ⊗ A^n (basis e_0, …, e_{n−1} of A^n) with φ_n(v ⊗ e_i) = v ⊗ e_{i+1} for 0 ≤ i < n − 1 and φ_n(v ⊗ e_{n−1}) = φ(v) ⊗ e_0. Then det(1 − X·φ_n) = det(1 − X^n·φ) in A[X]; equivalently the characteristic polynomial of φ_n is charpoly(φ)(X^n).
hypotheses: Deligne states the lemma for vector spaces over a field and proves it by reduction to φ diagonal ('principe de prolongement des identités algébriques'); the identity holds over every commutative ring, with the direct proof below
n ≥ 1; for n = 1, φ_1 = φ
proofSteps: Write 1 − Xφ_n = (1 − XS) − X·(i_0 ∘ φ ∘ p_{n−1}), where S(v ⊗ e_i) = v ⊗ e_{i+1} for i < n − 1 and S(v ⊗ e_{n−1}) = 0, i_0 : V → V^n is the inclusion of the summand of e_0 and p_{n−1} : V^n → V the projection to the summand of e_{n−1}. S is nilpotent, 1 − XS is unitriangular in a basis adapted to the summands, det(1 − XS) = 1 and (1 − XS)^{-1} = Σ_{k < n} X^kS^k.

Hence det(1 − Xφ_n) = det(1 − (1 − XS)^{-1}·X·i_0 ∘ (φ ∘ p_{n−1})) = det(1 − X·φ ∘ p_{n−1} ∘ (1 − XS)^{-1} ∘ i_0) by Mathlib's Matrix.det_one_sub_mul_comm (Weinstein–Aronszajn; in bases of V and V^n, with LinearMap.det), and p_{n−1} ∘ (1 − XS)^{-1} ∘ i_0 = X^{n−1}·id_V, because only the term X^{n−1}S^{n−1} carries the summand of e_0 to that of e_{n−1}. So det(1 − Xφ_n) = det(1 − X^nφ).
Characteristic polynomial: det(X − φ_n) = X^{n·rank V}·det(1 − X^{-1}φ_n) = X^{n·rank V}det(1 − X^{-n}φ) = det(X^n − φ) (an identity of polynomials, checked after inverting X).
acceptance: n = 2, V = A, φ = a: φ_2 has matrix [[0, a], [1, 0]] and det(1 − Xφ_2) = 1 − aX².
V = A, φ = 1: φ_n is the cyclic permutation matrix and det(1 − Xφ_n) = 1 − X^n, the Euler factor of the representation induced from the trivial character of the unramified extension of degree n.

nodes.title: Inertia invariants of a representation induced from the Weil group of a finite extension
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a finite separable extension of nonarchimedean local fields inside K̄ with residue degree f, Ω a field and V a representation of W_L on a finite-dimensional Ω-vector space. Realise Ind V = Ind_{W_L}^{W_K} V as the space of functions φ : W_K → V with φ(hw) = h·φ(w) for h ∈ W_L, on which W_K acts by right translation. Then (Ind V)^{I_K} consists of the φ that are invariant under right translation by I_K; such φ take values in V^{I_L} and factor through W_K/I_K ≅ Z. For geometric Frobenius lifts F_K of K and F_L of L, the map φ ↦ (φ(F_K^{f−1}), …, φ(F_K), φ(1)) is an isomorphism (Ind V)^{I_K} → (V^{I_L})^f which carries the action of F_K to the cyclic block endomorphism φ_f of determinant-of-a-cyclic-block-endomorphism built on the action of F_L on V^{I_L}. Consequently det(1 − X·F_K | (Ind V)^{I_K}) = det(1 − X^f·F_L | V^{I_L}). For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) of W_L, the kernel of the induced monodromy is Ind(ker N), so the same identity holds with V^{I_L} replaced by (ker N)^{I_L} and (Ind V)^{I_K} by (ker N_Ind)^{I_K}.
hypotheses: no hypothesis on the characteristic of Ω or on the kernel of the representation is needed for the description of the invariants
Deligne's Proposition 3.8 is the case Ω = C, N = 0
proofSteps: I_K is normal in W_K, so the I_K-invariants of Ind V are the functions invariant under right translation by I_K. For h ∈ I_L = W_L ∩ I_K and such φ, h·φ(w) = φ(hw) = φ(w·(w^{-1}hw)) = φ(w), so φ has values in V^{I_L}; and φ factors through W_K/I_K, which is infinite cyclic generated by the class of F_K (ClassFieldTheory layer 9).

The image of W_L in W_K/I_K is generated by the class of F_K^f, and F_L ≡ F_K^f modulo I_K (weilDegree_K = f·weilDegree_L on W_L, ClassFieldTheory layer 9). The covariance condition becomes φ(F_K^{f+j}) = F_L·φ(F_K^j), so φ is determined by the values c_j = φ(F_K^j) ∈ V^{I_L}, 0 ≤ j < f, which are arbitrary.

Action: (F_K·φ)(F_K^j) = φ(F_K^{j+1}), so F_K sends (c_0, …, c_{f−1}) to (c_1, …, c_{f−1}, F_Lc_0); in the reversed coordinates d_i = c_{f−1−i} this is d ↦ (F_Ld_{f−1}, d_0, …, d_{f−2}), the endomorphism φ_f for φ = F_L. The determinant identity is determinant-of-a-cyclic-block-endomorphism.

Monodromy: the induced monodromy acts on each coset summand by a nonzero multiple of N (weil-deligne-representation, induction), so its kernel is the induced representation of ker N, to which the first three steps apply.
acceptance: L/K unramified of degree f and V the trivial character: (Ind 1)^{I_K} = Ind 1 has dimension f and det(1 − X·F_K) = 1 − X^f.
L/K totally ramified (f = 1): (Ind V)^{I_K} ≅ V^{I_L} with F_K acting as F_L, although Ind V has dimension [L : K]·dim V.

nodes.title: The monodromy filtration of a nilpotent endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, V a finite-dimensional k-vector space and N a nilpotent endomorphism of V. The monodromy filtration of N is the unique family of subspaces (M_a)_{a ∈ Z} of V with: M_a ⊂ M_{a+1}; M_a = 0 for a ≪ 0 and M_a = V for a ≫ 0; N·M_a ⊂ M_{a−2}; and, for every a ≥ 0, N^a induces an isomorphism gr^M_a V → gr^M_{−a} V, where gr^M_a = M_a/M_{a−1}. It exists, it is unique, and M_a = Σ_{i − j = a; i, j ≥ 0} (ker N^{i+1} ∩ im N^j). Properties. (1) If N^{d+1} = 0 then M_d = V and M_{−d−1} = 0. (2) g·M_a = M_a for every g ∈ GL(V) with gNg^{-1} ∈ k^×·N, and N and cN (c ∈ k^×) have the same monodromy filtration. (3) A linear map f : V → V' with f∘N = N'∘f maps M_a(N) into M_a(N'); the filtration of N ⊕ N' is the direct sum. (4) Primitive decomposition: for a ≥ 0 let P_a = ker(N^{a+1} : gr^M_a → gr^M_{−a−2}); then gr^M_b = ⊕_{j ≥ max(0, −b)} N^j·P_{b+2j} for every b, dim P_a is the number of Jordan blocks of N of size a + 1, and Σ_a a²·dim gr^M_a = 2·Σ_{k ≥ 1} k·rank(N^k). (5) Dual: M_a(N^∨) is the annihilator of M_{−a−1}(N) in the dual of V. (6) Tensor product, for k of characteristic 0: M_a(N ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ N') = Σ_{b + c = a} M_b(N) ⊗ M_c(N'). For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) the filtration is r(W_K)-stable by (2), so W_K acts on the graded pieces.
hypotheses: k is any field for existence, uniqueness and (1)–(5)

(6) needs characteristic 0: over F_2, for N = N' a Jordan block of size 2, N ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ N' has square 0 and Jordan type (2, 2), with graded pieces of dimension 2 in degrees ±1, whereas the convolution has dimensions 1, 2, 1 in degrees 2, 0, −2
indexing as in FSY §5.3.2 and Deligne, Weil II 1.6: N lowers the index by 2
proofSteps: Uniqueness and existence by induction on the nilpotency order: if N^{d+1} = 0, the conditions force M_d = V and M_{−d−1} = 0, then M_{d−1} = ker N^d and M_{−d} = im N^d (N^d kills M_{d−1} and induces an isomorphism V/M_{d−1} → M_{−d}); N induces a nilpotent endomorphism of ker N^d/im N^d with d-th power 0, whose monodromy filtration, pulled back to ker N^d, is forced to be (M_a) for −d ≤ a ≤ d − 1; conversely these subspaces satisfy the conditions.

Formula: for a single Jordan block with basis v, Nv, …, N^dv give N^jv the weight d − 2j; the span of the vectors of weight ≤ a satisfies the conditions, and equals Σ_{i − j = a}(ker N^{i+1} ∩ im N^j), since ker N^{i+1} is spanned by the last i + 1 basis vectors and im N^j by those of index ≥ j. The conditions and the formula are compatible with direct sums, and V is a direct sum of Jordan blocks for N (structure of a finitely generated torsion module over k[X]; any field).

(1) is in the first step. (2): g·M_•(N) satisfies the conditions for gNg^{-1}, and the conditions for cN are those for N; conclude by uniqueness. (3): from the formula, because f maps ker N^{i+1} ∩ im N^j into ker N'^{i+1} ∩ im N'^j.

(4) and (5) for one Jordan block by inspection (the primitive part is the class of v in degree d; the dual basis vector of a vector of weight x has weight −x for N^∨), then by direct sums. The rank identity: a block of size s contributes Σ_{j=0}^{s−1}(s − 1 − 2j)² = (s³ − s)/3 to the left side and 2·Σ_{k=1}^{s−1}k(s − k) = (s³ − s)/3 to the right side.

(6): in characteristic 0 a Jordan block of size s is the irreducible representation of sl_2 of dimension s with N the lowering operator and the weight the eigenvalue of H; for every finite-dimensional representation of sl_2 (completely reducible in characteristic 0) the filtration by the sums of H-eigenspaces of eigenvalue ≤ a satisfies the defining conditions for the lowering operator. On V ⊗ V' the operators N ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ N' and H ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ H' belong to the tensor product representation, and the eigenspaces of H ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ H' are the sums of tensor products of eigenspaces; uniqueness gives the convolution formula (Deligne, Weil II 1.6.9).
acceptance: For a single Jordan block of size n (the space of Sp(n)), gr^M_a is one-dimensional for a ∈ {n − 1, n − 3, …, 1 − n} and zero otherwise.
For N of Jordan type (2, 1): M_{−2} = 0, M_{−1} = im N, M_0 = ker N, M_1 = V; the rank identity reads 1 + 0 + 1 = 2·1.

nodes.title: The monodromy filtration and purity of Weil–Deligne representations
nodes.statement: Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over Ω, F a geometric Frobenius lift and w ∈ Z. Let M_• be the monodromy filtration of N (monodromy-filtration); it is stable under r(W_K), so W_K acts on each gr^M_a V. An element α of an algebraic closure of Ω is a q-Weil number of weight m if α is algebraic over Q and |τ(α)| = q^{m/2} for every field embedding τ : Q(α) → C. (V, r, N) is pure of weight w if, for every a, every eigenvalue of r(F) on gr^M_a V is a q-Weil number of weight w + a (FSY §5.3.2, geometric Frobenius). An ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K (ℓ ≠ p) is pure of weight w if WD(ρ) is; mixed if V has a filtration by subspaces stable under r(W_K) and under N (sub-objects in WD_Ω(K)) whose graded pieces, with the induced r and N, are pure.
hypotheses: geometric Frobenius: weights are measured with F, so Q_ℓ(1) = (ω, 0) is pure of weight −2
purity depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification
proofSteps: The monodromy filtration and its r(W_K)-stability are monodromy-filtration (existence, uniqueness, and property (2) applied to g = r(w), for which r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} is a nonzero multiple of N). The behaviour of purity under tensor products and duals (api isPure_tensor) is properties (5) and (6) of that node.

The Weil-number condition does not depend on the choice of F: for σ ∈ I_K the endomorphisms r(Fσ) and r(F) have a common power (r(Fσ)^{mk} = r(F)^{mk} when r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) and r(I_K) has exponent dividing k; this is the computation in frobenius-semisimplification, independence of F), and both preserve every M_a. So their eigenvalues on gr^M_a differ by roots of unity, which changes neither algebraicity nor the complex absolute values of the conjugates.
acceptance: Sp(2) is pure of weight −1: a geometric Frobenius acts by q^{-1} (weight −2 = −1 + (−1)) on gr^M_{−1} = ker N and by 1 (weight 0 = −1 + 1) on gr^M_1 = V/ker N; hence V_ℓ(E_q) is pure of weight −1 and V_ℓ(E_q)^∨ of weight 1.
1 ⊕ ω with N = 0 is not pure (weights 0 and −2 on gr_0).

nodes.title: A nilpotent operator with pure graded has the Jordan type of its graded (the count behind FSY Lemma 5.40)
nodes.statement: Let Ω be a field of characteristic 0, q ≥ 2 an integer, V a finite-dimensional Ω-vector space, N a nilpotent endomorphism of V and φ ∈ GL(V) with N∘φ = q·φ∘N. Let 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_c = V be subspaces stable under N and φ, V̄ = ⊕_i V_i/V_{i−1}, and N̄, φ̄ the induced endomorphisms. Suppose (V̄, φ̄, N̄) is pure of weight w: for every a, the eigenvalues of φ̄ on gr_a of the monodromy filtration of N̄ are q-Weil numbers of weight w + a (purity-of-weil-deligne-representations). Then: (i) rank N^k = rank N̄^k for all k ≥ 0, so N and N̄ have the same Jordan type and dim gr^{M(N)}_a V = dim gr^{M(N̄)}_a V̄ for all a; (ii) (V, φ, N) is pure of weight w; (iii) the filtration induced on ker N has graded ker N̄: (ker N ∩ V_i + V_{i−1})/V_{i−1} = ker(N̄ | V_i/V_{i−1}) for every i.
hypotheses: characteristic 0 and q ≥ 2 (weights are defined through complex absolute values)
purity of the graded cannot be dropped: for the Tate curve, V_1 = Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q has N̄ = 0 and N ≠ 0
FSY assert (i) and (ii) in one sentence of the proof of Lemma 5.40 (source issue E253); the argument is the one below
proofSteps: rank N̄^k ≤ rank N^k: the image of N̄^k is ⊕_i (N^kV_i + V_{i−1})/V_{i−1}, and Σ_i dim (N^kV_i + V_{i−1})/V_{i−1} ≤ Σ_i dim (N^kV ∩ V_i + V_{i−1})/V_{i−1} = dim N^kV.

φ preserves the flag, so φ and φ̄ have the same characteristic polynomial and every eigenvalue of φ is a q-Weil number. Let S = Σ (x − w)², the sum over the eigenvalues of φ with multiplicity, x the weight. By purity of the graded and monodromy-filtration (4), S = Σ_a a²·dim gr^{M(N̄)}_a = 2·Σ_{k ≥ 1} k·rank N̄^k.

Strings: the monodromy filtration of N is φ-stable (monodromy-filtration (2), since φ^{-1}Nφ = qN) and φ acts on the primitive parts P_a; as N^jφ = q^jφN^j, the eigenvalues of φ on N^jP_a are q^{-j} times those on P_a. By the primitive decomposition the eigenvalues of φ on V are the union, over a ≥ 0 and the eigenvalues α of φ on P_a, of the strings α, q^{-1}α, …, q^{-a}α, of weights x, x − 2, …, x − 2a. Writing x − a = w + c, the string contributes Σ_{j=0}^{a}(c + a − 2j)² = (a + 1)c² + Σ_{j=0}^{a}(a − 2j)² to S, so S = Σ_{strings}(a + 1)c² + Σ_a a²·dim gr^{M(N)}_a = Σ_{strings}(a + 1)c² + 2·Σ_{k ≥ 1} k·rank N^k.
Comparison: 2Σ k·rank N̄^k = S ≥ 2Σ k·rank N^k ≥ 2Σ k·rank N̄^k. Equality holds throughout: every c is 0, which is the purity of (V, φ, N) in weight w, and rank N^k = rank N̄^k for all k ≥ 1.
(iii): (ker N ∩ V_i + V_{i−1})/V_{i−1} ⊂ ker(N̄ | V_i/V_{i−1}) for each i, and the two sides have total dimension dim ker N = dim V − rank N = dim V̄ − rank N̄ = dim ker N̄.
acceptance: Frobenius weights {w + 1, w − 1, w + 1, w − 1} with N̄ of Jordan type (2, 2): N has type (2, 2); the types (4) and (3, 1) are excluded by the strings, (2, 1, 1) and (1, 1, 1, 1) by rank N ≥ rank N̄.
If N̄ = 0 and the graded is pure of weight w, then all Frobenius eigenvalues have weight w and N = 0 is forced (rank N = rank N̄ = 0); indeed N ≠ 0 would give a string with two different weights.

nodes.title: A representation with pure graded Weil–Deligne representation is pure, with the same L- and ε-factors (FSY Lemma 5.40)
nodes.statement: Let p ≠ ℓ be primes, K/Q_p finite (FSY: K = Q_p) and r : G_K → GL(V) a continuous ℓ-adic representation with a filtration 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_c = V by G_K-stable subspaces such that the Weil–Deligne representation of r̄ on V̄ = ⊕_i V_i/V_{i−1} is pure of weight w. Then WD(r) is pure of weight w, and r and r̄ have the same local L-factor and the same ε-factor: L(r, X) = L(r̄, X) and ε(WD(r), ψ, dx) = ε(WD(r̄), ψ, dx) (local-epsilon-factor).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p
the filtration is by G_K-stable subspaces; V̄ is the associated graded, not the semisimplification (though the conclusion passes to it)
the ε-statement is for complex coefficients after an embedding ι : Q̄_ℓ → C
proofSteps: FSY's proof (from a referee's sketch): the ε-factor of the Weil representation ρ in (5.33) depends only on the semisimplification of r by multiplicativity (local-epsilon-factor (1)).
With φ = ρ(F_p), the relation Nφ = pφN shows an eigenvalue α of φ on gr^M_a gives αp^{-b} on gr^M_{a−2b} with at least the same multiplicity, 0 ≤ b ≤ a.

By uniqueness of the monodromy operator (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence), N restricts to the monodromy of each V_i and induces the monodromy N̄ of V̄; det(1 − φT) = det(1 − φ̄T), and purity of (ρ̄, N̄) forces the monodromy filtrations of N and N̄ to have the same graded dimensions, so (ρ, N) is pure. This is purity-from-a-pure-graded, applied to φ = ρ(F) for a geometric Frobenius lift F (so N∘φ = q·φ∘N) and the flag (V_i); it also gives that the filtration induced on ker N has graded ker N̄.

ρ|_{ker N} and ρ̄|_{ker N̄} have the same semisimplification; taking I_p-invariants is exact on Weil representations (I_p acts through finite quotients), giving equal det(1 − φT | ker(N)^{I}) and equal det(φT | V^{I}/ker(N)^{I}); hence equal L- and ε-factors by local-euler-factor and local-epsilon-factor.
acceptance: For the Tate curve, the filtration Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q has associated graded (1 ⊕ ω, 0), which is not pure, so the lemma does not apply; and indeed L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X differs from L(1 ⊕ ω, X) = (1 − X)(1 − q^{-1}X): the purity hypothesis cannot be dropped.
FSY apply the lemma for even k to replace {r_{k,ℓ}} by its semisimplification in the functional equation.

sources.match: Conclusion of Lemma 5.40; the hypothesis is that the Weil–Deligne representation of the graded representation of a stable filtration is pure.

nodes.title: Deligne–Langlands local constants ε(V, ψ, dx) of Weil and Weil–Deligne representations
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, ψ : K → C^× a nontrivial continuous additive character, dx a Haar measure on K, and W_K the Weil group, with local class field theory normalised as in Deligne 2.3 (Art_K : K^× ≅ W_K^{ab} sending uniformisers to GEOMETRIC Frobenius lifts; in terms of Tau Ceti's arithmetic artinMap, Art_K(x) = artinMap(x)^{-1} = artinMap(x^{-1}), not the inverse isomorphism). (Deligne Théorème 4.1) There is a unique function ε assigning to each isomorphism class of (K, K̄, ψ, dx, V, ρ), V a finite-dimensional complex representation of W_K with open kernel on I_K, a number ε(V, ψ, dx) ∈ C^×, such that: (1) ε is multiplicative in short exact sequences (hence defined on virtual representations); (2) ε(V, ψ, a·dx) = a^{dim V}ε(V, ψ, dx), so ε(V, ψ) is defined for virtual V of dimension 0; (3) for L/K finite inside K̄ and a virtual representation V_L of W_L of dimension 0, ε(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K} V_L, ψ) = ε(V_L, ψ ∘ Tr_{L/K}); (4) for dim V = 1, given by the quasi-character χ of K^× through Art_K, ε(V, ψ, dx) is Tate's local constant ε(χ, ψ, dx) (for χ = ωω_s with ω a character of K^×, and the Haar measure dx_ψ self-dual for ψ, this is ε(s, ω, ψ) of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1; the explicit dictionary is the API item epsilonWeil_character_explicit). For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over C: ε((V, r, N), ψ, dx) := ε(r, ψ, dx)·det(−r(F) | V^{r(I_K)}/(ker N)^{r(I_K)}) with F a geometric Frobenius lift (equivalently Deligne (8.12.4) ε = ε_0(r)·det(−F | V^I)^{-1}, V^I = (ker N)^{r(I)}); with the s-variable, ε(V, s) = ε(V ⊗ ω_s) (FSY (5.31)–(5.33)). For an ℓ-adic representation ρ (ℓ ≠ p) and ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C, ε(ρ, ψ, dx) := ε(ι WD(ρ), ψ, dx); it depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification and its ε_0-part only on the semisimplification.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (finite over Q_p): the Tau Ceti reciprocity isomorphism of ClassFieldTheory layer 9 is available only there; Deligne's theorem itself also covers archimedean and equal-characteristic local fields, which are recorded as a gap
normalisation of local class field theory: uniformiser ↔ geometric Frobenius (Deligne 2.3, CG18); Tau Ceti's artinMap must be inverted
uniqueness is local (Brauer induction); existence (Deligne §4) is global and uses Artin L-functions of number fields, whose functional equation has no owner (gap)
proofSteps: Uniqueness: every irreducible representation of W_K is r_0 ⊗ χ with r_0 of finite image (Deligne 4.10) and the finite-image part factors through Gal(L/K) for L/K finite Galois; Brauer's induction theorem (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 6) writes any virtual representation of a finite group as a Z-combination of representations induced from one-dimensional characters of subgroups; (1), (3), (4) then determine ε (Deligne 4.1–4.3).
Reduction for existence: Deligne 4.10–4.11 reduce by the type decomposition to the existence of an α-theory of constants for each finite Galois K'/K and each quasi-character α (4.9 (*)).

Existence (Deligne 4.12–4.16): globalise K'/K as the completion of a Galois extension of number fields at a non-split place (Lemme 4.13, Krasner and weak approximation), choose an idele class character with prescribed ramification (Lemme 4.14), and define the local constant at v as the global constant of 3.12 (functional equation of Artin L-functions, from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation, AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation) divided by the product of the local constants at the other places, known by induction on ramification (Lemmes 4.15, 4.16 for unramified and highly ramified twists).

Weil–Deligne extension: the factor det(−r(F) | V^{I}/(ker N)^{I}) is multiplicative on Frobenius semisimplifications; FSY (5.33) and Deligne (8.12.4) agree because Deligne's ε_0(r) = ε(r)·det(−r(F) | V^{r(I)}) (Deligne (5.1): ε(V, ψ, dx) = ε_0(V, ψ, dx)·det(−F, V^I)^{-1}; (3.4.3.3) for characters).

Dictionary with AL.1 (api epsilonWeil_character_explicit). Unramified ω: for n(ψ_0) = 0 and ∫_O dx = 1, ε(χ, ψ_0, dx) = 1 (Deligne (3.4.3.1)), so ε(χ, ψ_0, dx) = ∫_O dx in general ((3.3.2): ε(χ, ψ, a dx) = a·ε(χ, ψ, dx)); ψ = ψ_0(ϖ^ν x) has n(ψ) = ν and (3.3.3), ε(χ, ψ(ax), dx) = χ(a)‖a‖^{-1}ε(χ, ψ, dx), gives ε(χ, ψ, dx) = χ(ϖ^ν)q^ν∫_O dx; with ∫_O dx_ψ = q^{−ν/2} (the dual of O for ψ is ϖ^{−ν}O) and χ = ωω_s this is ω(ϖ^ν)q^{(1/2−s)ν}. Ramified ω: (3.4.3.2) is ε(χ, ψ, dx) = ∫_{γ^{-1}O^×} χ^{-1}(x)ψ(x)dx with γ of valuation n(ψ) + sw(χ) + 1 = ν + c (Deligne 3.4); substituting x = ϖ^{−(ν+c)}y, dx_ψ = q^{ν+c}dy_ψ, gives χ(ϖ^{ν+c})q^{(ν+c)}∫_{O^×}χ^{-1}(y)ψ(ϖ^{−ν−c}y)dy_ψ, which for χ = ωω_s is ω(ϖ^{ν+c})q^{(1/2−s)(ν+c)}𝔤(ω, ψ). Both agree with AL.1/explicit-epsilon-factors (i), (ii).
acceptance: For an unramified character χ with n(ψ) = 0 and ∫_{O_K} dx = 1, ε(χ, ψ, dx) = 1 (Deligne (3.4.3.1)); for the WD representation Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N), ε(Sp(2), ψ, dx) = ε(1)ε(ω)·det(−r(F) | V/ker N) = −1 (F acts by 1 on V/ker N).
Unramified twists: ε(χω, ψ, dx) = ω(π^{n(ψ)+a(χ)})ε(χ, ψ, dx) for ω unramified (Deligne (3.4.3.5)), which must agree with AL.1's ε(s, ω, ψ) = ω(ϖ^ν)q^{(1/2−s)ν} after the change of normalisation.

api.statement: Normalisations: ϖ a uniformiser, q the residue cardinality, ‖ϖ‖ = q^{-1}, ω_s = ‖·‖^s; n(ψ) = ν is the largest integer with ψ trivial on ϖ^{−ν}O (Deligne 3.4; it is the conductor exponent ν of ψ in AL.1); dx_ψ is the Haar measure self-dual for ψ, so ∫_O dx_ψ = q^{−ν/2}; a(ω) = c is the conductor exponent of a ramified character ω (the least c ≥ 1 with ω trivial on 1 + ϖ^cO). Then for a character ω of K^× and s ∈ C: if ω is unramified, ε(ωω_s, ψ, dx_ψ) = ω(ϖ^ν)·q^{(1/2−s)ν}; if ω is ramified, ε(ωω_s, ψ, dx_ψ) = ∫_{ϖ^{−(ν+c)}O^×} (ωω_s)^{-1}(x)ψ(x)dx_ψ = ω(ϖ^{ν+c})·q^{(1/2−s)(ν+c)}·𝔤(ω, ψ), with 𝔤(ω, ψ) = q^{(ν+c)/2}∫_{O^×} ω^{-1}(y)ψ(ϖ^{−ν−c}y)dy_ψ the Gauss sum of AL.1/local-gauss-sum. These are the formulas (i) and (ii) of AL.1/explicit-epsilon-factors, so Deligne's ε(ωω_s, ψ, dx_ψ) equals AL.1's ε(s, ω, ψ) for every character ω of K^×, every s and every ψ.

nodes.title: Required examples: the cyclotomic character, an unramified character, and the Tate curve
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite with residue cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, Φ an arithmetic and F = Φ^{-1} a geometric Frobenius lift. (1) Cyclotomic: WD(Q_ℓ(1)) = (ω, 0) with ω(Φ) = q; P(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q, L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, pure of weight −2; for K = Q_p and p ≠ ℓ this is the place-p component of χ_ℓ of G_Q. (2) Unramified character: for α ∈ O_E^×, WD(λ(α)) = (λ_W(α), 0), L(λ(α), X) = 1 − α^{-1}X, and λ^{geom}(γ) = λ(γ^{-1}). (3) Tate curve: for q_E ∈ K^× with v(q_E) > 0 and E = E_{q_E} the Tate curve, V_ℓE sits in 0 → Q_ℓ(1) → V_ℓE → Q_ℓ → 0, ρ(I_K) is infinite, and WD(V_ℓE) ≅ Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N) with N ≠ 0 mapping the quotient onto ker N = Q_ℓ(1) (N is v(q_E) times a generator, up to the scaling of Lemme 8.4.3); it is Frobenius-semisimple, not semisimple; its Frobenius semisimplification is itself and its semisimplification is (1 ⊕ ω, 0); L(V_ℓE, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, L(V_ℓE^∨, X) = 1 − X; it is pure of weight −1 (V_ℓE^∨ = H^1 of weight 1); the non-split twist by the unramified quadratic character η gives Sp(2) ⊗ η with L(V^∨, X) = 1 + X. (4) For ℓ | v(q_E) the residual E[ℓ] is unramified while V_ℓE is not.
hypotheses: the Tate curve and its Tate module are owned by Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 4 and R01.6; this node computes their Weil–Deligne data
ℓ ≠ p
proofSteps: (1): cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters (b) and grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (unramified case).
(2): unramified-character-lambda and the unramified case of the functor.

(3): the Tate parametrisation K̄^×/q_E^Z ≅ E(K̄) (EllipticCurves layer 4) gives E[ℓ^n] as an extension of Z/ℓ^n by μ_{ℓ^n} whose extension class is the Kummer class of q_E; σ ∈ I_K acts by e_2 ↦ e_2 + v(q_E)t_ℓ(σ)e_1 (Kummer theory with t_ℓ), so ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) with N e_2 = v(q_E)e_1; Frobenius acts by q on e_1 and by 1 on the quotient; then local-euler-factor, purity-of-weil-deligne-representations, frobenius-semisimplification.
(4): the Kummer class of q_E in K^×/K^{×ℓ} is unramified iff ℓ | v(q_E).
acceptance: The three Euler factors 1 − q^{-1}X, 1 − X, 1 + X are recovered for Q_ℓ(1), the split and the non-split multiplicative H^1.

The relation r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN is verified on the Tate curve with Φ arithmetic, and r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N with F geometric, matching PadicHodgeTheory R06.3's p-adic computation r(Φ) = diag(p, 1).

nodes.title: Upper-numbering breaks and the Swan conductor of a representation with finite wild image
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (the class Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, taken as a hypothesis on K: finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t)) satisfy it, but at the pinned commits instances are provided only for Q_p and, in Tau Ceti, for adic completions with finite residue field). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(AlgebraicClosure K/K) with its Krull topology, identified with Gal(K^sep/K) by restriction (TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv, an isomorphism of topological groups): when K has characteristic p the extension AlgebraicClosure K/K is not Galois and its fixed field is the perfect closure of K, so the finite Galois extensions L/K, their fixed-field correspondence and the ramification filtration are taken inside K^sep and transported to G_K along this isomorphism; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C, and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ or F = Q̄_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (R01.3/finite-wild-image); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. (i) Absolute upper filtration. For real u ≥ −1 let G_K^u ⊆ G_K be the closed normal subgroup of those σ whose restriction to every finite Galois L/K inside the fixed algebraic closure lies in Gal(L/K)^u, the upper-numbering group of LocalFieldsRamification layer 3; put G_K^{u+} := closure of ⋃_{w>u} G_K^w. Then G_K^{−1} = G_K, G_K^0 = I_K, G_K^{0+} = P_K, the image of G_K^u in Gal(L/K) is Gal(L/K)^u, and ⋂_u G_K^u = 1. (ii) Breaks. There is a unique decomposition V = ⊕_{λ ∈ Q, λ ≥ 0} V(λ) into G_K-stable subspaces, almost all zero, with V(0) = V^{ρ(P_K)} and, for λ > 0, V(λ)^{ρ(G_K^λ)} = 0 and V(λ)^{ρ(G_K^{λ+})} = V(λ). The λ with V(λ) ≠ 0 are the breaks (slopes) of V; the largest is the highest break. (iii) Swan conductor. Sw(V) := Σ_λ λ·dim_F V(λ) = ∫_0^∞ codim_V V^{ρ(G_K^u)} du = Σ_{i ≥ 1} (|G_i|/|G_0|)·codim_V V^{ρ(G_i)}, where in the last expression G = Gal(L/K) for any finite Galois L/K with ρ trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ P_K, G_i are its lower-numbering groups (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3), and G_i (i ≥ 1) acts on V through lifts in P_K: lifts exist because G_i is the image of G_K^{φ_{L/K}(i)} ⊆ P_K, and the action does not depend on the lift because ρ is trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ P_K. Sw(V) ∈ Q_{≥0}; its integrality is R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality. Sw depends only on the restriction of ρ to P_K together with the filtration, and is an isomorphism invariant.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued with perfect residue field of characteristic p; tier (F) is supplied by LocalFieldsRamification layers 3–4, tier (P) rests on the gap 'ramification filtration over a perfect infinite residue field'
char F ≠ p and ρ(P_K) finite; for F a finite extension of Q_p with p the residue characteristic and ρ(P_K) infinite, Sw is NOT defined here (p-adic Hodge theory owns that case)
the upper numbering is the one compatible with quotients; the lower-numbering sum is taken over a finite Galois L/K large enough for ρ|P_K, never over Gal(L/K) for an arbitrary L
proofSteps: Construct G_K^u as the intersection over finite Galois L/K of the preimages of Gal(L/K)^u; compatibility of these preimages in towers is upperRamificationGroup_quotient (Herbrand's theorem, LocalFieldsRamification layer 3); G_K^0 = I_K and G_K^{0+} = P_K follow from the layer-4 identifications of the images of I_K and P_K in finite quotients with G_0 and G_1.

Break decomposition: ρ(P_K) = H is a finite p-group and char F ≠ p, so V|_H is semisimple; the subgroups ρ(G_K^u), u > 0, form a decreasing family of normal subgroups of ρ(G_K) contained in H with finitely many jumps, and V(λ) is the image of the idempotent e_{G^{λ+}} − e_{G^λ} (e_N = |N|^{-1} Σ_{n∈N} n), which commutes with ρ(G_K) because each ρ(G_K^u) is normal; uniqueness from the defining invariant conditions (Ulmer 2016 §2; Katz's slope decomposition).

Equality of the three expressions for Sw: on V(λ) the function u ↦ codim V^{ρ(G^u)} is dim V(λ) on [0, λ] and 0 after, giving the integral; the substitution u = φ_{L/K}(t), dφ/dt = |G_t|/|G_0| (Herbrand function, LocalFieldsRamification layer 3) turns the integral into the lower-numbering sum, which is therefore independent of L (DDT §1.1 gives the integral form; Serre 1987 (1.2.1)–(1.2.2) the lower form).

Existence of L and rationality of the breaks: R01.3/wild-action-factors-through-a-finite-galois-extension gives a finite Galois L/K such that ρ|_{P_K} factors through Gal(L/K)_1. For u > 0 the group ρ(G_K^u) is then the image of Gal(L/K)^u, so the jumps of u ↦ ρ(G_K^u) are among the upper breaks of L/K: finitely many and rational; the filtration is left continuous (G^u = G_{ψ(u)}), which makes the idempotents e_{G^{λ+}} − e_{G^λ} sum to 1.
acceptance: Q_2(√−1)/Q_2: the nontrivial character χ_{−4} has upper break 1 and Sw = 1 (lower filtration G_1 = G, G_2 = 1 for the uniformiser 1 + i); Q_2(√2)/Q_2: the character χ_8 has break 2 and Sw = 2 (v(σ√2 − √2) = 3), matching the LocalFieldsRamification example in which Q_2(√2) has different exponent 3

Over L = Q_2(ζ_8) (lower jumps 1 and 3, |G_0| = |G_1| = 4, |G_2| = |G_3| = 2), the weighted sum for χ_8 is 1 + 2/4 + 2/4 = 2 = Sw(χ_8), the same value as over Q_2(√2): independence of the finite quotient on a wild example at 2
A tamely ramified character (p ∤ order of χ(I_K)) has the single break 0 and Sw = 0

nodes.title: Finiteness of the wild inertia image for coefficients of characteristic different from p
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p > 0 (the local setting of R01.3), P_K ⊆ G_K its wild inertia group, a closed normal pro-p subgroup (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4), and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation on a finite-dimensional F-vector space V in the sense of R01.1. Then ρ(P_K) is a finite p-group in each of the following cases: (a) F carries the discrete topology (a finite field or F̄_ℓ), where even ρ(G_K) is finite; (b) F = C with its usual topology, where again ρ(G_K) is finite; (c) F = E a finite extension of Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p; (d) F = Q̄_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p. In case (c), for every G_K-stable O_E-lattice Λ ⊂ V the reduction map ρ(P_K) → GL(Λ/m_EΛ) is injective. For ℓ = p the conclusion of (c) fails in general.
hypotheses: K as in the local setting of R01.3; that P_K is pro-p: tier (F) (finite residue field) is supplied by the LocalFieldsRamification layers cited; tier (P) rests on the gap 'Ramification filtration over a perfect infinite residue field'
continuity in the sense of R01.1 for the stated topology of F
ℓ ≠ p in (c) and (d)
proofSteps: (a), (b): ρ has open kernel and finite image (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients, with its complement for F = C); a finite continuous image of the pro-p group P_K is a p-group.

(c): choose a G_K-stable O_E-lattice Λ (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices (c)), so that ρ: G_K → GL(Λ) ≅ GL_n(O_E) is continuous. Let U_i := ker(GL(Λ) → GL(Λ/m_E^iΛ)) for i ≥ 1: open normal subgroups with ⋂ U_i = 1 and U_i/U_{i+1} ≅ M_n(k_E) through x ↦ (x − 1)/ϖ^i, an ℓ-group. The closed subgroup H := P_K ∩ ρ^{-1}(U_1) of P_K is pro-p; the image of H in each finite group U_1/U_{i+1} is a quotient of a pro-p group, hence a p-group, and a subgroup of an ℓ-group, hence trivial because ℓ ≠ p; so ρ(H) ⊆ ⋂ U_i = 1. Therefore ρ(P_K) maps injectively to the finite group GL(Λ/m_EΛ).
(d): ρ takes values in GL_n(E) for a finite extension E/Q_ℓ (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field); apply (c).
Failure for ℓ = p: for p odd the p-adic cyclotomic character of G_{Q_p} maps P_{Q_p} onto 1 + pZ_p, the pro-p Sylow subgroup of Gal(Q_p(μ_{p^∞})/Q_p) ≅ Z_p^×, which is infinite.
acceptance: The ℓ-adic Tate module of a Tate curve (ℓ ≠ p): ρ(I_K) is infinite and ρ(P_K) = 1
χ_p: G_{Q_p} → Z_p^× for p odd: χ_p(P_{Q_p}) = 1 + pZ_p is infinite, so ℓ ≠ p cannot be dropped
The character of G_{Q_2} with values ±1 in Q̄_3^× cutting out Q_2(√2): its image on P_{Q_2} is {±1}, mapped injectively to F̄_3^×

nodes.title: Wild action factors through a finite Galois extension
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. There is a finite Galois L/K in K^sep with Gal(K^sep/L)∩P_K⊂kerρ.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: ker(ρ|_{P_K}) is closed in P_K (the stabiliser of each vector is closed, the action being continuous and V Hausdorff) and of finite index, hence open in P_K; so it equals P_K ∩ O for an open subset O of G_K containing 1.

The group Gal(K^sep/K) is profinite, so O contains an open normal subgroup U (mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one, applied on Gal(K^sep/K) and transported by TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv), and U contains the fixing subgroup of a finite normal, hence finite Galois, subextension L/K of K^sep (tauceti:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.exists_finiteDimensional_normal_fixingSubgroup_le). Then Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ P_K ⊆ ker ρ: this is (a).
acceptance: The fixed-field argument uses the separable closure even for imperfect K.

nodes.title: Equivariance of finite wild factorisation
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. For such L the wild action factors uniquely through Gal(L/K)₁ with image ρ(P_K); conjugation by any element of Gal(L/K) is intertwined with conjugation by any lift in G_K.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: The restriction P_K→Gal(L/K) has image Gal(L/K)₁ by the local tame-quotient supplier and has kernel Gal(K^sep/L)∩P_K, which ρ kills by R01.3/wild-action-factors-through-a-finite-galois-extension. The quotient universal property gives the unique factor. Since P_K is normal in G_K, conjugation by any lift of a finite Galois element is intertwined by ρ; different lifts give the same formula on the quotient.
acceptance: The representation is on the finite wild subgroup, not necessarily on all Gal(L/K).

nodes.title: The Artin conductor exponent and its wild part
nodes.statement: Local setting (fixed throughout R01.3): K is a field complete for a discrete valuation v_K normalised by v_K(K^×) = Z, with ring of integers O_K, maximal ideal m_K and PERFECT residue field k of characteristic p > 0; K has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic (0, p)) or p (equal characteristic, e.g. k((t))). Tier (F): k finite, i.e. K is a nonarchimedean local field (the class Mathlib IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, taken as a hypothesis on K: finite extensions of Q_p and of F_p((t)) satisfy it, but at the pinned commits instances are provided only for Q_p and, in Tau Ceti, for adic completions with finite residue field). Tier (P): k perfect and arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed, as for F̄_q((t)) or the completion of K^ur). G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology; I_K ⊇ P_K are inertia and wild inertia (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4). Coefficients: F is a field of characteristic different from p (characteristic 0, e.g. C, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ; or a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p), V a finite-dimensional F-vector space and ρ: G_K → GL_F(V) a continuous representation in the sense of R01.1 (discrete topology for finite F, the ℓ-adic topology for E, the usual topology for C) such that ρ(P_K) is finite. Finiteness of ρ(P_K) is automatic for finite F, for F = C (continuity forces finite image) and for F = E finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (ρ(G_K) lies in a compact GL(Λ) whose open pro-ℓ subgroup meets the pro-p group ρ(P_K) trivially); it is a hypothesis when ℓ = p. The Artin conductor exponent is a(V) := codim_V V^{ρ(I_K)} + Sw(V) = (dim V − dim V^{ρ(I_K)}) + Sw(V), with Sw from R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor; ε(V) := codim V^{ρ(I_K)} is the tame part and Sw(V) = b(V) the wild part. When ρ(I_K) is finite and G = Gal(L/K) for a finite Galois L/K with ρ trivial on Gal(K^sep/L) ∩ I_K, a(V) = Σ_{i ≥ 0} (|G_i|/|G_0|)·dim_F(V/V^{G_i}) (Serre (1.2.1)) = dim V/V^{G_0} + b(V) (Serre (1.2.2)). For an ℓ-adic representation (ℓ ≠ p) with infinite inertia image, V^{ρ(I_K)} is the actual subspace of inertia invariants; it equals (ker N)^{r(I_K)} for the Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) of R01.2, which is where the monodromy term enters (R01.3/conductor-of-a-weil-deligne-representation). For a residual representation ρ̄ over a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, a(ρ̄) uses ρ̄'s own (finite) inertia action, never that of a lift. Representations over fields of characteristic p (for instance mod p representations of G_K with K of residue characteristic p) are excluded, as in Serre 1987, which restricts N to places prime to p. a(V) ∈ Q_{≥0}; it is a nonnegative integer by R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality, and the exponent used in every global conductor.
hypotheses: same local setting and coefficients as R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor
the tame part is the codimension of the invariants of the ACTUAL inertia image (for ℓ-adic ρ this already contains the monodromy contribution)
integrality is a theorem (R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality), not visible from the formula; the wild term is never omitted at p = 2 or 3
proofSteps: Define a(V) by the displayed formula; for finite inertia image the identity with Serre's lower-numbering sum is the i = 0 term (|G_0|/|G_0|)·codim V^{G_0} plus the Swan sum of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor (Serre 1987 §1.2).
Independence of L and of the extension of the valuation: inherited from the Swan term (Herbrand) and from I_K being normal in G_K (conjugate subspaces of invariants have equal dimension).

For ℓ-adic ρ = (r, N) after R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor: a vector fixed by ρ(I_K) is fixed by the open subgroup J ⊆ I_K on which r is trivial, where ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) with t_ℓ(σ) ≠ 0 for some σ ∈ J, so Nv = 0, and then r(σ)v = v for σ ∈ I_K; conversely; hence V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N)^{r(I_K)} (Ulmer 2016 §8, PDF p. 7: equation (8.1) with m = 0 gives V_N^{I_F} = V_ℓ^{I_F}).
acceptance: Steinberg: for the ℓ-adic Tate module V_ℓ of a Tate curve over K (ℓ ≠ p), V^{I_K} is one-dimensional and P_K acts trivially, so a = 1

A tamely ramified two-dimensional residual representation with ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ ψ ⊕ ψ^q, ψ ≠ 1 of order prime to p, has no inertia invariants and a = 2 (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.3 Theorem 3.3 initial case)
Over Q_2: a(χ_{−4}) = 2 and a(χ_8) = 3, the conductors 4 and 8 of the Dirichlet characters of Q(√−1) and Q(√2) at 2

nodes.title: Conductor of a ramified character
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. For a ramified character χ with finite wild image, Sw(χ)=u(χ) and a(χ)=1+u(χ), where u(χ) is its upper break and is an integer. For tame ramified χ the break is zero.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: (d): let K_χ be the fixed field of ker χ, an abelian extension of K that may be infinite (χ(P_K) is finite but χ need not have finite image). u(χ) is a jump of the upper filtration of Gal(K_χ/K) = G_K/ker χ, hence of Gal(L/K) for some finite subextension L/K (the filtration of the quotient is the image of the filtration, R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor (i)); L/K is abelian, so the jump is an integer by the Hasse–Arf theorem (LocalFieldsRamification layer 3, hasseArf, Serre LF V §7). Sw(χ) = u(χ) by the integral formula, and codim χ^{I_K} = 1 when χ is ramified.
acceptance: An unramified character instead has conductor zero.

nodes.title: Integrality for a characteristic-zero finite-group representation
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. For a finite Galois extension L/K and a characteristic-zero representation W of Gal(L/K), a(W) and Sw(W) are nonnegative integers.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: Characteristic 0, finite group (Artin's theorem; Serre 1961, Théorème 2): let W be a representation, over a field of characteristic 0, of G = Gal(L/K′) for a finite Galois extension L/K′ of fields of the local setting. By Brauer's induction theorem (InductionRestriction layer 6) the character of W is a Z-combination of characters Ind_H^G ψ with ψ one-dimensional; a(Ind_H^G ψ) = δ(L^H/K′)·ψ(1) + f(L^H/K′)·a(ψ) by R01.3/local-induction-formula (c), which uses no integrality, and a(ψ) ∈ Z by (d). The lower-numbering formula is linear in the character, so a(W) ∈ Z, and a(W) ≥ 0 from the formula.
The tame term dimW−dimW^{I} is an integer, so Sw(W)=a(W)−(dimW−dimW^{I}) is an integer too; both conductors are nonnegative by their defining codimension sums.
acceptance: Brauer induction uses the local conductor formula without assuming integrality in its proof.

nodes.title: Integrality of Swan and Artin conductors
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. Both Sw(V) and a(V) are nonnegative integers.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: Choose a finite Galois L/K killing the wild kernel by R01.3/wild-action-factors-through-a-finite-galois-extension. Replace K by its maximal unramified subfield in L when computing the lower sum, so G₀=Gal(L/(L∩K^ur)) is inertia and G₁ is wild inertia. Extension of coefficient fields preserves invariant dimensions and conductors by R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor, so take algebraically closed coefficients.

R01.3/swan-conductor-orbit-formula expresses Sw(V) as a sum, with nonnegative integral multiplicities, of Swan conductors of characteristic-zero representations of G₀. R01.3/artin-conductor-integral-finite-group makes every summand integral. Then a(V)=Sw(V)+dimV−dimV^{I_K} is integral, and both terms are nonnegative.
acceptance: Infinite tame inertia and modular coefficients prime to p are allowed.

nodes.title: Independence of conductor choices
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. The conductors do not depend on the auxiliary finite Galois extension, the algebraic closure, or the valuation extension, and are invariant under representation isomorphism.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: Independence (b): the integral formula of R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor is intrinsic to G_K; changing the algebraic closure conjugates ρ by an isomorphism, and conjugate subgroups have invariant subspaces of equal dimension.
acceptance: The intrinsic upper-filtration integral gives the same value after enlarging L.

nodes.title: Vanishing criteria for conductors
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap. Then a(V)=0 iff inertia acts trivially; Sw(V)=0 iff wild inertia acts trivially; and a(V)=codim V^{I_K} iff V is tame.
hypotheses: Let K be complete for a normalised discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p>0. Let F be a topological field of characteristic different from p, and V a finite-dimensional continuous F-representation of G_K with finite wild image. The arbitrary-perfect-residue-field case retains the recorded ramification-theory gap.
proofSteps: (c) is read off the formula: every term is ≥ 0, the i = 0 term vanishes iff G_0 acts trivially, and the wild sum vanishes iff G_1 = image of P_K acts trivially (Serre 1987 (b), (c)).
acceptance: A nontrivial tame character has Swan zero but Artin conductor one.

nodes.title: Lifting a simple wild-inertia module
nodes.statement: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p. Every simple F[G₁]-module θ has a characteristic-zero lift θ̃ preserving invariant dimensions for every subgroup of G₁. The G₀-stabilisers of θ and θ̃ agree, and θ̃ extends to its stabiliser T because T/G₁ is cyclic.
hypotheses: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p.
proofSteps: (b): if char F = ℓ > 0 then ℓ ∤ |G_1|, F[G_1] is semisimple and reduction modulo ℓ is a bijection between the simple modules in characteristic 0 and in characteristic ℓ that preserves the dimensions of the invariants of every subgroup (Brumer–Kramer, Lemma 2.7: the averaging idempotents e_N have coefficients in Z[1/p]). The bijection commutes with conjugation by G_0, so the two stabilisers agree. T/G_1 is cyclic, so the T-stable θ̃ extends to T (Clifford theory and the vanishing of H²(C, C^×) for C cyclic: InductionRestriction layers 5 and 7).
acceptance: Invariant dimensions alone do not uniquely identify a lift; the reduction bijection does.

sources.match: Source context for Lifting a simple wild-inertia module. Brumer–Kramer, Lemma 2.7: for a field k of characteristic l in which |G| is invertible, an absolutely irreducible k[G]-module lifts to characteristic 0 with dim_k W^N = dim_F V^N for every subgroup N, so the same conductor; used here for the p-group G_1. The exact extracted statement and any generalisation are justified by this node’s proof plan, not by treating the source’s other bundle clauses as this declaration.

nodes.title: Swan conductor of a constituent orbit
nodes.statement: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p. Let θ be a simple F[G₁]-module, θ̃ its characteristic-zero lift and T⊆G₀ its isomorphism-class stabiliser, as in R01.3/wild-character-lift. If θ̃_T extends θ̃ to T, then Res_{G₁}Ind_T^{G₀}θ̃_T is the sum of the distinct orbit conjugates, once each, and Sw(Ind_T^{G₀}θ̃_T)=[G₀:T]sw(θ).
hypotheses: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p.
proofSteps: For every subgroup G_i of G₁, the lift θ̃ preserves dim θ^{G_i}. Since each G_i is normal in G₀, conjugate modules have the same invariant dimensions and the same lower-numbering Swan sum.

Mackey restriction along the normal G₁⊆T⊆G₀ gives Res_{G₁}Ind_T^{G₀}θ̃_T=⊕_{g∈G₀/T}θ̃^g, with distinct isomorphism classes because T is the stabiliser. Add their identical invariant-codimension sums to get Sw(Ind_T^{G₀}θ̃_T)=[G₀:T]sw(θ).
acceptance: Normality of each G_i makes sw invariant under conjugation.

nodes.title: Orbit formula for Swan conductors
nodes.statement: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p. If V is a continuous representation of G_{K₀} whose wild action factors through this G₁ compatibly with inertia conjugation, choose one simple F[G₁]-module θ in each G₀-orbit O, let T be its stabiliser and θ̃_T the extension supplied by R01.3/wild-character-lift. Then its multiplicities m_θ are constant on G₀-orbits and Sw(V)=∑_O m_θSw(Ind_T^{G₀}θ̃_T).
hypotheses: Let M/K₀ be a finite totally ramified Galois extension in the local setting, with inertia G₀, wild group G₁ and lower groups G_i. Let F be algebraically closed of characteristic different from p.
The wild factorisation of V comes from a G_{K₀}-representation and intertwines inertia conjugation; an arbitrary G₁-module need not have constant orbit multiplicities.
proofSteps: (d): V|_{G_1} = ⊕_θ θ^{m_θ}; for g̃ ∈ I_K lifting g ∈ G_0, ρ(g̃) carries the θ-isotypic component onto that of a conjugate of θ (R01.3/finite-wild-factorisation-equivariant), so m_θ is constant on orbits. Sw(V) = sw(V|_{G_1}) = Σ_θ m_θ·sw(θ) in the lower-numbering form, the groups G_i (i ≥ 1) of Gal(L/K) being those of G_0 = Gal(L/L ∩ K^ur); group the sum by orbits and apply (c).
acceptance: The formula reduces modular and infinite-tame cases to characteristic-zero finite-group conductors.
