nodes.title: Two transvections with distinct axes generate SL_2(F_ℓ)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a prime and a, b ∈ F_ℓ^×. The elements x = [[1, a], [0, 1]] and y = [[1, 0], [b, 1]] generate SL_2(F_ℓ). Consequently, if V is a plane over F_ℓ and G ⊂ GL(V) contains two elements of order ℓ whose fixed lines are distinct, then G ⊃ SL(V). The prime field is essential: over F_q with q = ℓ^n, n ≥ 2, the group generated by x and y can be smaller than SL_2(F_q) even when ab generates F_q (order 120 in SL_2(F_9) for (ab)² = −1; dihedral in characteristic 2); the general case is R01.4/subgroups-of-psl2-with-several-sylow-p-subgroups.
hypotheses: ℓ prime; the coefficient field is the prime field F_ℓ = ℤ/ℓ
a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0; no restriction on ℓ (ℓ = 2, 3 included)
proofSteps: x^n = [[1, na], [0, 1]], and a ≠ 0 generates the additive group of ℤ/ℓ; so the subgroup generated by x is the group of all upper unitriangular matrices, and likewise y generates all lower unitriangular matrices.

For the index set Fin 2 the elementary transvections are exactly the matrices [[1, c], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [c, 1]]; over a field they generate the special linear group (tauceti:Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field). Hence x and y generate SL_2(F_ℓ) (mathlib:Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup).

Consequence: an element of order ℓ of GL(V) is unipotent and fixes exactly one line (R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups). In a basis (e_1, e_2) with e_1, e_2 on the two fixed lines the two elements are x and y for some a, b ≠ 0, and the subgroup SL(V) does not depend on the basis. This is the argument of Serre 1972, §2.4, who quotes Bourbaki A III p. 104 prop. 17 for the generation.
acceptance: ℓ = 2: [[1, 1], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [1, 1]] are two transpositions of SL_2(F_2) = GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 and generate it.
ℓ = 3 and ℓ = 5: the two elements with a = b = 1 generate groups of order 24 = |SL_2(F_3)| and 120 = |SL_2(F_5)|.
Not over F_9: for λ ∈ F_9 with λ² = −1, [[1, 1], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [λ, 1]] generate a group of order 120 < 720 = |SL_2(F_9)|.

sources.locator: §2.4, proof of Proposition 15, printed p. 280 (read on the page image)
sources.match: Serre's reduction to the two matrices x, y with a, b ≠ 0, followed by ‘SL_2(F_p) est engendré par ses sous-groupes’ of upper and lower unitriangular matrices, cf. Bourbaki A III p. 104 prop. 17; the lemma is that generation statement.

nodes.title: Dihedral projective image if and only if induced from an index-two subgroup
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group, k an algebraically closed field (any characteristic) and ρ : Γ → GL_2(k) a homomorphism whose projectivisation π∘ρ has open kernel and finite image (automatic for k = F̄_p discrete and ρ continuous). (a) The following are equivalent: (1) ρ is irreducible and π(ρ(Γ)) is dihedral of order 2n for some n ≥ 2; (2) ρ ≅ Ind_Δ^Γ χ (R01.1/continuous-induction) for an open subgroup Δ of index 2 and a continuous character χ : Δ → k^× with χ ≠ χ^σ, where χ^σ(δ) = χ(σ δ σ⁻¹) for any σ ∈ Γ ∖ Δ. (b) In (2), ρ|_Δ ≅ χ ⊕ χ^σ, π(ρ(Δ)) is cyclic of order n = order of χ/χ^σ (so char k ∤ n), elements of ρ(Γ ∖ Δ) have trace 0, and det ρ = (χ ∘ Ver_{Γ→Δ}) · ε_Δ (R01.1/determinant-of-induced-representation; Ver_{Γ→Δ} is the transfer and ε_Δ : Γ → Γ/Δ ≅ {±1} ⊂ k^× the sign character, which is the quadratic character with kernel Δ when char k ≠ 2 and is trivial when char k = 2). For n ≥ 3, Δ is unique: it is the preimage of the cyclic subgroup of order n; for n = 2 (Klein image) there are exactly three such Δ. (c) If char k ≠ 2 and ρ is irreducible, ρ ≅ Ind_Δ^Γ χ for some χ iff ρ ⊗ ε_Δ ≅ ρ. (d) If ρ is irreducible and ρ|_{Γ′} is reducible for an open normal subgroup Γ′ with Γ/Γ′ abelian, then ρ(Γ′) is diagonalisable (so char k does not divide the order of π(ρ(Γ′))) and one of two cases holds. Either ρ(Γ′) has two distinct eigencharacters; then ρ is induced from the stabiliser of one of the two eigenlines of ρ(Γ′), an open subgroup of index 2 containing Γ′. Or ρ(Γ′) is scalar; then π(ρ(Γ)) is an abelian quotient of Γ/Γ′, and irreducibility of ρ forces char k ≠ 2 and π(ρ(Γ)) ≅ (ℤ/2)², so ρ is induced from each of the three index-2 subgroups containing ker(π∘ρ) ⊃ Γ′ (example: ρ(Γ) the quaternion group Q_8 ⊂ SL_2(k) and Γ′ the preimage of its centre). When Γ/Γ′ is cyclic the scalar case does not occur. (e) In characteristic 2, an irreducible ρ with dihedral projective image has n odd ≥ 3; every value of det ρ of finite order has odd order (k^× has no element of order 2), in particular det ρ has odd order when k = F̄_2 and ρ has finite image (for instance ρ continuous for the discrete topology of F̄_2).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; when k = ℚ̄_ℓ or ℂ the dihedral image is finite by hypothesis
Δ open of index 2; χ continuous for the topology in which ρ is continuous
(c) needs char k ≠ 2 (ε_Δ is trivial modulo 2)
proofSteps: (2) ⇒ (1): in a basis {e, σe} of Ind χ, ρ(δ) = diag(χ(δ), χ^σ(δ)) and ρ(σ) is antidiagonal. Since χ ≠ χ^σ the only Δ-stable lines are the two eigenlines, swapped by σ, so ρ is irreducible (characteristic-free; when ρ factors through a finite quotient of Γ and char k = 0 this is also tauceti:TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacter_iff, which is stated for a finite group, a normal subgroup and an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and does not apply when χ has infinite image). The projective image of Δ is isomorphic, by diag(a, b) ↦ a/b, to the group of values of χ/χ^σ, a finite subgroup of k^× and therefore cyclic (mathlib:isCyclic_subgroup_units), of order n ≥ 2 prime to char k; an antidiagonal element is an involution in PGL_2 inverting it, so the image is dihedral of order 2n.

(1) ⇒ (2): let C ⊂ π(ρ(Γ)) be a cyclic subgroup of index 2 and Δ its preimage, open of index 2. ρ(Δ) is a central extension of a cyclic group, hence abelian, and has a common eigenvector over k (tauceti:TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed) with character χ. Frobenius reciprocity (R01.1/continuous-induction; for an open subgroup of finite index induction is both adjoints of restriction) turns the inclusion of the eigenline χ ⊂ ρ|_Δ into a nonzero Γ-map Ind χ → ρ, surjective since ρ is irreducible and bijective since both have dimension 2; χ = χ^σ would make Ind χ ≅ χ̃ ⊗ k[Γ/Δ] reducible, χ̃ an extension of χ (which exists as H²(ℤ/2, k^×) = k^×/k^{×2} = 1).

(b) The cyclic subgroup of order n ≥ 3 is characteristic in the dihedral group; the Klein group has three subgroups of order 2. The trace of an antidiagonal matrix is 0 (for a finite group this vanishing of an induced character off a subgroup of index two is tauceti:TauCeti.character_indFDRep_eq_zero_of_notMem_of_index_two). The determinant formula is R01.1/determinant-of-induced-representation with rank 1.

(c) Ind χ ⊗ ε_Δ ≅ Ind(χ ⊗ ε_Δ|_Δ) = Ind χ; conversely an isomorphism A : ρ ≅ ρ ⊗ ε_Δ has A² scalar by Schur (A² commutes with ρ; End_Γ = k by R01.1/absolutely-irreducible), A non-scalar (ε_Δ ≠ 1 and char ≠ 2), and its two eigenspaces are Δ-stable lines, so ρ|_Δ is reducible and (1) ⇒ (2) applies with this Δ.

(d) ρ|_{Γ′} is semisimple (tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype), so ρ|_{Γ′} ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2. If ψ_1 ≠ ψ_2, the only Γ′-stable lines are the two eigenlines; the translate ρ(g)D of a Γ′-stable line D is Γ′-stable (tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.conjSubrep), so Γ permutes the two lines, and the translates of one of them span (tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.iSup_conjSubrep_eq_top), so the action is transitive; the stabiliser Δ of one line has index 2, contains Γ′, and Frobenius reciprocity gives ρ ≅ Ind_Δ^Γ of the character of Δ on that line. If ψ_1 = ψ_2, ρ(Γ′) is scalar and π(ρ(Γ)) is a quotient of the abelian group Γ/Γ′; then R01.4/irreducible-with-abelian-projective-image-is-klein gives char k ≠ 2 and π(ρ(Γ)) ≅ (ℤ/2)², and (a), (b) apply with n = 2.
(e) In characteristic 2 the image of Δ is diagonalisable, so its projective image has odd order n; n = 2 is excluded since the Klein group would be a 2-group fixing a line.
acceptance: Instance (Swinnerton-Dyer's mod-23 representation): for L the splitting field of x³ − x − 1 (Galois group S_3, quadratic subfield ℚ(√−23)), the standard two-dimensional representation of S_3 over F̄_23 composed with G_ℚ → S_3 is Ind_{G_{ℚ(√−23)}}^{G_ℚ} χ with χ of order 3; projective image S_3, dihedral of order 6.

Klein case: M = ℚ(√((2 + √2)(3 + √3))) is Galois over ℚ with group the quaternion group Q_8 (σ : √2 ↦ −√2 and τ : √3 ↦ −√3 lift to elements of order 4 with σ² = τ² = −1 on the generator) and biquadratic subfield ℚ(√2, √3). The faithful representation Q_8 ⊂ SL_2(ℂ) composed with G_ℚ → Gal(M/ℚ) is irreducible with projective image (ℤ/2)², and is induced from each of the three quadratic subfields ℚ(√2), ℚ(√3), ℚ(√6). Not every biquadratic field occurs: ℚ(i, √2) lies in no Q_8-extension of ℚ.
Characteristic-2 instance: E[2] for E : y² = x³ − 2 is Ind from ℚ(√−3) of a character of order 3 (n = 3 odd).

nodes.title: An irreducible subgroup of GL_2 with abelian projective image has projective image (ℤ/2)²
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and G ⊂ GL_2(k) a subgroup acting irreducibly on k² whose image π(G) in PGL_2(k) is abelian. Then char k ≠ 2, G is not abelian, π(G) ≅ (ℤ/2)², and every non-scalar element of G has trace 0 and scalar square. In particular an irreducible subgroup of GL_2(k) never has cyclic projective image, and in characteristic 2 it never has abelian projective image. No finiteness of G is assumed.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed, of any characteristic
G irreducible on k² (so absolutely irreducible); G may be infinite
proofSteps: Let g ∈ G be non-scalar. For h ∈ G, π(h) commutes with π(g), so h g h⁻¹ = c(h)·g with c(h) ∈ k^×; c is a homomorphism G → k^×, and taking determinants gives c(h)² = 1.

c ≠ 1: otherwise g commutes with G, and an eigenspace of g (k is algebraically closed) is a G-stable subspace, non-zero and proper because g is not scalar (mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar identifies the scalars with the centre), against irreducibility. So c(h) = −1 ≠ 1 for some h: char k ≠ 2 and G is not abelian. Then Tr g = Tr(h g h⁻¹) = −Tr g, so Tr g = 0, and g² = −det g is scalar by Cayley–Hamilton.

Hence every element of π(G) has order ≤ 2 (mathlib:Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup). Diagonalise g = diag(μ, −μ), μ ≠ −μ. The matrices h with h g h⁻¹ = g are the diagonal ones and those with h g h⁻¹ = −g the antidiagonal ones; a non-scalar diagonal element of G has trace 0 by the previous step, so it is a scalar multiple of g. So ker c has image {1, π(g)} in π(G), of index 2, and |π(G)| = 4 with exponent 2.
acceptance: The quaternion group generated by [[i, 0], [0, −i]] and [[0, 1], [−1, 0]] in SL_2(ℂ): irreducible, projective image (ℤ/2)², every non-central element has trace 0 and square −1.
The normaliser of the split Cartan of GL_2(F_3), dihedral of order 8, is irreducible over F̄_3 with projective image (ℤ/2)².
Characteristic 2: the non-split Cartan F_4^× ⊂ GL_2(F_2) has cyclic projective image of order 3 and is reducible over F̄_2, as the lemma requires.

sources.locator: proof of Lemma 1.13, p. 8 of arXiv v2
sources.match: In the source G lies in the normaliser N of the diagonal torus T and φ is the map N → N/T ≅ ℤ/2: if φ(G) were trivial, G would lie in T, hence be abelian and reducible. This is the fact ‘an abelian subgroup of GL_2 over an algebraically closed field is reducible’ used in the proof; the source does not state the lemma, which is the node's own formulation.

nodes.title: Bad dihedral representations
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and p* := (−1)^{(p−1)/2} p. For a number field F let K_F := F(ζ_p) and let F′ ⊂ K_F be the fixed field of the subgroup of squares of the cyclic group Gal(K_F/F) (so F′ = F if [K_F : F] is odd, and F′ is the quadratic subextension of K_F/F otherwise). For F = ℚ, F′ = ℚ(√p*), the quadratic subfield of ℚ(ζ_p), equal to ℚ(g) for the quadratic Gauss sum g with g² = p* (mathlib:gaussSum_sq). Let k be a finite field of characteristic p (or k = F̄_p) and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous. ρ̄ is bad dihedral if ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is not absolutely irreducible. For F = ℚ this is Dieulefait–Pacetti Definition 1.12: ρ̄ irreducible (over F̄_p) and ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} reducible. Equivalently (R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion) ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is not; ‘not bad dihedral and absolutely irreducible’ is Wiles's condition ‘ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} absolutely irreducible’.
hypotheses: p odd
coefficients finite of characteristic p or F̄_p; ‘reducible’ means not absolutely irreducible
F′ is defined by the squares of Gal(F(ζ_p)/F), not by adjoining √p* (for F ∋ √p*, F′ = F(ζ_p)^{Gal²} is different)
proofSteps: Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/p)^× (mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.galEquivZMod, i.e. mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow applied with the irreducibility of the cyclotomic polynomial over ℚ) is cyclic of even order p − 1, its squares form the unique index-2 subgroup, and its fixed field is ℚ(g) with g² = χ(−1)p = p* for χ the quadratic character of the field ℤ/p and a primitive additive character with values in a domain containing ζ_p (mathlib:gaussSum_sq). For a general number field F the cyclotomic polynomial need not be irreducible over F and only the injection Gal(F(ζ_p)/F) → (ℤ/p)^× is available (mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow_injective); it makes Gal(F(ζ_p)/F) cyclic, which is all that the definition of F′ uses.
Absolute irreducibility is invariant under extension of k (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible), so the definition does not depend on k.
acceptance: Instance: the mod-23 representation attached to x³ − x − 1 (standard representation of S_3 over F_23 through G_ℚ → Gal(L/ℚ)) is absolutely irreducible and odd, and its restriction to G_{ℚ(√−23)} has image of order 3 with eigenvalues primitive cube roots of unity not in F_23: irreducible over F_23 but not absolutely irreducible. So it is bad dihedral (p = 23, p* = −23).
If p ≥ 5 and ρ̄(G_ℚ) ⊇ SL_2(F_p) then ρ̄ is not bad dihedral (the image of G_{ℚ(√p*)} has index ≤ 2 and contains SL_2(F_p)).

uses.how: the residual hypothesis ‘ρ̄|_{ℚ(√p*)} absolutely irreducible’ of modularity lifting
Taylor–Wiles primes exist when ρ̄|_{G_L} is absolutely irreducible, L = ℚ(√p*)
bad dihedral ρ̄ have p = 2k − 1 or p = 2k − 3
members in the Fontaine–Laffaille range are not bad dihedral
hypothesis ρ̄|_{G_L} absolutely irreducible for L = ℚ(√ℓ*)
identification of the two residual hypotheses
ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible over a totally real F

A representation Ind_{G_{ℚ(ζ_5)}}^{G_F} χ with χ ≠ χ^σ is bad dihedral; the tempting definition ‘ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(√p*)}} reducible’ declares no representation of G_F bad dihedral.

nodes.title: The quadratic–cyclotomic irreducibility criterion and projective inertia of bad dihedral representations
nodes.statement: (a) [cyclic restriction criterion] Let L/F be a finite cyclic Galois extension of fields, F′ ⊂ L the fixed field of the subgroup of squares of Gal(L/F), k an algebraically closed field and ρ : G_F → GL_2(k) a homomorphism with open kernel. Then ρ|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible iff ρ|_{G_L} is irreducible. (b) [Dieulefait–Pacetti Lemma 1.13, strengthened] Let F be a number field, p an odd prime, F′ as in R01.4/bad-dihedral-representation, m ≥ 1 and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous with k finite of characteristic p. The following are equivalent: (1) ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} absolutely irreducible; (2) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible; (3) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^m})}} absolutely irreducible. No oddness hypothesis is needed (the source assumes ρ̄ odd and F = ℚ). (c) If ρ̄ is bad dihedral then ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p ≅ Ind_{G_{F′}}^{G_F} χ with χ ≠ χ^σ, the projective image is dihedral of order 2n with p ∤ n, and |ρ̄(G_F)| is prime to p. (d) [Dieulefait–Pacetti Lemma 1.14, inertia part] If F = ℚ and ρ̄ is bad dihedral, then the projective image of ρ̄(I_p) has order ≤ 2 (so the source; in fact exactly 2, since ℚ(√p*) is ramified at p). Writing (ρ̄|_{I_p}) ⊗ F̄_p ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 (tame characters, R01.2/tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations), ψ_1/ψ_2 has order ≤ 2: in niveau 1, ψ_1/ψ_2 = ω^a with (p − 1) | 2a; in niveau 2, ψ_1 = ω_2^b, ψ_2 = ω_2^{pb} with (p + 1) | 2b. The translation into Serre weights (p = 2k(ρ̄) − 1 in niveau 1, p = 2k(ρ̄) − 3 in niveau 2, after normalising 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1) belongs to AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4 and is not stated here.
hypotheses: (a) is characteristic-free; k algebraically closed
(b)–(d): p odd
(d) uses that ℚ(√p*) is ramified at p and unramified elsewhere; it is stated over ℚ as in the source
proofSteps: (a) ⇐ is clear. ⇒: suppose ρ|_{G_{F′}} irreducible and ρ|_{G_L} reducible. If char k | |ρ(G_L)|, the normal unipotent subgroup O_p(ρ(G_L)) fixes a unique line, which ρ(G_{F′}) stabilises (R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups): contradiction. So ρ(G_L) ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 is diagonalisable. If ψ_1 = ψ_2, ρ(G_L) is scalar, π(ρ(G_{F′})) is cyclic, ρ(G_{F′}) abelian and reducible: contradiction. If ψ_1 ≠ ψ_2, G_F (which normalises G_L) permutes the two eigenlines through G_F/G_L = Gal(L/F) → S_2; every element of Gal(L/F′) is a square in the cyclic group Gal(L/F), so acts trivially, and G_{F′} stabilises both lines: contradiction.

(b) Apply (a) to L = F(ζ_p) and L = F(ζ_{p^m}) (cyclic over F since p is odd: Gal(F(ζ_{p^m})/F) embeds in (ℤ/p^m)^× by mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow_injective, and (ℤ/p^m)^× is cyclic by mathlib:ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow); [F(ζ_{p^m}) : F(ζ_p)] is a power of p, odd, so both have the same subfield F′. This replaces the case analysis of the source proof (Borel / split Cartan normaliser / A_4, S_4), which is also correct.

(c) G_{F′} is normal of index 2 in G_F (F′ ≠ F, since ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is not). Apply R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced (d) to Γ = G_F, Γ′ = G_{F′} and ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p: Γ/Γ′ is cyclic, so ρ̄(G_{F′}) is diagonalisable with two distinct characters χ, χ^σ, G_F swaps the eigenlines and ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p ≅ Ind χ; the projective image is dihedral of order 2n with p ∤ n by part (a) of that node. The image of G_{F′} is diagonalisable, of order prime to p, and has index 2 in ρ̄(G_F); p is odd.

(d) Following the source (after Ribet 1997 Prop. 2.2): the image has no element of order p, so ρ̄|_{I_p} is tame, semisimple, with cyclic projective image. By (c) the projective image is dihedral and π(ρ̄(G_{ℚ(√p*)})) is a cyclic subgroup C of index 2 in it. Every element outside C has order 2 (it swaps the two eigenlines of ρ̄(G_{ℚ(√p*)}), so its square is scalar), hence a cyclic subgroup not contained in C has order 2. If π(ρ̄(I_p)) had order > 2 it would lie in C, so I_p ⊂ G_{ℚ(√p*)} and ℚ(√p*) would be unramified at p, a contradiction (its quadratic character has conductor p, so it is ramified at p, R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters (c)); in fact I_p ⊄ G_{ℚ(√p*)} shows that the order is exactly 2. The niveau computations: ω has order p − 1 and ω_2^{b(1−p)} has order (p + 1)/gcd(p + 1, b).
acceptance: Check both niveau cases on explicit representations: x³ − x − 1 at p = 23 is niveau 1 with ψ_1/ψ_2 of order 2 = ω^{11}; a dihedral representation induced from ℚ(√p*) with niveau-2 inertia ω_2^b ⊕ ω_2^{pb}, (p + 1)/2 | b, illustrates the second case.
Check that the oddness hypothesis is not used: the even representation Ind_{ℚ(√5)}^{ℚ} χ (χ ≠ χ^σ of odd order, p = 5) is irreducible and reducible on both G_{ℚ(√5)} and G_{ℚ(ζ_5)}, as (b) predicts.
Check that at p = 2 the oddness argument of R01.4/odd-irreducible-implies-absolutely-irreducible fails by the F_2-irreducible representation of image order 3 that splits over F_4.

nodes.title: The image of a restriction and linear disjointness
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, ρ : G_F → GL_n(A) continuous with A discrete (finite image), K = F̄^{ker ρ} its kernel field, so that ρ induces an isomorphism Gal(K/F) ≅ ρ(G_F). Let F′/F be a finite separable extension inside F̄. Then: (a) ρ(G_{F′}) is the image of Gal(K/K ∩ F′) ⊂ Gal(K/F) under this isomorphism; (b) if F′ is linearly disjoint from K over F (equivalently K ∩ F′ = F, as K/F is Galois; equivalently [KF′ : F′] = [K : F]), then ρ(G_{F′}) = ρ(G_F); (c) the same holds for the projective image with K replaced by the projective kernel field M = F̄^{ker π∘ρ} ⊂ K, so linear disjointness from M suffices for the projective image; (d) if F′/F is linearly disjoint from K(μ_p) (resp. from M(μ_p)), then ρ(G_{F′(ζ_p)}) = ρ(G_{F(ζ_p)}) (resp. for projective images); (e) if H ⊂ ρ(G_F) is a perfect subgroup and F′/F is a soluble tower (each step Galois with solvable group), then H ⊂ ρ(G_{F′}); (f) absolute irreducibility and the Dickson type of the (projective) image depend only on the image and so pass to ρ|_{G_{F′}} in cases (b)–(d). The condition ‘not bad dihedral’ depends on the pair (ρ(G_F), ρ(G_{F(ζ_p)})) and passes to F′ in case (d), where both images are unchanged; it can be lost in case (b): for p ≥ 5 and ρ̄ = Ind_{G_{ℚ(√d)}}^{G_ℚ} χ with χ of order 3 and image S_3, K unramified at p, ρ̄ is not bad dihedral, F′ = ℚ(√(d p*)) is linearly disjoint from K, and ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is bad dihedral because F′(√p*) = F′(√d).
hypotheses: ρ continuous with discrete coefficients (finite image); for ℓ-adic ρ apply the lemma to each finite quotient
linear disjointness of F′ and K over F means K ⊗_F F′ is a field, equivalently [KF′ : F′] = [K : F] since K/F is Galois
proofSteps: Galois theory for the finite Galois extension K/F: restriction G_{F′} → Gal(K/F) has image Gal(K/K ∩ F′) because K/F is Galois (mathlib:IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup); the image is everything iff K ∩ F′ = F iff [KF′ : F′] = [K : F].

(d) Put N = K(ζ_p), Galois over F. Since N ∩ F′ = F, restriction is an isomorphism Gal(NF′/F′) ≅ Gal(N/F), under which the subgroup fixing F′(ζ_p) = F′·F(ζ_p) corresponds to Gal(N/F(ζ_p)); so ρ(G_{F′(ζ_p)}) = ρ(G_{F(ζ_p)}). No Galois hypothesis on F′/F is needed.

(e) For each Galois step F_i ⊂ F_{i+1} with solvable group, ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}) is normal in ρ(G_{F_i}) with solvable quotient, so H ∩ ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}) is normal in H with solvable quotient; H perfect has no nontrivial solvable quotient (mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable), so H ⊂ ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}).

(f) Absolute irreducibility and the Dickson type are properties of the subgroup ρ(G_{F′}) ⊂ GL_n, equal to ρ(G_F) in (b)–(d). ‘Not bad dihedral’ is absolute irreducibility of ρ(G_{F′(ζ_p)}) (R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion (b)), equal to ρ(G_{F(ζ_p)}) in case (d). In the counterexample, K ∩ F′ = ℚ because the only quadratic subfield of the S_3-field K is ℚ(√d), and √p* ∉ K.
acceptance: Instance: F = ℚ, p odd, ρ̄ = ρ̄_{E,p} surjective onto GL_2(F_p), F′ = ℚ(√d). The only quadratic subfield of ℚ(E[p]) is ℚ(√p*) (GL_2(F_p) has a unique subgroup of index 2), so ℚ(E[p]) ∩ F′ = ℚ unless d is p* times a square, and then the image over F′ is again GL_2(F_p).
Non-example: F′ = ℚ(√p*) ⊂ ℚ(ζ_p) ⊂ ℚ(E[p]) is never linearly disjoint, and ρ̄(G_{F′}) = {g : det g a square} has index 2.

nodes.title: Normal subgroups, quotients and automorphisms of SL_2, PSL_2, PGL_2 over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let k = F_q be a finite field of characteristic p. (a) If q ≥ 4: SL_2(k) is perfect, PSL_2(k) is simple, and every normal subgroup of GL_2(k) either contains SL_2(k) or is central (contained in k^×). The only normal subgroups of SL_2(k) are 1, {±1} ∩ SL_2(k), SL_2(k); hence its only nontrivial quotients are PSL_2(k) and SL_2(k). For q odd the only nontrivial proper normal subgroup of PGL_2(k) is PSL_2(k), of index 2; for q even PGL_2(k) = PSL_2(k) ≅ SL_2(k). Abelianisations: GL_2(k)^{ab} ≅ k^× via det (q ≥ 3), PGL_2(k)^{ab} ≅ k^×/k^{×2}. (b) Small fields: GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 has normal subgroup A_3 ≅ ℤ/3 (not central, not containing SL_2(F_2) = GL_2(F_2)); GL_2(F_3) has normal subgroups 1, {±1}, Q_8, SL_2(F_3), GL_2(F_3); PGL_2(F_3) ≅ S_4, PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4. In particular ‘central or ⊇ SL_2’ fails for q ≤ 3. (c) Automorphisms (Schreier–van der Waerden, Dieudonné): for q ≥ 4, Aut(PSL_2(F_q)) = Aut(PGL_2(F_q)) = PΓL_2(F_q) = PGL_2(F_q) ⋊ Gal(F_q/F_p), acting by conjugation and by the Frobenius on entries; for q = p ≥ 5 every automorphism of PGL_2(F_p) is inner. Consequently every automorphism of PSL_2(F_q) maps the class of an element with eigenvalue ratio α to one with ratio Frob^i(α), so eigenvalues in F_p are preserved up to scalar. (d) Products: if S is non-abelian simple, a subgroup of S^r projecting onto each factor is isomorphic to S^s, s ≤ r, cut out by diagonal identifications through automorphisms (Goursat), and Aut(S^r) = Aut(S)^r ⋊ S_r. (e) For two continuous ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 : G_F → GL_2(k̄) whose projective images are, after conjugation, the standard subgroups PSL_2(F_{q_i}) or PGL_2(F_{q_i}) with q_i ≥ 4 powers of p (i = 1, 2; the fields and the types may differ), the projective kernel fields M_1, M_2 satisfy: M_1 ∩ M_2 = F, or M_1 ∩ M_2 is quadratic over F (possible only if both images are of type PGL_2 with q_i odd), or M_1 = M_2. If M_1 = M_2 then q_1 = q_2 = q, the types agree, and the projective representations are conjugate in PGL_2(k̄) up to an automorphism of the coefficient field F_q (a power of x ↦ x^p).
hypotheses: (c) is the theorem of Schreier–van der Waerden and Dieudonné (La géométrie des groupes classiques, Ch. IV §6; Steinberg for Chevalley groups), quoted with the reduction of step [3]
proofSteps: (a) Perfectness and simplicity are in Mathlib: mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top and mathlib:SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top under the hypothesis ∃ a ≠ 0, a² ≠ 1, and mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple under 4 ≤ Nat.card k. The passage from q ≥ 4 to the first form is a private lemma of Mathlib and is proved again here: at most three elements of a field satisfy a = 0 or a² = 1. For N ⊴ GL_2(k): N ∩ SL_2 maps to a normal subgroup of PSL_2, trivial or all. If all, (N ∩ SL_2)·Z = SL_2 and perfectness gives SL_2 = [SL_2, SL_2] ⊂ N. If trivial, [N, GL_2] ⊂ N ∩ SL_2 ⊂ {±1}; for g ∈ N, h ↦ [g, h] is a homomorphism SL_2 → {±1}, trivial by perfectness, so g centralises SL_2(k), whose k-span is M_2(k), so g is scalar (mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar).

Quotients of SL_2: a normal subgroup not containing SL_2 is central, i.e. inside {±1}. PGL_2(k)/PSL_2(k) ≅ k^×/k^{×2} via det, and PSL_2(k) is perfect (mathlib:SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top), so this quotient is the abelianisation of PGL_2(k); a normal subgroup of PGL_2 meets PSL_2 in 1 or PSL_2; in the first case it centralises PSL_2, hence is trivial.
(b) by direct computation in groups of order 6 and 48.

(c) An automorphism permutes the q + 1 Sylow p-subgroups (unipotent radicals of Borels, R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups), i.e. acts on P¹(F_q), normalising the image of PSL_2(F_q) in Sym(P¹(F_q)); that normaliser is PΓL_2(F_q) (Dieudonné, La géométrie des groupes classiques, Ch. IV §6; Steinberg's theorem on automorphisms of Chevalley groups for the general case, as cited by Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 5.2.3). For q = p, Gal(F_p/F_p) = 1.
(d) Goursat's lemma (mathlib:Subgroup.goursat) and simplicity by induction on r; minimal normal subgroups of S^r are the factors.

(e) Gal(M_1 ∩ M_2/F) is a common quotient of the two projective images G_1, G_2. By (a) the quotients of PSL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4, are 1 and itself, and those of PGL_2(F_q), q odd, are 1, ℤ/2 and itself. If the common quotient is isomorphic to G_1, then M_1 ⊂ M_2 and G_1 is a quotient of G_2 of order ≥ 60, so G_1 ≅ G_2 and M_1 = M_2. Isomorphic groups in this list have the same order, hence the same q (compare the p-parts) and the same type; so for M_1 = M_2 the two projective representations are two isomorphisms of Gal(M_1/F) with the same standard subgroup, and differ by an automorphism of it, which is given by (c).
acceptance: PGL_2(F_5) ≅ S_5 and PSL_2(F_5) ≅ A_5 (simple also by mathlib:alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup, in agreement with (a)): Aut(A_5) = S_5 = PGL_2(F_5), all automorphisms of PGL_2(F_5) inner, consistent with (c) for q = p = 5.
PSL_2(F_9) ≅ A_6: Aut(A_6) has order 1440 = 2·|PGL_2(F_9)| = |PΓL_2(F_9)|, so the Frobenius of F_9 gives automorphisms not induced by PGL_2(F_9); ‘every automorphism is inner’ needs q = p.

The sentence in the proof of Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.8(2), ‘any normal subgroup of GL_2(F_l) either contains SL_2(F_l) or is central’, fails for l = 3 (Q_8 ⊴ GL_2(F_3)) and for l = 2 (A_3 ⊴ GL_2(F_2)), as (b) shows; it holds for l ≥ 5 by (a). The lemma's conclusion survives for l = 3 and fails for l = 2 (source issue of this packet on that lemma).

nodes.title: Residual images under restriction to cyclotomic fields
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime, k a finite field of characteristic p and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous; write G = ρ̄(G_F), H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) ⊴ G with G/H a quotient of Gal(F(ζ_p)/F), which embeds in (ℤ/p)^× (mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow_injective) and is therefore cyclic. (a) [cyclic restriction] For p odd and m ≥ 1, ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^m})}} is absolutely irreducible iff ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is iff ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is (R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion). (b) [Caraiani–Newton Lemma 7.1.1(1)] If ρ̄ is irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is absolutely reducible, then G lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup of GL_2(k) (in the Cartan itself if ρ̄ is not absolutely irreducible). (c) [CN 7.1.1(2),(3)] If moreover k = F_p and det ρ̄ = χ̄_p: for p = 3, G is conjugate to C_s^+(3) or to a subgroup of C_ns(3); for p = 5 and [F(ζ_5) : F] = 4, G is conjugate to a subgroup of C_ns^+(5). (d) [big-image bookkeeping, BCGNT] If p ≥ 5, SL_2(F_p) ⊂ G ⊂ GL_2(F_p) and det ρ̄ is trivial on G_{F(ζ_p)} (for instance det ρ̄ = χ̄_p^{−m}), then H = SL_2(F_p). More generally if G ⊃ SL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4, then H ⊃ SL_2(F_q), and π(H) is conjugate to PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) for a finite field F_0 ⊃ F_q by R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (c). (e) [Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.6(1), which reduces to m = 1; the source assumes l > 2m + 3, the case m = 1 needs only p ≥ 5] If p > 3, F′/F is finite, ρ̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_p) for the normal closure F̃ of F, F′ is linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker ρ̄} over F and p is unramified in F′/ℚ, then ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad ρ̄}·F′: the projective image PSL_2(k_0) or PGL_2(k_0) has no cyclic quotient of order p − 1 > 2 while Gal(F′(ζ_p)/F′) ≅ (ℤ/p)^×. (f) [Caraiani–Newton Lemma 6.1.4] If ζ_5 ∉ F and the projective image of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) is conjugate to PSL_2(F_5), with ρ̄(G_F) ⊂ GL_2(F_5) and det ρ̄ = χ̄_5, then the field cut out by the projective image of ρ̄(G_F) does not contain ζ_5. (g) [Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.8(2), group part] If l ≥ 3 and Δ ⊴ GL_2(F_l) has det(Δ) = F_l^×, then Δ = GL_2(F_l). (h) For p > 2 and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible: no nonzero X ∈ M_2(k) with Tr X = 0 satisfies ρ̄(σ)Xρ̄(σ)⁻¹ = X for all σ ∈ G_F, and none satisfies ρ̄(σ)Xρ̄(σ)⁻¹ = χ̄_p(σ)⁻¹X for all σ, nor ρ̄(σ)Xρ̄(σ)⁻¹ = χ̄_p(σ)X for all σ (the invariants H⁰(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄) and H⁰(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) vanish once G7/adjoint-representations identifies ad⁰ρ̄ with this module).
hypotheses: p prime; in (a), (h) p odd; in (d), (e) p ≥ 5 (perfectness of SL_2(F_p))

(e) requires p unramified in F′: then the cyclotomic polynomial Φ_p is irreducible over F′ (tauceti:IsCyclotomicExtension.irreducible_cyclotomic_of_unramified), so Gal(F′(ζ_p)/F′) ≅ (ℤ/p)^× by mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow and [F′(ζ_p) : F′] = p − 1

(g) needs l ≥ 3: for l = 2, A_3 ⊴ GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 has det(A_3) = F_2^× = {1} but A_3 ≠ GL_2(F_2); Allen et al. print Lemma 7.1.8(2) without l > 2, and it is false for l = 2 (source issue of this packet)
proofSteps: (a) is R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion (b).

(b) H is absolutely reducible and normal in G; by R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced (d) and R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups, H is diagonalisable over k̄ with eigenlines {D_1, D_2}, a Frobenius-stable pair; G permutes it, so G lies in the normaliser of the split (D_i rational) or non-split (D_i conjugate over F_{q²}) Cartan attached to it; if H is scalar, π(G) is cyclic, G abelian, contained in a Cartan. CN prove (1) with [FLHS15, Lemma 2.2].

(c) A finite verification. Under the hypotheses G is an irreducible subgroup of GL_2(F_p) with G ∩ SL_2(F_p) = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) absolutely reducible and det(G) of order [F(ζ_p) : F]. Among the 55 subgroups of GL_2(F_3) those with these properties are the normalisers of the split Cartans (dihedral of order 8) and subgroups of non-split Cartans; among the 466 subgroups of GL_2(F_5) those with det(G) = F_5^× lie in the normaliser of a non-split Cartan. CN argue through [FLHS15, Lemma 2.2 and Prop. 4.1(b)] (Freitas–Le Hung–Siksek), which is not needed.
(d) det is trivial on G_{F(ζ_p)} so H ⊂ SL_2(F_p) ∩ G; G/H is abelian, so H ⊃ [G, G] ⊃ [SL_2(F_p), SL_2(F_p)] = SL_2(F_p) by mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top.

(e) As in Allen et al.: reduce to m = 1; by R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield the projective image over F′ equals that over F, which is PSL_2(k_0) or PGL_2(k_0) (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (c)) with abelianisation of order ≤ 2 (R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2); since p is unramified in F′, Φ_p is irreducible over F′ (tauceti:IsCyclotomicExtension.irreducible_cyclotomic_of_unramified) and Gal(F′(ζ_p)/F′) ≅ (ℤ/p)^× (mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow); if ζ_p were in the compositum, this cyclic group of order p − 1 > 2 would be a quotient of the projective image.
(f) CN: ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) ⊂ SL_2(F_5) surjects onto PSL_2(F_5), so equals SL_2(F_5); compare [G : H] with [F(ζ_5) : F] according as det ρ̄ has order 2 or 4.

(g) By R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2 (a) for l ≥ 5, Δ is central (det(Δ) ⊂ squares, not all of F_l^×) or contains SL_2(F_l); for l = 3 every proper normal subgroup of GL_2(F_3) lies in SL_2(F_3) (list (b)).

(h) An X of the first kind commutes with the absolutely irreducible ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}), so is scalar by Schur (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible, End = k), hence 0 as Tr X = 2x and p ≠ 2; an X of the second kind is invariant under G_{F(ζ_p)} (χ̄_p trivial there), hence scalar, and Tr X = 0 forces X = 0.
acceptance: Instance: for E/ℚ with surjective mod-p image, p ≥ 5, the image of G_{ℚ(ζ_p)} on E[p] is SL_2(F_p) by (d).
Instance (CN): for p = 5 and [F(ζ_5) : F] = 4, an irreducible ρ̄ with cyclotomically reducible restriction has image in C_ns^+(5).
Non-example for (g) at l = 3 in the source's form: Q_8 ⊴ GL_2(F_3) is neither central nor ⊇ SL_2(F_3).

nodes.title: Large residual image: persistence under small index and soluble base change, and a tame-inertia criterion
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and G ⊂ GL_2(F̄_p) a finite subgroup containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a}) with p^a ≥ 5. (a) [Newton–Thorne Lemma 2.3(3), group part] If a ≥ 2, every subgroup H ⊂ G of index [G : H] < 2p contains gSL_2(F_{p^a})g⁻¹, the same conjugate that G contains. The bound a ≥ 2 is needed (Newton–Thorne assume a ≥ a_0(p) ≥ 3): for a = 1 the Borel subgroup of SL_2(F_p) has index p + 1 < 2p. (b) [perfect subgroups] If H ⊂ ρ̄(G_F) is perfect (e.g. a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a}), p^a ≥ 4), it remains in the image after restriction to any soluble tower F′/F (R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield (e)); in particular ‘ρ̄(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a})’ survives soluble base change. (c) [tame-inertia criterion, after Boxer–Calegari–Gee Theorem 3.1] Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_p) be continuous, unramified outside p, with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{I_p} ≅ ω_2^{a} ⊕ ω_2^{pa} for an integer a with gcd(a, p + 1) = 1. Then ρ̄(G_ℚ) contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_p). Statements that need automorphic input (Newton–Thorne Proposition 5.4 and Theorem 5.9, large image from tamely dihedral local components) are not stated here; their group-theoretic step is R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (e).
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 in (a), (c)
(c) uses fundamental characters ω_2 of niveau 2 (R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters)
proofSteps: (a) Put S = gSL_2(F_{p^a})g⁻¹ ⊂ G and q = p^a. Then [S : H ∩ S] ≤ [G : H] < 2p. By R01.4/minimal-index-of-proper-subgroups-of-psl2 (Galois's theorem, Dickson §262) a proper subgroup of SL_2(F_q) has index ≥ q + 1 unless q ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11}. For a ≥ 2, q ≥ 25 and q + 1 > 2p, so H ∩ S = S. Newton–Thorne quote Lemma 2.3 from Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3; the adequacy parts (1)–(2) belong to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7.
(b) Group.IsPerfect has no nontrivial solvable quotient; apply R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield (e).

(c) The projective image of I_p is generated by ω_2^{a(1−p)}, of order (p + 1)/gcd(p + 1, a) = p + 1 > 5, so π(ρ̄(G_ℚ)) is not A_4, S_4, A_5 (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (e)); it is not in a Borel since ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is absolutely irreducible. If it were dihedral, ρ̄ would be induced from the quadratic field cut out by the rotation subgroup (R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced), unramified outside p, hence ℚ(√p*) (by R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters (c), (d) the quadratic character of such a field is the Galois character of a primitive Dirichlet character of order 2 whose conductor is a power of p; there is exactly one such character, of conductor p, because (ℤ/p^m)^× is cyclic, mathlib:ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow; and ℚ(√p*) ⊂ ℚ(ζ_p) is such a field); then ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is induced from ℚ_p(√p*) and hence ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} ⊗ η with η the quadratic character of ℚ_p(√p*)/ℚ_p, η|_{I_p} = ω^{(p−1)/2} = ω_2^{(p²−1)/2}. Comparing {ω_2^{a}, ω_2^{pa}} with {ω_2^{a+(p²−1)/2}, ω_2^{pa+(p²−1)/2}}: the first cannot match itself (ω_2 has order p² − 1), so ω_2^{a+(p²−1)/2} = ω_2^{pa}, i.e. (p − 1)a ≡ (p² − 1)/2 mod p² − 1, i.e. a ≡ (p + 1)/2 mod p + 1, and then gcd(a, p + 1) = (p + 1)/2 > 1, a contradiction (Boxer–Calegari–Gee print ρ̄_f|_{I_p} ≃ ω_2^{k−1} ⊕ ω_2^{p(k−1)} and conclude k ≡ (p + 3)/2 mod p + 1; a = k − 1 and a = 1 − k give the same congruence, since (p + 1)/2 ≡ −(p + 1)/2 mod p + 1, so the sign of the exponents does not matter here). The remaining case PSL_2/PGL_2(F_{p^s}) gives SL_2(F_{p^s}) ⊂ ρ̄(G_ℚ) by (c) of the Dickson node.
acceptance: Instance of (c) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee, Corollary 3.2): a level-one eigenform f of weight k = 38 that is non-ordinary at p = 79 has ρ̄_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} irreducible with ρ̄_f|_{I_p} ≅ ω_2^{a} ⊕ ω_2^{pa}, a = ±37, and gcd(37, 80) = 1; so ρ̄_f(G_ℚ) contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_79) (the modular-form input is not planned here). The weight-26 form ΔE_4²E_6 at p = 107 is not an instance of (c): a_107 = 35830422465487817813321292 ≡ −1 mod 107, so the form is ordinary at 107; its image is GL_2(F_107) by Swinnerton-Dyer's theorem, as Boxer–Calegari–Gee, Theorem 2.4, quote.
Sharpness for a = 1: in SL_2(F_5) ≅ 2.A_5 the subgroup SL_2(F_3) ≅ 2.A_4 has index 5 < 10 and the Borel has index 6 < 10; neither contains SL_2(F_5).

nodes.title: Galois's theorem: proper subgroups of PSL_2(F_q) have index at least q + 1 for q ≠ 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11
nodes.statement: Let q be a prime power. PSL_2(F_q) has a subgroup of index q + 1, the stabiliser of a point of P¹(F_q). If q ∉ {2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11}, every proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_q) has index ≥ q + 1; if moreover q ≥ 4, every proper subgroup of SL_2(F_q) has index ≥ q + 1. For q = 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 the least index of a proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_q) is 2, 3, 5, 7, 6, 11.
hypotheses: q = p^n any prime power; the exceptional values are exactly 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11
the statement for SL_2 needs q ≥ 4 (perfectness)
proofSteps: Dickson §262 (printed p. 286). By the classification (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (a); Dickson's summary §260 for PSL_2(F_s), s = q) every proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_s) lies in one of: the stabiliser of a point of P¹(F_s), of order s(s − 1)/(2;1); a dihedral group of order at most 2(s + 1)/(2;1) (its rotations lie in the image of a Cartan subgroup, of order (s ∓ 1)/(2;1), R01.4/cartan-subgroups-and-normalisers); PSL_2(F_{p^k}) or PGL_2(F_{p^k}) with k ≤ n/2; a group of order 12, 24 or 60. A subgroup fixing a point of P¹(k̄) that is not F_s-rational fixes its Frobenius conjugate too, so it lies in the image of a non-split Cartan subgroup or is trivial.

Orders (Dickson, loc. cit.): p^k(p^{2k} − 1) ≤ p^k(p^n − 1) < s(s − 1)/(2;1) for k ≤ n/2 and s ≥ 4; 2(s + 1)/(2;1) < s(s − 1)/(2;1) for s ≥ 4; 60 < s(s − 1)/(2;1) for s > 11; for s = 8 no group of order 12, 24 or 60 occurs, and for s = 4 the groups of order 12 are the point stabilisers and the group of order 60 is everything. So for s ∉ {2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11} a proper subgroup has order at most s(s − 1)/(2;1), that is, index at least s + 1.

Exceptional values: PSL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 and PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4 have subgroups of index 2 and 3; A_4 ⊂ PSL_2(F_5) has index 5, S_4 ⊂ PSL_2(F_7) index 7, A_5 ⊂ PSL_2(F_9) index 6 and A_5 ⊂ PSL_2(F_11) index 11.

SL_2: a proper subgroup K of SL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4, has proper image in PSL_2(F_q); otherwise K·{±1} = SL_2(F_q), K is normal with abelian quotient and K ⊃ [SL_2(F_q), SL_2(F_q)] = SL_2(F_q) (mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top). So its index is at least that of its image.
acceptance: Least index of a proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_q), found by listing all subgroups: q = 4: 5; q = 5: 5; q = 7: 7; q = 8: 9; q = 9: 6; q = 11: 11.

q = 25: |PSL_2(F_25)| = 7800; the point stabiliser has index 26, PGL_2(F_5) has index 65, the dihedral groups of order 24 and 26 and A_5 have larger index; the bound 26 is attained only by point stabilisers.
Use in R01.4/large-image-persistence (a): for p ≥ 5 and a ≥ 2 a subgroup of SL_2(F_{p^a}) of index < 2p is everything, since p^a + 1 > 2p.

nodes.title: Characteristic two: non-solvable residual images and the module M_2(F)
nodes.statement: Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2, F_0 ⊂ F a subfield with |F_0| = 2^r, r ≥ 2, and G_0 = SL_2(F_0) ≅ PGL_2(F_0) acting on Ad := M_2(F) by conjugation (through SL_2(F_0) ⊂ GL_2(F)); Z := F·1 ⊂ Ad^0 := {X : Tr X = 0} ⊂ Ad (Z ⊂ Ad^0 since Tr 1 = 2 = 0). Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL_2(F) be continuous and absolutely irreducible with non-solvable image, K a number field. (a) [projective image] π(ρ̄(G_K)) is conjugate to PGL_2(F_0) = PSL_2(F_0) ≅ SL_2(F_0) for some F_0 ⊂ F with |F_0| ≥ 4 (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (d)). (b) [Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 4.3(2)(ii)] H⁰(G_0, Ad) = H⁰(G_0, Ad^0) = Z is one-dimensional, and H⁰(G_0, Ad/Z) = H⁰(G_0, (Ad^0)^*) = 0, where (Ad^0)^* ≅ Ad/Z through the trace pairing. (c) [KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(i), Dickinson Lemma 42] H¹(SL_2(F_0), M_2(F)) = 0. (d) [KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(ii)] The only G_0-submodules of Ad are 0, Z, Ad^0, Ad; the only nonzero irreducible submodule is Z. (e) Every one-dimensional F[G_0]-module is trivial (G_0 perfect), and Ad^0/Z is the Frobenius-twisted natural representation, irreducible of dimension 2.
hypotheses: characteristic 2 and |F_0| ≥ 4. For F_0 = F_2, SL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 is solvable and (b), (d) fail: H⁰(S_3, Ad/Z) is one-dimensional (spanned by the class of an element s of order 3, since g s g⁻¹ − s ∈ {0, 1}), and F·1 ⊕ F·s and a complement of Z in Ad^0 are two-dimensional submodules. Statement (c) and the conclusions of (e) still hold for F_0 = F_2 (the natural module of S_3 is projective in characteristic 2, so M_2(F) is; the only character S_3 → F^× is trivial because F^× has odd order)

(c) is the statement of Dickinson, Duke Math. J. 109 (2001), Lemma 42, as quoted in Khare–Wintenberger II, Lemma 4.3(5)(i), and rests on that reference for general r ≥ 2; the computation of proof step [1] confirms it for |F_0| = 4, 8, 16

H⁰ and H¹ are Mathlib's groupCohomology of the finite group G_0 = SL_2(F_0) with coefficients in the F-linear representations of G_0 on Ad = M_2(F), Ad^0, Z and their quotients (objects of Rep F G_0); no continuous or profinite cohomology is involved
proofSteps: (b) As in KW II: an element of Ad^G0 commutes with [[1, 1], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [1, 1]], so is scalar (a matrix commuting with the first is a + b·E_12, and commuting with the second forces b = 0; this is H⁰(G_0, Ad) through mathlib:groupCohomology.H0Iso); Ad^0 ∋ 1. For Ad/Z: if l ∈ Ad maps to a nonzero invariant of Ad/Z, take g ∈ G_0 semisimple non-scalar with eigenlines D_1, D_2; Ad(g) acts unipotently on the plane P = ⟨1, l⟩ and 1 is not an eigenvalue on Ad/P, so P is the diagonal subalgebra for D_1 ⊕ D_2; P is G_0-stable, so G_0 stabilises {D_1, D_2} and would be solvable, a contradiction. The trace pairing identifies (Ad^0)^* with Ad/Z.

(c) Dickinson Lemma 42, quoted by KW II; equivalently Ext¹_{F[SL_2(F_0)]}(V, V) = 0 for the natural module V = F², since H¹(G, Hom(V, V)) = Ext¹(V, V). The composition factors of Ad are Z ≅ F, Ad^0/Z ≅ V^{(2)} (torus weights λ^{±2}) and Ad/Ad^0 ≅ F (trace), and H¹(SL_2(F_0), F) = 0 (perfect); the vanishing of H¹(G_0, Ad) is not a formal consequence of these factors (H¹(G_0, V^{(2)}) need not vanish) and is Dickinson's computation. It suffices to treat F = F_0, since H¹(G_0, M_2(F_0) ⊗_{F_0} F) = H¹(G_0, M_2(F_0)) ⊗_{F_0} F. For |F_0| = 4, 8, 16 a direct computation of cocycles on generators gives dim Z¹(G_0, M_2(F_0)) = 3 = dim B¹(G_0, M_2(F_0)) (B¹ ≅ Ad/H⁰(G_0, Ad) has dimension 4 − 1 = 3), so H¹ = 0.

(d) KW II: 1-dimensional submodules are trivial, hence inside H⁰ = Z; a 2-dimensional submodule of Ad^0 would give a trivial quotient Ad^0 → F, a nonzero element of H⁰((Ad^0)^*), contradicting (b); a 2-dimensional V ⊂ Ad meets Ad^0 in Z, and V/Z ⊂ Ad/Z would be a trivial line, contradicting H⁰(Ad/Z) = 0; a 3-dimensional V ≠ Ad^0 meets Ad^0 in dimension ≥ 2, so contains Ad^0 and equals it.
(e) mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top (|F_0| ≥ 4 provides a with a ≠ 0, a² ≠ 1).
acceptance: Instance: F_0 = F = F_4, G_0 = SL_2(F_4) ≅ A_5 acting on M_2(F_4): Z ⊂ Ad^0 ⊂ Ad with Ad^0/Z ≅ V^{(2)} of dimension 2, irreducible.

Degenerate case F_0 = F_2: SL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 is solvable with abelianisation ℤ/2, so (a) has no content and H¹(S_3, Z) = Hom(S_3, F) ≠ 0; H⁰(S_3, Ad/Z) ≠ 0 and Ad has two invariant planes, so (b) and (d) fail. H¹(S_3, M_2(F)) = 0 still holds. So r ≥ 2 is necessary for (a), (b), (d) and for H¹(G_0, Z) = 0, not for (c).
Odd p contrast: for p odd, Ad = Z ⊕ Ad^0 and H¹(SL_2(F_p), ad^0) is owned by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients).

nodes.title: Frobenius density in a finite quotient
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, G_K its absolute Galois group with the Krull topology, and Σ a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. Frobenius means arithmetic Frobenius, with all places above v allowed. For U open normal in G_K and g∈G_K, the v∈Σ unramified in L=K̄^U for which some w|v has every Frobenius lift in gU have Dirichlet density #C/[G_K:U]>0, where C is the conjugacy class of gU.
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, G_K its absolute Galois group with the Krull topology, and Σ a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. Frobenius means arithmetic Frobenius, with all places above v allowed.
proofSteps: Reduce (a) to a finite quotient: a basic open set of G_K is a coset gU with U open normal; L = K̄^U is finite Galois over K (Krull topology) and only finitely many v ramify in L (tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet: only finitely many primes lie in no Artin fibre, and every member of a fibre is unramified in L).

Apply the Chebotarev density theorem of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev layer 10 (hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet) to L/K and the class C of g|_L: frobeniusPrimeSet K L C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K) > 0.

Intersect with Σ: frobeniusPrimeSet K L C is the disjoint union of Σ ∩ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C and a subset of the complement of Σ. The complement of Σ has Dirichlet density 0 (complements), hence so has each of its subsets (the ratio is squeezed between 0 and that of the complement), and by finite additivity on disjoint unions Σ ∩ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K) > 0 (density calculus of ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7.3). In particular it is nonempty and infinite, because a finite set has density 0.

For v in the intersection, tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt gives a prime Q of 𝓞 L above v with g|_L an arithmetic Frobenius at Q (mathlib:IsArithFrobAt). Choose a place w of K̄ above Q (a maximal ideal of 𝓞 K̄ contracting to Q; lying over for the integral extension 𝓞 K̄/𝓞 L). For every arithmetic Frobenius lift σ at w, the restriction σ|_L is an arithmetic Frobenius at w ∩ 𝓞 L = Q (tauceti:IsArithFrobAt.restrictNormal for K ⊂ L ⊂ K̄ with L/K normal; the declaration has no finiteness hypothesis on the top field), and v is unramified in L, so σ|_L = g|_L by uniqueness of the Frobenius at an unramified prime (tauceti:NumberField.isArithFrobAt_eq_of_isUnramifiedAt); hence σ ∈ gU. Conversely, let v ∈ Σ be unramified in L and w | v a place all of whose Frobenius lifts lie in gU. A Frobenius lift σ at w exists (R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place), σ|_L = g|_L is an arithmetic Frobenius at w ∩ 𝓞 L, and the same membership lemma gives v ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C. So the set of the statement is equal to Σ ∩ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C, whose density is #C/#Gal(L/K) by step 3.
acceptance: For U=G_K the density is one.

nodes.title: Density of Frobenius images
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, G_K its absolute Galois group with the Krull topology, and Σ a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. Frobenius means arithmetic Frobenius, with all places above v allowed. If φ:G_K→H is a continuous homomorphism into a Hausdorff group and φ(I_w)=1 above every v∈Σ, the well-defined φ(Frob_w) are dense in the compact subgroup φ(G_K). Two continuous maps from φ(G_K) to a Hausdorff space that agree on these images agree everywhere.
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, G_K its absolute Galois group with the Krull topology, and Σ a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one. Frobenius means arithmetic Frobenius, with all places above v allowed.
proofSteps: Two Frobenius lifts at w differ by I_w, which φ kills. Thus φ(Frob_w) is well defined. If an open subset of H meets φ(G_K), its inverse image is nonempty and open in G_K; R01.5/frobenius-density supplies a Σ-Frobenius lift there. These images are dense in φ(G_K).
The image is compact, hence closed in H. The equaliser of two maps to a Hausdorff space is closed, so agreement on the dense images implies agreement on the image.
acceptance: Closedness of the equaliser uses the Hausdorff target; no finite ramification set is required.

nodes.title: Every element of a finite image is a Frobenius at a set of primes of positive density
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, H a finite group with the discrete topology and φ : G_K → H a continuous homomorphism (for instance ρ : G_K → GL_n(k) continuous with k finite, or with finite image in GL_n(ℂ), R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients). Let S be the finite set of finite places at which φ is ramified and T any finite set of finite places. Then for every h ∈ φ(G_K) the set of v ∉ S ∪ T such that h = φ(Frob_w) for some place w | v has Dirichlet density #(conjugacy class of h in φ(G_K))/#φ(G_K) > 0, and in particular is infinite.
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, φ:G_K→H a continuous map to a finite discrete group, S its finite ramification set, and T any finite set of places.
proofSteps: φ factors through Gal(L/K) ≅ φ(G_K) with L = K̄^{ker φ} finite Galois (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); v is unramified in L iff φ is unramified at v (R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set).

Apply hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet (Chebotarev layer 10) to the class C of the element of Gal(L/K) corresponding to h; removing the finite set S ∪ T does not change the density (hasDirichletDensity_of_symmDiff_finite, ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7).

This is R01.5/frobenius-density-finite-level for U = ker φ and Σ the complement of T: for v in the set, tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt gives a prime Q of L above v at which the chosen representative g|_L is an arithmetic Frobenius; for a place w of K̄ above Q every arithmetic Frobenius lift at w restricts on L to the unique Frobenius at the unramified prime Q, so it lies in gU and h = φ(Frob_w). Conversely, if h = φ(Frob_w) with w | v and v ∉ S ∪ T, the restriction of Frob_w to L is an arithmetic Frobenius at w ∩ O_L, so v lies in frobeniusPrimeSet K L C; the two sets are equal.
acceptance: The density for the identity is 1/#φ(G_K).

nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, φ:G_K→H a continuous map to a finite discrete group, S its finite ramification set, and T any finite set of places. Any property holding at φ(Frob_w) for every w above every v outside a finite exceptional set holds on every element of φ(G_K).
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, φ:G_K→H a continuous map to a finite discrete group, S its finite ramification set, and T any finite set of places.
proofSteps: The consequence: the identity holds at h because h is φ(Frob_w) for some v outside the given finite exceptional set.
acceptance: The property need not be conjugation invariant, because all w over each v are allowed.

nodes.title: Sign vectors of multiquadratic automorphisms
nodes.statement: Let d₁,…,dᵣ be nonzero integers and εᵢ∈{±1}, and put M=Q(√d₁,…,√dᵣ). An automorphism σ of M/Q with σ(√dᵢ)=εᵢ√dᵢ exists iff every square subproduct ∏_{i∈J}dᵢ has ∏_{i∈J}εᵢ=1. The degree [M:Q] equals the order of the subgroup of Qˣ/Qˣ² generated by the dᵢ.
hypotheses: Let d₁,…,dᵣ be nonzero integers and εᵢ∈{±1}, and put M=Q(√d₁,…,√dᵣ).
proofSteps: Let M = ℚ(√d_1, …, √d_r) ⊂ ℚ̄ and let Δ be the subgroup of ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} generated by the d_i. Choose a subfamily (d_i)_{i∈B} whose classes form an F_2-basis of Δ; no nonempty subproduct of it is a square, and it generates M. For such a family tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquiv (stated over any field in which 2 ≠ 0) is an isomorphism of Gal(M/ℚ) onto the group of sign vectors (ℤ/2)^B, tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquiv_symm_apply_gen says that the sign vector ε is realised by the automorphism multiplying √d_i by (−1)^{ε_i}, and tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_aut_adjoin_range gives #Gal(M/ℚ) = 2^{#B} = #Δ. For j ∉ B write d_j = c²·∏_{i∈B_j} d_i with c ∈ ℚ^×; then √d_j = ±c·∏_{i∈B_j} √d_i, so σ(√d_j)/√d_j = ∏_{i∈B_j} σ(√d_i)/√d_i for σ ∈ Gal(M/ℚ). Hence σ ↦ (d ↦ σ(√d)/√d) identifies Gal(M/ℚ) with the group of characters Δ → {±1}.
acceptance: For d₁=d₂ the two signs must agree.

nodes.title: Primes with prescribed quadratic residue symbols, possibly coincident quadratic fields
nodes.statement: Let d₁,…,dᵣ be nonzero integers and εᵢ∈{±1}, and put M=Q(√d₁,…,√dᵣ). Let d_1, …, d_r be nonzero integers and ε_1, …, ε_r ∈ {±1}. The following are equivalent: (i) there are infinitely many odd primes p ∤ d_1⋯d_r with legendreSym p d_i = ε_i for all i; (ii) the set of such primes has Dirichlet density 2^{-m} > 0, where 2^m = [ℚ(√d_1, …, √d_r) : ℚ]; (iii) for every subset J ⊆ {1, …, r} with ∏_{i∈J} d_i a square in ℚ, ∏_{i∈J} ε_i = 1. In particular, for two non-squares d_1, d_2 (the fields ℚ(√d_1), ℚ(√d_2) may coincide, i.e. d_1d_2 may be a square) there are infinitely many primes at which both are quadratic nonresidues; for three non-squares with d_1d_2d_3 a square there are none.
hypotheses: Let d₁,…,dᵣ be nonzero integers and εᵢ∈{±1}, and put M=Q(√d₁,…,√dᵣ).
proofSteps: For an odd prime p ∤ ∏ d_i and a prime Q of O_M above p, every arithmetic Frobenius σ at Q satisfies σ(√d_i) = legendreSym p d_i · √d_i (tauceti:NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt), and one exists (tauceti:NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic).

Hence, for p odd, p ∤ ∏ d_i and p unramified in M (all but finitely many primes), p has the prescribed symbols iff the element ε ∈ Gal(M/ℚ) with ε(√d_i) = ε_i√d_i exists and p ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet ℚ M {ε} (tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt). By step 1, ε exists iff d_i ↦ ε_i extends to a character of Δ, i.e. iff (iii) holds. If one prime p has the prescribed symbols then (iii) holds, by multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol: this gives (i) ⇒ (iii) and shows the set is empty when (iii) fails.

If ε exists, Chebotarev layer 10 (Gal(M/ℚ) abelian, so the class is a singleton) gives Dirichlet density 1/#Gal(M/ℚ) = 2^{-m} for frobeniusPrimeSet ℚ M {ε}, hence for the set of the statement, which differs from it by a finite set (hasDirichletDensity_of_symmDiff_finite); R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius packages this. A set of positive density is infinite: (iii) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (i).
acceptance: Three nonsquares with square product cannot all have symbol −1 at one prime.

nodes.title: Recognition on a dense subset
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E₁,E₂ topological fields with continuous embeddings into a common Hausdorff topological field E, and ρᵢ continuous n-dimensional representations. Write Wᵢ=Vᵢ⊗_{Eᵢ}E. If their characteristic polynomials agree in E[X] on a dense subset D⊂Γ, then W₁ˢˢ≅W₂ˢˢ. If both Wᵢ are semisimple, W₁≅W₂.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E₁,E₂ topological fields with continuous embeddings into a common Hausdorff topological field E, and ρᵢ continuous n-dimensional representations. Write Wᵢ=Vᵢ⊗_{Eᵢ}E.
proofSteps: Base change is R01.1/coefficient-extension. The polynomial-coefficient functions on Γ are continuous; their equaliser is closed because E is Hausdorff, hence all of Γ. Semisimplification preserves characteristic polynomials; apply R01.1/brauer-nesbitt over E.
acceptance: A discontinuous embedding of Q_ℓ into Q̄_ℓ can fix every rational Frobenius value of χ_ℓ while changing the character.

nodes.title: Recognition by Frobenius polynomials
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, E₁,E₂ topological fields with continuous embeddings into a common Hausdorff topological field E, and ρᵢ continuous n-dimensional representations. Write Wᵢ=Vᵢ⊗_{Eᵢ}E. For Γ=G_K, K a number field, if both representations are unramified on a density-one set Σ and their Frobenius polynomials agree there, then W₁ˢˢ≅W₂ˢˢ. No finiteness of either ramification set is assumed.
hypotheses: Let Γ be profinite, E₁,E₂ topological fields with continuous embeddings into a common Hausdorff topological field E, and ρᵢ continuous n-dimensional representations. Write Wᵢ=Vᵢ⊗_{Eᵢ}E.
proofSteps: The functions γ ↦ det(X − ρ_i(γ)) ∈ E[X]_{≤n}, i = 1, 2, are continuous and class functions on G_K and factor through G_K → GL_n(E_1) × GL_n(E_2) (ρ_1, ρ_2), which is trivial on the inertia groups at all places above Σ; the two maps to E[X]_{≤n} ≅ E^{n+1} are continuous because the embeddings E_i → E are continuous, and they agree at every Frobenius element at a place above Σ.

R01.5/frobenius-density-image applied to φ = (ρ_1, ρ_2) : G_K → GL_n(E_1) × GL_n(E_2) and Σ: the images of the Frobenius elements at places above Σ are dense in φ(G_K), and the set where the two characteristic polynomials agree is closed because E[X]_{≤n} is Hausdorff; so they agree on all of G_K.
Apply R01.5/recognition-on-a-dense-subset to the dense images of (ρ₁,ρ₂), supplied by R01.5/frobenius-density-image.
acceptance: Equality compares coefficients through the continuous embeddings into E.

nodes.title: Rank-two trace and determinant identities
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, Γ a group, and ρ:Γ→GL₂(A). Put T=tr∘ρ and δ=det∘ρ. Then δ:Γ→Aˣ is a homomorphism, T(1)=2, T(gh)=T(hg), and δ(g)T(g⁻¹h)−T(g)T(h)+T(gh)=0 for all g,h.
hypotheses: Let A be a commutative ring, Γ a group, and ρ:Γ→GL₂(A). Put T=tr∘ρ and δ=det∘ρ.
proofSteps: (1): δ is multiplicative, T(1) = tr(1) = 2 and T(gh) = T(hg) (mathlib:Matrix.trace_mul_comm). Cayley–Hamilton for the 2 × 2 matrix ρ(g) (mathlib:Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly with mathlib:Matrix.charpoly_fin_two: the characteristic polynomial is X² − tr·X + det) gives ρ(g)² − T(g)ρ(g) + δ(g) = 0; multiplying by ρ(g)^{-1}ρ(h) gives ρ(gh) − T(g)ρ(h) + δ(g)ρ(g^{-1}h) = 0, and taking the trace gives the identity.
acceptance: The identities hold over F₂ without division by two.

nodes.title: Rank-two determinants and trace data
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, Γ a group, and ρ:Γ→GL₂(A). Put T=tr∘ρ and δ=det∘ρ. Under IHG.0/determinant-dimension-two, (T,δ) corresponds to the law det∘ρ. For two rank-two representations, equality of all characteristic polynomials, equality of T and δ, and equality of the determinant laws on A[Γ] are equivalent.
hypotheses: Let A be a commutative ring, Γ a group, and ρ:Γ→GL₂(A). Put T=tr∘ρ and δ=det∘ρ.
proofSteps: (2): by IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation, D = det ∘ ρ is a 2-dimensional determinant with Tr = tr ∘ ρ, D|_Γ = det ∘ ρ and χ(g, t) = charpoly ρ(g); the bijection of IHG.0/determinant-dimension-two sends D to (Tr|_Γ, D|_Γ) = (T, δ).
(3): (i) ⇔ (ii) because det(X − ρ(g)) = X² − T(g)X + δ(g); (ii) ⇔ (iii) by step 2 and the injectivity of D ↦ (T, D|_Γ) in IHG.0/determinant-dimension-two.
acceptance: Equality on group elements alone is converted to equality of polynomial laws by the two-dimensional bijection.

nodes.title: Rank-two recognition in every characteristic
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, Γ a group, and ρ:Γ→GL₂(A). Put T=tr∘ρ and δ=det∘ρ. nodes.title: The image algebra, field of definition and Brauer class of an absolutely irreducible representation
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with algebraic closure k̄, Γ a group and ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄) an absolutely irreducible representation (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible). (1) The field of traces k(ρ) := k(tr ρ(γ) : γ ∈ Γ) ⊂ k̄. (2) The image algebra B(ρ) := the k(ρ)-linear span of ρ(Γ) in M_n(k̄); it is a k(ρ)-subalgebra, central simple over k(ρ) of dimension n², and the inclusion induces B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ ≅ M_n(k̄). (3) The Brauer class β(ρ) := [B(ρ)] ∈ Br(k(ρ)) (Mathlib BrauerGroup, Tau Ceti group structure), and the Schur index s(ρ) := index of B(ρ) = the degree of the division algebra in B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ), n = a·s(ρ). These depend only on the isomorphism class of ρ. For a determinant D on k[Γ] whose base change to k̄ is det ∘ ρ (IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation), B(ρ) ≅ k[Γ]/ker(D) when k(ρ) = k, which is Chenevier's central simple quotient R/ker(D). For every b ∈ B(ρ) (in particular b = ρ(γ)) the characteristic polynomial det(X − b) has coefficients in k(ρ): it is the reduced characteristic polynomial of b in B(ρ); so k(ρ) is also the field generated over k by the coefficients of all det(X − ρ(γ)), in every characteristic.
hypotheses: ρ absolutely irreducible over k̄ (irreducible suffices since k̄ is algebraically closed).
No condition on the characteristic: the trace form on M_n(k̄) is nondegenerate in every characteristic, which is what makes B(ρ) central simple of the right dimension.
Γ arbitrary (no topology needed); for Galois representations take Γ = G_K or a finite quotient.

Library: Mathlib's BrauerGroup K is only the quotient type of central simple algebras; the group structure, the class map and the constructor of a central simple algebra are Tau Ceti's (TauCeti.BrauerGroup.instCommGroup on algebras in the universe of K, TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk, TauCeti.CSA.of), as are base change of Brauer classes (TauCeti.BrauerGroup.baseChange), the degree and the index of a central simple algebra (TauCeti.Algebra.deg, TauCeti.Algebra.index) and the splitting-field predicate. B(ρ) ⊂ M_n(k̄) and k(ρ) ⊂ k̄ live in the universe of k̄, as that group structure requires. What this node adds is the algebra B(ρ) attached to a representation and the translation of these notions into statements about ρ.
proofSteps: B(ρ) is closed under multiplication because ρ(Γ) is a group, and tr(B(ρ)) ⊂ k(ρ).

Burnside: the k̄-span of ρ(Γ) is M_n(k̄) for absolutely irreducible ρ (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible (iii); SemisimpleAlgebras layer 3 density / layer 1 Schur). Choose e_1, …, e_{n²} ∈ ρ(Γ) forming a k̄-basis of M_n(k̄) and let e'_i be the trace-dual basis; for b ∈ B(ρ), b = Σ tr(b e_i) e'_i with tr(b e_i) ∈ k(ρ), so Σ k(ρ) e_i ⊂ B(ρ) ⊂ Σ k(ρ) e'_i, both of dimension n² (BLGGT Lemma A.1.5, proof).

Hence B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ → M_n(k̄) is an isomorphism, so B(ρ) is central simple over k(ρ): it is central by tauceti:TauCeti.Algebra.isCentral_baseChange_iff, and simple because a two-sided ideal I of B(ρ) gives the two-sided ideal I ⊗ k̄ of the simple ring M_n(k̄), which is 0 or everything. For b ∈ B(ρ) the polynomial det(X − b) has coefficients in k(ρ), in every characteristic; it is the reduced characteristic polynomial of b. This is the case A = B(ρ), Z = k(ρ), Ω = k̄, θ = the multiplication map, of the following fact, proved here because no library layer states it: for a central simple algebra A of degree n over a field Z, an algebraic closure Ω of Z and an Ω-algebra isomorphism θ : Ω ⊗_Z A ≅ M_n(Ω), det(X − θ(1 ⊗ a)) ∈ Z[X] for every a ∈ A. Proof: let Z^s be the separable closure of Z in Ω; it is separably closed and Galois over Z (mathlib:separableClosure.isSepClosure, mathlib:separableClosure.isGalois). Choose a Z^s-algebra isomorphism ψ : Z^s ⊗_Z A ≅ M_n(Z^s) (tauceti:TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.nonempty_algEquiv_matrix_baseChange_of_isSepClosed) and put P_a = det(X − ψ(1 ⊗ a)) ∈ Z^s[X]. For σ ∈ Gal(Z^s/Z), with σ acting on matrices entrywise, σ ∘ ψ ∘ (σ^{-1} ⊗ 1) is again a Z^s-algebra isomorphism Z^s ⊗_Z A ≅ M_n(Z^s), so it differs from ψ by a Z^s-algebra automorphism of M_n(Z^s), which is conjugation by an element of GL_n(Z^s) (R01.5/matrix-algebra-endomorphisms-are-inner-over-local-rings; a field is a local ring); evaluating at 1 ⊗ a gives σ(P_a) = P_a. So the coefficients of P_a are fixed by Gal(Z^s/Z) and lie in Z (mathlib:InfiniteGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup for the bottom field). Finally θ and the base change of ψ to Ω are two Ω-algebra isomorphisms Ω ⊗_Z A ≅ M_n(Ω); they differ by an inner automorphism by the same lemma, so det(X − θ(1 ⊗ a)) = P_a.

Isomorphic representations have conjugate image algebras (conjugation by an element of GL_n(k̄) is a k(ρ)-algebra isomorphism), so β(ρ) = TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk (TauCeti.CSA.of k(ρ) B(ρ)) is well defined. A Wedderburn presentation B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ) with Δ central division over k(ρ) exists by tauceti:TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_centralDivisionRing; the Schur index is s(ρ) = TauCeti.Algebra.index k(ρ) B(ρ) = deg Δ (tauceti:TauCeti.Algebra.index_eq_deg_of_algEquiv_matrix), it divides deg B(ρ) = n (tauceti:TauCeti.Algebra.index_dvd_deg), and n = a·s(ρ).

Comparison with Chenevier Definition-Proposition 2.18(iii): for an absolutely irreducible determinant D on k[Γ] with k(ρ) = k, k[Γ]/ker(D) is central simple of rank n², and the map k[Γ] → M_n(k̄) identifies it with B(ρ).
acceptance: Quaternion group: ρ : Q_8 → GL_2(ℚ(i)) ⊂ GL_2(ℚ̄) (the embedding Q_8 ⊂ ℍ^× ⊂ GL_2(ℂ), whose matrices have entries in ℚ(i)) has, for k = ℚ, k(ρ) = ℚ (traces 2, −2, 0) and B(ρ) = the rational quaternions (−1, −1)_ℚ; over k = ℝ, B = ℍ and β(ρ) = [ℍ] ≠ 1 (tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one), s(ρ) = 2.
For Γ = GL_2(F_q), ρ the standard representation over k = F_q: B(ρ) = M_2(F_q), β = 1.

β(ρ) = 1 because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (Deligne–Serre 6.13: no Schur index)
BLGGT Lemma A.1.5's proof: an element with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces every Schur index and centre degree to be 1
subrepresentations are defined over M_λ after a finite extension; the obstruction to doing so without extension is this Brauer class
an absolutely irreducible determinant D has R/ker(D) central simple of rank d²

api.name: TauCeti.GaloisRep.schurIndex_spec
api.statement: For absolutely irreducible ρ of dimension n ≥ 1: B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ) for some a ≥ 1 and some division algebra Δ of dimension s(ρ)² over k(ρ), with n = a·s(ρ); and in every presentation B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ) with Δ a division ring, Δ has dimension s(ρ)² over k(ρ). This determines s(ρ).

nodes.title: Surjectivity onto simple endomorphism factors
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ. The map k[Γ]→∏_i End_k(V_i) is surjective.
hypotheses: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ.
proofSteps: M = V_1 ⊕ … ⊕ V_r is a semisimple k[Γ]-module. A k[Γ]-linear map between simple modules is bijective or zero (mathlib:LinearMap.bijective_or_eq_zero), hence zero from V_i to V_j for i ≠ j, and End_{k[Γ]}(V_i) = k for absolutely irreducible V_i (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible (iv)); so End_{k[Γ]}(M) = ∏_i k·id_{V_i}.

Every family (f_i) ∈ ∏_i End_k(V_i) commutes with End_{k[Γ]}(M); by the Jacobson density theorem (mathlib:jacobson_density, applied to a finite k-basis of M) there is a ∈ k[Γ] acting on each V_i as f_i. This is (1).
acceptance: Distinct simple modules give distinct maximal two-sided annihilator ideals.

nodes.title: Linear independence of absolutely irreducible characters
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ. The functions trρ_i:Γ→k are linearly independent over k.
hypotheses: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ.
proofSteps: Extend the χ_i k-linearly to k[Γ] by χ_i(a) = tr(a | V_i). By R01.5/surjectivity-onto-product-of-endomorphism-algebras choose a_i ∈ k[Γ] acting on V_i as a projector of rank one and on V_j, j ≠ i, as 0; then χ_j(a_i) = δ_{ij} in k. If Σ_j c_j χ_j = 0 on Γ then also on k[Γ], and evaluating at a_i gives c_i = 0. Consequently the characters are linearly independent; no integer is inverted.
acceptance: Use a rank-one projector in one factor; tr(identity) may vanish in characteristic p.

nodes.title: Absolutely irreducible representations are determined by trace
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ. Two absolutely irreducible k-representations with equal trace are isomorphic, in any characteristic. If k′⊂k and σ:k′→k is an embedding, an absolutely irreducible k′-representation ρ satisfies ρ⊗_σk≅ρ⊗k iff σ fixes its traces.
hypotheses: Let k be a field and ρ₁,…,ρᵣ pairwise nonisomorphic finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible k-representations of a group Γ.
proofSteps: If V and W are nonisomorphic, their two characters are linearly independent by R01.5/linear-independence-of-absolutely-irreducible-characters; equality contradicts that independence. For σ:k′→k, both coefficient extensions are absolutely irreducible by R01.1/absolutely-irreducible; the σ-extension has trace σ∘trρ, so apply the first assertion.
acceptance: This uses absolute irreducibility, not invertibility of the representation dimension.

nodes.title: Base change of a simple module
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as. Over k̄, W decomposes as ⊕_{τ:Z→k̄}ρ_τ^{⊕s}, where the ρ_τ are pairwise nonisomorphic absolutely irreducibles of dimension m. Thus dim_kW=m·s·[Z:k].
hypotheses: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as.
proofSteps: B acts faithfully on the simple module W and is finite-dimensional, so it is a simple algebra with W as its simple module (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 2). Its centre Z is a field, finite over k and separable because k is perfect, and B is central simple over Z; so B ≅ M_a(Δ) with Δ a central division Z-algebra (tauceti:TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_centralDivisionRing), s = deg Δ = TauCeti.Algebra.index Z B, and W ≅ Δ^a.

Z ⊗_k k̄ ≅ ∏_τ k̄ over the k-embeddings τ (Z = k[x]/(f) with f separable, and f splits into distinct linear factors over k̄), so B ⊗_k k̄ ≅ ∏_τ B ⊗_{Z,τ} k̄; each factor is the scalar extension along τ of the central simple Z-algebra B, hence isomorphic to M_m(k̄) with m = deg B (tauceti:TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.nonempty_algEquiv_matrix_baseChange_of_isSepClosed, k̄ being separably closed).

W ⊗_k k̄ = ⊕_τ W ⊗_{Z,τ} k̄, and W ⊗_{Z,τ} k̄ is a module over M_m(k̄) of k̄-dimension dim_Z W = a·s² = m·s, hence the sum of s copies of the simple module k̄^m; ρ_τ is this simple module with Γ acting through B. It is irreducible because the image of k̄[Γ] is all of M_m(k̄), and ρ_τ ≇ ρ_{τ'} for τ ≠ τ' because the idempotent of B ⊗_k k̄ belonging to the factor τ, which lies in the image of k̄[Γ], acts as 1 on ρ_τ and as 0 on ρ_{τ'}. This gives the decomposition and the dimension formula of (1).
σ ∈ Gal(k̄/k) acts on B ⊗_k k̄ through the second factor and maps the factor τ to the factor σ∘τ, so σ(ρ_τ) ≅ ρ_{σ∘τ}; the action on Hom_k(Z, k̄) is transitive.
acceptance: Separability of Z/k is supplied by perfectness of k.

nodes.title: Trace field and index of a geometric constituent
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as. For each τ the trace field of ρ_τ is τ(Z), its central simple image algebra is B⊗_{Z,τ}τ(Z), and its Schur index is s.
hypotheses: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as.
proofSteps: (2): tr ρ_τ(γ) is the trace of the image of γ under a splitting B ⊗_{Z,τ} k̄ ≅ M_m(k̄) of the central simple Z-algebra B, and the characteristic polynomial of the image of an element of B under such a splitting has coefficients in τ(Z) (the fact proved in the reduced-characteristic-polynomial argument of R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation, applied to A = B and to k̄ as an algebraic closure of Z through τ); so k(ρ_τ) ⊂ τ(Z). The k-span of ρ_τ(Γ) is the image of B under the injective map B → B ⊗_{Z,τ} k̄ ≅ M_m(k̄); it has k-dimension m²·[Z : k] and is contained in B(ρ_τ), of k-dimension m²·[k(ρ_τ) : k] (R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation (2)). Hence [Z : k] ≤ [k(ρ_τ) : k] ≤ [Z : k]: k(ρ_τ) = τ(Z) and the image of B is B(ρ_τ).
acceptance: The trace field is the embedded centre, not necessarily all of k̄.

nodes.title: The simple module attached to an irreducible representation
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as. Conversely an absolutely irreducible ρ over k̄ with finite trace field over k belongs to the scalar extension of a unique simple k[Γ]-module W_ρ. The simple modules over k correspond to the Galois orbits of such ρ.
hypotheses: Let k be perfect, W a finite-dimensional simple k[Γ]-module, and B its image algebra. Write B=M_a(Δ), Z=centre(Δ), [Δ:Z]=s² and m=as.
proofSteps: Let U be the simple module of the central simple trace-field algebra B(ρ), regarded over k, and choose a simple k[Γ]-submodule W₀. Splitting B(ρ) over k̄ gives U⊗k̄ as the sum of the conjugates of ρ with multiplicity its Schur index. By R01.5/simple-modules-over-the-algebraic-closure, the constituents of W₀⊗k̄ are one entire orbit, hence this orbit of ρ.

R01.5/image-algebra-of-a-constituent now identifies the k-span of ρ(Γ) with B(ρ), so U is simple over k[Γ] and W₀=U. For any other simple W whose extension contains ρ, the same result identifies its image algebra with B(ρ) compatibly with Γ. A simple Artin–Wedderburn algebra has one simple module up to isomorphism, proving uniqueness. Its scalar extension is exactly the orbit already computed.
acceptance: The multiplicity of ρ in W_ρ⊗k̄ is its Schur index, not always one.

nodes.title: Galois invariance of constituent multiplicities
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, k̄ an algebraic closure, and ρ a finite-dimensional semisimple representation over k̄ whose irreducible constituents have finite trace fields over k. The characteristic polynomials of ρ lie in k iff Gal(k̄/k) preserves its multiset of irreducible constituents, including multiplicities.

proofSteps: For σ∈Gal(k̄/k), conjugation applies σ to all polynomial coefficients. R01.1/brauer-nesbitt identifies ρ and ρ^σ iff these coefficients agree; uniqueness of semisimple decomposition identifies the constituent multisets.
acceptance: In positive characteristic use all polynomial coefficients rather than just traces.

nodes.title: Schur-index obstruction to descent
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, k̄ an algebraic closure, and ρ a finite-dimensional semisimple representation over k̄ whose irreducible constituents have finite trace fields over k. Assume the constituent multiset is Galois invariant. For each orbit O let Z_O be its trace field, s_O its Schur index and m_O its common constituent multiplicity. Then ρ has a k-form iff s_O divides m_O for every orbit O.
hypotheses: Let k be perfect, k̄ an algebraic closure, and ρ a finite-dimensional semisimple representation over k̄ whose irreducible constituents have finite trace fields over k.
proofSteps: R01.5/galois-action-on-constituents identifies the invariant multiset. R01.5/simple-module-of-an-irreducible-representation assigns one simple k[Γ]-module W_O to each constituent orbit O. R01.5/simple-modules-over-the-algebraic-closure computes W_O⊗k̄ as the direct sum of that orbit with each constituent repeated s_O times.

Any k-form of ρ is semisimple: the radical of its finite-dimensional image algebra extends to a nilpotent ideal acting on the semisimple scalar extension, hence acts trivially; the original image algebra acts faithfully, so its radical is zero. Therefore the form is a sum of the W_O, and comparison of constituent multiplicities forces s_O|m_O.

Conversely, if all these divisibilities hold, the direct sum of W_O with multiplicities m_O/s_O is a k-form. This criterion permits nonsplit simple image algebras when their index divides the multiplicity; it does not use the stronger matrix-algebra condition rejected in source issue E501.
acceptance: An irreducible constituent with index two and multiplicity one obstructs descent.

nodes.title: Descent obstruction and determinant reconstruction
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, k̄ an algebraic closure, and ρ a finite-dimensional semisimple representation over k̄ whose irreducible constituents have finite trace fields over k. For a k-valued determinant D attached to ρ, the Chenevier 2.16 factorisation is D=∏_O N_{Z_O/k}∘Nrd_{S_O/Z_O}^{m_O}, with one factor for each constituent orbit O and S_O its central simple image algebra. This records determinant descent even when the representation has no k-form.
hypotheses: Let k be perfect, k̄ an algebraic closure, and ρ a finite-dimensional semisimple representation over k̄ whose irreducible constituents have finite trace fields over k.
proofSteps: The semisimple quotient and its determinant factorisation are IHG.1, Chenevier Theorem 2.16; use one central simple factor per Galois orbit. Over k̄, reduced norm becomes the matrix determinant, and field norm multiplies over the embeddings of Z_O. The resulting multiplicity m_O is the given constituent multiplicity.
acceptance: The product is over orbits, not over each geometric constituent separately.
