nodes.title: Realisation over a finite polynomial field
nodes.statement: Let k⊂k′ be finite fields and Γ profinite. If ρ:Γ→GL_n(k′) is continuous and semisimple with all characteristic polynomials in k[X], it has a continuous k-form with the same kernel.
hypotheses: Let k⊂k′ be finite fields and Γ profinite.
proofSteps: The image Φ is finite because the coefficient fields are finite and the representation is continuous. Extend to an algebraic closure k̄; semisimplicity is preserved because k′ is perfect. The k-rational characteristic polynomials and Brauer–Nesbitt imply that the constituents and their multiplicities are Galois invariant. R01.5/descent-obstruction is the general semisimple criterion: each constituent Schur index must divide its multiplicity. Every centre here is a finite extension of the finite field k and has trivial Brauer group (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite), so each Schur index is one. This supplies a k[Φ]-module V whose scalar extension to k̄ is the given module. Brauer–Nesbitt over k′ identifies V⊗_k k′ with ρ; no absolute irreducibility hypothesis is imposed.

Continuity and kernel: φ_0 ⊗ k' ≅ φ forces ker φ_0 = ker φ, open when φ is continuous (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); Frobenius characteristic polynomials are unchanged by the isomorphism.
acceptance: Brauer groups of finite fields are trivial, so no Schur-index obstruction remains.

nodes.title: Residual realisation over its Frobenius field

nodes.title: Descent of a semisimple image algebra
nodes.statement: Let M be a characteristic-zero field, M̄ its algebraic closure and r:Γ→GL_n(M̄) semisimple with traces in M. The M-span B of r(Γ) is a finite-dimensional semisimple M-algebra and B⊗_M M̄ maps isomorphically to the M̄-span B_{M̄} of r(Γ).
hypotheses: Let M be a characteristic-zero field, M̄ its algebraic closure and r:Γ→GL_n(M̄) semisimple with traces in M.
proofSteps: Write B_{M̄} as a product of matrix algebras, with their positive multiplicities in r. In characteristic zero the trace pairing on it is nondegenerate. Choose a basis from r(Γ); its trace-dual coefficient equations have coefficients in M, so every r(g) is in their M-span and the basis remains independent after extension. Semisimplicity descends from the faithfully flat scalar extension.
acceptance: Characteristic zero prevents a constituent multiplicity from becoming zero in the trace pairing.

nodes.title: Descent from distinct rational eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Let M be a characteristic-zero field, M̄ its algebraic closure and r:Γ→GL_n(M̄) semisimple with traces in M. If some r(g₀) has n distinct eigenvalues in M, then r has an M-form.
hypotheses: Let M be a characteristic-zero field, M̄ its algebraic closure and r:Γ→GL_n(M̄) semisimple with traces in M.
proofSteps: R01.5/image-algebra-of-a-semisimple-representation gives a finite-dimensional semisimple image algebra B over M. Write its simple factors as M_{a_j}(D_j), with division algebra D_j of degree s_j over its centre Z_j. Over M̄ the representation is a sum of the standard modules of these split factors; trace rationality makes their multiplicities equal across embeddings of each centre.

An element b = (b_j) of B with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces r_j = n_j = [Z(D_j) : M] = 1 for all j: the characteristic polynomial of b on M̄^n is ∏_{j,τ} τ(P_j)^{n_j}, P_j ∈ Z(D_j)[X] the reduced characteristic polynomial of b_j, so n_j = 1; a root α ∈ M of τ(P_j) is a root of P_j, hence of every τ'(P_j), so [Z(D_j) : M] = 1; and then M[b_j] ≅ M^{m_j r_j} gives m_j r_j orthogonal idempotents in M_{m_j}(D_j), whose left module has length m_j, so r_j = 1. Hence B ≅ ⊕ M_{m_j}(M) and M^n with this action is an M-form of r (R01.5/descent-obstruction with all Schur indices 1).
acceptance: Repeated rational eigenvalues do not give the same splitting argument.

nodes.title: Additive Haar invariance under units
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺. Left and right multiplication by any unit preserve μ⁺.
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺.
proofSteps: (1): A^× acts on the additive group A by left multiplication, continuously and by additive automorphisms. For such an action on a locally compact group and a Haar measure μ⁺ one has Δ(u)·μ⁺(S) = μ⁺(uS) with Δ = MeasureTheory.distribHaarChar A (mathlib:MeasureTheory.distribHaarChar_mul). For S = A this reads Δ(u)·μ⁺(A) = μ⁺(A) with 0 < μ⁺(A) < ∞, so Δ(u) = 1. The same argument for the action of the opposite group gives right multiplication.
acceptance: No commutativity of A is required.

nodes.title: Compactness of the unit group
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺. The unit group Aˣ is compact, and its inclusion into A identifies its topology with the subspace topology.
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺.
proofSteps: (2): u ↦ (u, u^{-1}) embeds A^× into A × A^{op} with image the closed set {(a, b) : ab = ba = 1}, so A^× is compact; the continuous injection A^× → A from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism onto its image.

nodes.title: Haar probability on open unit subgroups
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺. If G⊂Aˣ is compact and its image is open in A, Haar probability on G is the normalised restriction of μ⁺ to G.
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺.
proofSteps: (3): G is open in A, hence open and therefore closed in the compact group A^×, hence compact. The measure ν(S) = μ⁺(S) on the Borel subsets of G is finite, positive on nonempty open sets (μ⁺ is, and G is open in A) and left invariant by (1); so it is a Haar measure on G, and ν/ν(G) is a Haar probability measure, equal to TauCeti.haarProb G by tauceti:TauCeti.eq_haarProb_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure.
acceptance: Openness is in the ring, not just in Aˣ.

nodes.title: Additive measure of integral invertible matrices
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺. For A=M_n(O_E), residue field size q, μ⁺(GL_n(O_E))=∏_{i=1}^n(1−q⁻ⁱ).
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological ring with additive Haar probability μ⁺.
proofSteps: (4): det : M_n(O_E) → O_E is continuous and GL_n(O_E) is the preimage of O_E^×, the complement of the maximal ideal, which is open and closed. GL_n(O_E) is the preimage of GL_n(F_q) under reduction, a union of #GL_n(F_q) cosets of M_n(m_E), each of μ⁺-measure q^{-n²} (the additive subgroup M_n(m_E) has index q^{n²} and is open; the additive form of mathlib:MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure); and #GL_n(F_q) = ∏_{i=0}^{n-1} (q^n − q^i) (mathlib:Matrix.card_GL_field).
acceptance: For n=0 the empty product and the measure both equal one.

nodes.title: Polynomial zero sets are Haar-null
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff second-countable topological integral domain with no isolated points, and use additive Haar probability. For every nonzero polynomial in N variables over A, its zero set in Aᴺ is closed and null for product Haar probability.
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff second-countable topological integral domain with no isolated points, and use additive Haar probability.
proofSteps: Z(f) is closed because polynomial evaluation is continuous on a topological ring; A is second countable, so the Borel σ-algebra of A^N is the product σ-algebra on which (μ⁺)^{⊗N} is defined, and Z(f) is measurable for it (without second countability a closed subset of A^N need not be measurable for the product σ-algebra, and step 4 could not be applied). (μ⁺)^{⊗N} is an additive Haar measure of A^N (the additive form of mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.pi.isHaarMeasure), and μ⁺ is finite.

Induction on N. For N = 0, f is a nonzero constant and Z(f) = ∅. For the step identify A^{N+1} with A × A^N compatibly with the measures (mathlib:MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove) and write f = Σ_j f_j(X_2, …, X_{N+1}) X_1^j (mathlib:MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv) with some f_j ≠ 0; by induction Z(f_j) ⊂ A^N is null.

For y ∉ Z(f_j) the polynomial f(X_1, y) ∈ A[X_1] is nonzero, so it has finitely many roots in the domain A (mathlib:Polynomial.rootSet_finite), and a finite set is μ⁺-null because an additive Haar measure on a group in which 0 is not isolated gives measure zero to points (the additive form of mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.IsHaarMeasure.noAtoms).

So for almost every y the slice {x_1 ∈ A : f(x_1, y) = 0} is null, and Fubini for measurable sets (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_prod_null, with the two factors exchanged) gives that Z(f) is null.
acceptance: In zero variables a nonzero constant has empty zero set.

nodes.title: Polynomial zero sets in open matrix groups
nodes.statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff second-countable topological integral domain with no isolated points, and use additive Haar probability. For O_E and G open in GL_n(O_E), a nonzero polynomial over E has Haar-null zero set on G. Hence a polynomial vanishing on a positive-measure subset of G is zero, and a polynomial not identically zero on G has null zero set there.
hypotheses: Let A be a compact Hausdorff second-countable topological integral domain with no isolated points, and use additive Haar probability.
proofSteps: Multiply the nonzero polynomial over E by a power of a uniformiser so that its coefficients lie in O_E, preserving its zero set. R01.5/polynomial-zero-sets-are-haar-null makes that zero set null for product additive Haar probability on O_E^{n²}. The coordinate isomorphism with M_n(O_E) transports this to additive Haar probability there.

The open subgroup G is open in the matrix ring. R01.5/haar-measure-on-open-subgroups-of-gl-n identifies its Haar probability with the normalised restriction of the additive measure, so its intersection with the zero set is null. A positive-measure zero set therefore forces the polynomial to be zero.
acceptance: Clear denominators before applying the compact-domain result; this only proves the open-GL_n case.

nodes.title: Chebotarev for clopen subsets
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}. If C is open and closed, Σ_C has both Dirichlet and natural density μ(C).
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}.
proofSteps: Open normal subgroups U of G form a basis at 1 (profinite). For C open and closed and conjugation-stable, C is a union of cosets of some open normal U (compactness), C = π^{-1}(C_U) for π : G → G/U, and μ(C) = #C_U/#(G/U): all cosets of U have the same measure and there are [G : U] of them (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure); equivalently the image of μ in G/U is a Haar probability measure, hence TauCeti.haarProb (G/U) by uniqueness, and tauceti:TauCeti.haarProb_apply evaluates it on a subset of a finite group.

(a): L = K̄^{ρ^{-1}(U)} is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ G/U, unramified outside S; v ∈ Σ_C iff Frob_v ∈ C_U; C_U is a union of conjugacy classes of G/U; Chebotarev layer 10 (resp. 14) for each of them, R01.5/frobenius-density-finite-level to pass from Frobenius classes in Gal(L/K) to Frobenius lifts in G_K, and finite additivity of the density give #C_U/#(G/U) = μ(C).
acceptance: In a finite quotient this is #C/#G, using probability normalisation.

nodes.title: Chebotarev upper bound for closed subsets
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}. If C is closed, the upper Dirichlet density of Σ_C is at most μ(C). In particular positive upper density forces μ(C)>0.
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}.

nodes.title: Polynomial Frobenius conditions of density zero
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}. For G open in GL_n(O_E), a polynomial f on M_n(E) that is conjugation invariant and does not vanish identically on G defines a density-zero set of Frobenius places. If f is not invariant, the closed null set ∩_{h∈G}h{f=0}h⁻¹ gives the statement for entire conjugacy classes.
hypotheses: Let K be a number field, ρ:G_K→G a continuous surjection to a profinite group, unramified outside a finite set S, and μ=TauCeti.haarProb G. For conjugation-stable C⊂G put Σ_C={v∉S:ρ(Frob_v)∈C}.
proofSteps: (e): C = {g ∈ G : f(g) = 0} is closed, and conjugation-stable because f is; it is null for μ by R01.5/polynomial-zero-sets-in-open-subgroups-of-gl-n, which combines the Fubini argument for zero sets of nonzero polynomials on O_E^{n²} with R01.5/haar-measure-on-open-subgroups-of-gl-n (the Haar probability measure of an open subgroup of GL_n(O_E) is the normalised restriction of the additive Haar measure of M_n(O_E)). Then (b) gives density 0. The trace is not identically zero on an open subgroup of GL_2(ℤ_ℓ): an open subgroup contains 1 + ℓ^m M_2(ℤ_ℓ) for some m, on which tr takes the value 2 + ℓ^m ≠ 0 (this also covers ℓ = 2, where tr(1) = 2 is still nonzero in ℤ_2).
acceptance: For an open image in GL₂(Z_ℓ), tr=0 has density zero, including ℓ=2.

nodes.title: R-algebra endomorphisms of M_d(R) are inner for a local ring R
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative local ring and d ≥ 0. Every R-algebra homomorphism φ : M_d(R) → M_d(R) has the form φ(x) = g x g^{-1} for some g ∈ GL_d(R); in particular φ is an automorphism. The element g is unique up to multiplication by an element of R^×.
hypotheses: R commutative and local; this is used once, to know that a finitely generated projective R-module is free.
φ is unital and R-linear; no topology.

Over a ring that is not local the statement can fail: for a Dedekind domain R with a non-principal ideal I such that I² is principal (R = ℤ[√−5], I = (2, 1 + √−5)), I ⊕ I ≅ R² and End_R(I ⊕ I) = M_2(R) give an automorphism of M_2(R) that is not inner.
proofSteps: For d = 0 the algebra M_0(R) is the zero ring, GL_0(R) is trivial and there is nothing to prove; let d ≥ 1. Let E_{ij} be the matrix units (mathlib:Matrix.single) and e_i = φ(E_{ii}); they are orthogonal idempotents of M_d(R) with sum φ(1) = 1, so R^d = ⊕_i e_iR^d, and φ(E_{i1}) : e_1R^d → e_iR^d is an isomorphism with inverse φ(E_{1i}).

P = e_1R^d is a direct summand of R^d, hence finitely generated projective, hence free because R is local (mathlib:Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing); R^d ≅ P^d and R ≠ 0 force rank P = 1. Choose a generator v of P and put v_i = φ(E_{i1})v; then (v_1, …, v_d) is a basis of R^d.

Let g ∈ GL_d(R) be the matrix with columns v_1, …, v_d. Then φ(E_{ij})v_k = φ(E_{ij}E_{k1})v = δ_{jk}v_i = gE_{ij}g^{-1}v_k, so φ(E_{ij}) = gE_{ij}g^{-1}; the E_{ij} span M_d(R) over R, hence φ(x) = gxg^{-1} for all x.

Uniqueness: if g and g' both work, g^{-1}g' commutes with every matrix unit, hence is a scalar matrix (mathlib:Matrix.mem_range_scalar_of_commute_single), and the scalar is a unit because g^{-1}g' is invertible.
acceptance: d = 1: the only R-algebra endomorphism of R is the identity, and g is any element of R^×.
R = k a field: every k-algebra endomorphism of M_d(k) is inner (Skolem–Noether for matrix algebras).
R = k[t]/(t²) and φ(x) = (1 + tN)x(1 − tN) for N ∈ M_d(k): g = 1 + tN, determined up to (k[t]/(t²))^×.
Non-example over a non-local ring: hypothesis 3.

sources.match: The matrix-unit argument over a local ring: a system of matrix units E_{i,j} with e_iRe_i = Ae_i identifies R with M_d(A). The node applies the same argument to the matrix units φ(E_{ij}) of M_d(R) to show that φ is conjugation by the change of basis.

nodes.title: Carayol recognition of lifts
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation. Equality of traces, or of characteristic polynomials, on a dense subset implies r′=grg⁻¹ with g∈ker(GL_d(R)→GL_d(k)), unique up to a scalar in 1+m. There is no invertibility assumption on d!.
hypotheses: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation.
proofSteps: Continuity and density: the characteristic-polynomial maps γ ↦ det(X − r(γ)), det(X − r'(γ)) ∈ R[X] are continuous and agree on a dense set, hence everywhere (R01.5/frobenius-density; R is Hausdorff). So det ∘ r = det ∘ r' as continuous determinants on R[Γ] (IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense, IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation).

Algebra (IHG.1, Chenevier Theorem 2.22(i)): for the common determinant D, D mod m_R is absolutely irreducible and split (its quotient k[Γ]/ker is M_d(k), because r̄ is absolutely irreducible over k), so the Cayley–Hamilton quotient R[Γ]/CH(D) ≅ M_d(R) with D = det. Both r and r' factor through it (a matrix representation kills the Cayley–Hamilton ideal of its determinant: the coefficients of χ(t_1x_1 + ⋯ + t_mx_m) are mapped to those of the characteristic polynomial of the matrix t_1r(x_1) + ⋯ + t_mr(x_m) over R[t_1, …, t_m] evaluated at itself, which vanish by mathlib:Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly; IHG.1/cayley-hamilton is the definition of the Cayley–Hamilton quotient) and so differ by an R-algebra endomorphism of M_d(R); by R01.5/matrix-algebra-endomorphisms-are-inner-over-local-rings it is conjugation by some g ∈ GL_d(R), so r' = g r g^{-1}.

Normalising g: ḡ commutes with r̄(Γ), so ḡ = c ∈ k^× by Schur's lemma for the absolutely irreducible r̄; replacing g by [c]^{-1}g ([c] ∈ R^× a lift) gives g ∈ 1 + M_d(m_R). Uniqueness: End_{R[Γ]}(r) = R (Nakayama plus residual Schur), so g is unique up to (1 + m_R).

Trace form of (a), without determinants: the R-algebra maps r, r' : R[Γ] → M_d(R) are surjective (Burnside for r̄, R01.1/absolutely-irreducible (iii), and Nakayama). The trace pairing (x, y) ↦ tr(xy) on M_d(R) is perfect, so ker r = {x ∈ R[Γ] : tr r(xy) = 0 for all y ∈ R[Γ]}, and the same for r'. If tr r = tr r' on a dense subset of Γ then on Γ (continuity, R Hausdorff) and on R[Γ] (linearity); the kernels coincide, r' ∘ r^{-1} is an R-algebra automorphism of M_d(R), which is conjugation by some g ∈ GL_d(R) (R01.5/matrix-algebra-endomorphisms-are-inner-over-local-rings), and steps 3–5 apply unchanged.
acceptance: The trace proof uses absolute residual irreducibility; factorial inversion is unnecessary.

nodes.title: Carayol recognition with a fixed symplectic form
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation. If r,r′ take values in GSp_{2a}(R) for the same alternating form J and multiplier ν, the strict conjugator belongs to ker(GSp_{2a}(R)→GSp_{2a}(k)).
hypotheses: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation.
proofSteps: (b): g^T J g is an r-invariant alternating form with multiplier ν: r(γ)^T(g^T J g)r(γ) = g^T r'(γ)^T J r'(γ) g = ν(γ) g^T J g. Such forms are Hom_{R[Γ]}(r, r^∨ ⊗ ν), free of rank one over R generated by J (step 3 applied to r^∨ ⊗ ν ≅ r via J), so g^T J g = cJ with c ∈ R^×, c ≡ 1 mod m_R; thus g ∈ GSp_{2m}(R) with multiplier c and ḡ = 1.
acceptance: The conjugator may have multiplier c∈1+m; membership in Sp is not asserted.

nodes.title: Gluing compatible polynomial data
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation. Let a_j be decreasing open ideals forming a neighbourhood basis of zero. Continuous lifts r_j over R/a_j with prescribed degree-d polynomials P_γ mod a_j on a fixed dense set can be strictly conjugated to a compatible system, which glues to a continuous lift over R, unique up to strict conjugacy. For GSp impose the same form and multiplier at each level.
hypotheses: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field k and maximal ideal m, Γ profinite, and r,r′:Γ→GL_d(R) continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible residual representation.
proofSteps: (c): by (a) applied over R/𝔞_j, r_{j+1} mod 𝔞_j and r_j are conjugate by an element of ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_j) → GL_d(k)); lift it to ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_{j+1}) → GL_d(k)) (1 + M_d(m) surjects) and conjugate r_{j+1}; inductively the system is compatible, and r = lim r_j is continuous for the inverse-limit topology, which is the m_R-adic topology because the 𝔞_j form a neighbourhood basis. The characteristic polynomials are the limits P_γ. Uniqueness follows from (a).
acceptance: An arbitrary decreasing family that is not a neighbourhood basis does not suffice.

nodes.title: Frobenius annihilation extends to the image closure
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified. Then P_ρ(g)(s(g))=0 for every g∈G_Q and on the Zariski closure of (ρ,s)(G_Q).
hypotheses: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified.
proofSteps: Density step: g ↦ char_ρ(g)(s(g)) is a continuous M_n(E)-valued function on G_ℚ vanishing at the Frobenius elements of a density-one set, hence identically (R01.5/frobenius-density-image, applied to φ = (ρ, s) and the density-one set); being polynomial in the matrix entries of (ρ(g), s(g)), it vanishes on the Zariski closure of (ρ, s)(G_ℚ).
acceptance: The annihilation hypothesis is stronger than containment of eigenvalue sets.

nodes.title: Constituents with induced GSp4 monodromy
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified. If the Zariski closure contains SL₂×SL₂ and ρ is absolutely irreducible but reducible on an index-two G_E, write ρ|_{G_E}=ϱ⊕ϱᶜ. Every irreducible subquotient of s|_{G_E} is ϱ or ϱᶜ.
hypotheses: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified.
proofSteps: (b): restrict to G_E, ρ|_{G_E} = ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c, and let t be an irreducible subquotient of s|_{G_E}. Let T and P be the Zariski closures of the images of t and of ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups); T is reductive (t is irreducible, characteristic 0), and by Goursat's lemma the Zariski closure of the image of t ⊕ ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c in T × P is the graph of an isomorphism between quotients T/K and P/K'. An element of K is paired with 1 ∈ P, so by the annihilation identity (extended by continuity) it is killed by (X − 1)^4: K is a unipotent normal subgroup of the reductive group T, hence trivial. So T is a quotient of P ⊃ SL_2 × SL_2, t is up to twist Sym^i ϱ ⊗ Sym^j ϱ^c, and t ∈ {ϱ, ϱ^c}. The algebraic-group facts used here beyond G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups are recorded as a gap.
acceptance: The algebraic-group Goursat and classification inputs remain recorded gaps.

nodes.title: Absence of self-extensions of the two constituents
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified. Under the induced-monodromy hypotheses, s|_{G_E} contains no nonsplit self-extension of ϱ or ϱᶜ.
hypotheses: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified.
proofSteps: No self-extensions of ϱ (or ϱ^c) occur in s|_{G_E}: a generic element of ϱ^c acts invertibly on ϱ, and the GL_2 version of Nekovář's criterion applies (first proved by Boston–Lenstra–Ribet, Quotients of group rings arising from two-dimensional representations, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 312 (1991), the reference [BLR91] of BCGP25).

nodes.title: Asai eigenvalues outside the inducing subgroup
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified. In the induced case let ν be the similitude character, so detϱ=ν|_{G_E}. For g∉G_E, the characteristic polynomial on A=Asai(ϱ)⊗ν⁻¹ is (X²−1)(X²−tX+1), t=trϱ(g²)/ν(g). Its eigenvalues are 1,−1,λ,λ⁻¹, with multiplicities.
hypotheses: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified.
proofSteps: In the tensor-induction model, after identifying the two factors, g acts by a twisted swap (B⊗1)swap, B=ϱ(g²). Triangularise B over Q̄_p with diagonal a,b. The eigenvalues of this swap are a,b and the two roots of X²−ab. Since ab=detϱ(g²)=ν(g)², division by ν(g) gives a/ν(g),b/ν(g),1,−1 with (a/ν(g))(b/ν(g))=1. The polynomial identity remains valid for repeated eigenvalues by triangularisation. The printed λ,−λ in BCGP25 is retained as source issue E502.
acceptance: If B=ν(g)I, the eigenvalues are 1,1,1,−1; opposite λ,−λ would give a wrong polynomial.

hypotheses: Let p be prime, ρ:G_Q→GSp₄(Q̄_p), s:G_Q→GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous, n≥1, and assume P_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l))=0 on a density-one set of primes where both are unramified.
proofSteps: R01.5/gsp4-semisimplicity-induced-constituents and R01.5/gsp4-semisimplicity-no-self-extensions reduce the obstruction to cross extensions of ϱ and ϱᶜ after restriction to G_E. Shapiro identifies their induced obstruction with extensions of 1 by A=Asai(ϱ)⊗ν⁻¹ or by A⊗χ, where χ is the quadratic character of E/Q.

R01.5/asai-eigenvalues-off-the-subgroup computes the eigenvalues 1,−1,λ,λ⁻¹ outside G_E, retaining E502. The algebraic-group analysis of a nonsplit extension in A⋊O₄ supplies an element with minimal polynomial of degree five, contradicting the degree-four identity in R01.5/frobenius-annihilation-extends. This algebraic-group classification and the GL₂ extension criterion remain the recorded gaps; the reduction does not claim them established.

Once those two inputs are supplied, no nonsplit extension remains. All composition factors are ρ by induction and Clifford theory, so s is a direct sum of copies of ρ. Its positive dimension forces a positive multiplicity.
acceptance: Both semisimplification and exclusion of nonsplit extensions are required.

nodes.title: Restriction of a potentially abelian representation
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L). The restriction is ⊕_{i=1}^bχ_i^{⊕a}, ab=n, with distinct continuous characters forming one Gal(L/F)-orbit for χ^σ(h)=χ(σ̃hσ̃⁻¹).
hypotheses: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L).
proofSteps: ρ|_{G_L} is semisimple (restriction of an irreducible characteristic-zero representation to an open normal subgroup, R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction, Clifford); its image is abelian and E algebraically closed, so it is a sum of characters.

By R01.1/clifford-isotypic-decomposition, Res_{G_L} ρ ≅ (W_1 ⊕ … ⊕ W_t)^{⊕e} with W_1, …, W_t the distinct G_F-conjugates of one irreducible constituent and t the index of the stabiliser of its isomorphism class; here the W_j are the characters χ_i, so t = b, e = a, the characters form one orbit and the multiplicity is constant. Explicitly, for σ ∈ G_F, ρ(σ) maps the χ-eigenspace of G_L to the χ^{σ^{-1}}-eigenspace (ρ(h)ρ(σ)v = ρ(σ)ρ(σ^{-1}hσ)v; the source prints χ^σ, source issue E551), and the sum of the eigenspaces over one orbit is G_F-stable.
acceptance: ρ(σ) sends the χ-eigenspace to the χ^{σ⁻¹}-eigenspace.

nodes.title: Induction from a character stabiliser
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L). If K_i is fixed by the stabiliser of χ_i in Gal(L/F), then [K_i:F]=b and the χ_i-isotypic space V_i is an irreducible continuous G_{K_i}-representation with ρ≅Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F}V_i.
hypotheses: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L).
proofSteps: The χ_i-eigenspace V_i is stable under G_{K_i}; orbit–stabiliser gives [K_i : F] = b; Frobenius reciprocity gives a nonzero map ρ → Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i, an isomorphism by irreducibility and dimension count (n = b·a), and then V_i is irreducible.
acceptance: The dimension count is n=b·a, and K_i need not be Galois over F.

nodes.title: Scalar restriction and finite projective image
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L). For the given L, b=1 iff ρ(G_L) consists of scalars, which implies finite projective image. Conversely finite projective image gives b=1 for L chosen as the fixed field of its kernel.
hypotheses: Let F be a field, E algebraically closed of characteristic zero, ρ:G_F→GL_n(E) continuous irreducible, and L/F finite Galois with abelian ρ(G_L).
proofSteps: (4): b = 1 means G_L acts by a single character, i.e. by scalars, so the projective image is a quotient of Gal(L/F); conversely, if the projective image is finite, its kernel is an open normal subgroup G_{L'} acting by scalars, and for L' the decomposition has b = 1.

nodes.title: Recognition of lisse sheaves on a curve over a finite field from a dense open subset
nodes.statement: Let F_q be a finite field of characteristic p, C a smooth geometrically connected curve over F_q, U ⊂ C a nonempty (hence dense) open subscheme, ℓ ≠ p, and E a field of characteristic 0 that is a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (or Q̄_ℓ). Let V_1, V_2 be lisse E-sheaves of rank n on C, i.e. continuous representations of π_1(C, c̄) on n-dimensional E-vector spaces. If det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{1,x̄}) = det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{2,x̄}) in E[t] for every closed point x ∈ |U| (geometric or arithmetic Frobenius, the same for both), then V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss as representations of π_1(C); if V_1, V_2 are semisimple, V_1 ≅ V_2. This is the step 'by the Chebotarev density Theorem, the semisimplifications … are isomorphic' in the proof of Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5.
hypotheses: C normal and connected (smooth geometrically connected), U dense open; equality at every closed point of U.
Common coefficient field E of characteristic 0 (for different ℓ the comparison is of polynomials with coefficients in a number field, after which a single ℓ is used).
Conclusion only for semisimplifications.
proofSteps: π_1(U) → π_1(C) is surjective for a dense open U of a normal connected scheme (IG.1 owner of the arithmetic fundamental group sequence and Frobenius at closed points).

Closed-point Chebotarev for U (FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5): for every connected finite étale Galois cover V → U with group G and every g ∈ G there is a closed point x of U and a point of V above it whose Frobenius is g (FA.5 gives more: if F_{q^m} is the field of constants of V and g maps to the class of d in Gal(F_{q^m}/F_q) = ℤ/m, there are such x of every sufficiently large degree ≡ d mod m). The open normal subgroups of π_1(U) are the groups of such covers, so the Frobenius elements Frob_x, x ∈ |U|, with all their conjugates, meet every coset of every open normal subgroup: they are dense in π_1(U), and their images are dense in π_1(C) by step 1.

The characteristic-polynomial maps π_1(C) → E[t] of V_1, V_2 are continuous class functions agreeing on a dense set, hence everywhere (as in R01.5/recognition-on-a-dense-subset); det(1 − g t) and det(1 − g^{-1} t) determine each other, so the Frobenius convention is irrelevant.
R01.1/brauer-nesbitt gives V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss; semisimple sheaves are equal to their semisimplifications.
acceptance: Semisimplicity is required: on C = P¹ ∖ {0, ∞} over F_q, the representation g ↦ [[1, deg(g)],[0, 1]] (deg : π_1(C) → Ẑ → ℤ_ℓ the degree map) is a nonsplit extension of the trivial sheaf by itself with det(1 − Frob_x t) = (1 − t)² at every closed point, the same as the trivial rank-two sheaf.

Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5: K^C_{ℓ'} and L^C_{ℓ'} agree on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C, so their semisimplifications agree on C and the conjugacy classes ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ}) and ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ'}) coincide at the image y = ψ(x) of the point x ∈ C(F_q), which may lie outside U.
U = C recovers recognition at every closed point; the content is that points of C ∖ U are controlled by continuity.

sources.match: The curve recognition step, from equality on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C.
The reduction to a dense open subset of the curve.

nodes.title: The ℓ-adic Tate module of an abelian variety as a continuous Galois representation
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction to K^sep identifies it, as a topological group, with Gal(K^sep/K): Tau Ceti absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv; Mathlib gives Field.absoluteGaloisGroup only its group and topological-group structure, and compactness is obtained through this isomorphism); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. For n ≥ 0 put A[ℓ^n] := ker([ℓ^n] : A → A) ([ℓ^n] is Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.mulBy), a finite étale K-group scheme of order ℓ^{2gn} (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3), and A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K̄) its group of geometric points, with the transition maps [ℓ] : A[ℓ^{n+1}](K^sep) → A[ℓ^n](K^sep). Define T_ℓA := lim_n A[ℓ^n](K^sep), with the inverse-limit topology of the discrete finite groups, V_ℓA := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Q_ℓ, and the prime-to-char K adelic module T̂A := lim_N A[N](K^sep) (N invertible in K) = ∏_{ℓ ≠ char K} T_ℓA. Then: (a) each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is a free Z/ℓ^n-module of rank 2g, the transition maps are surjective, and T_ℓA is a free Z_ℓ-module (Z_ℓ is Mathlib's PadicInt ℓ) of rank 2g whose inverse-limit topology is the ℓ-adic topology (equivalently Mathlib's module topology, IsModuleTopology Z_ℓ); (b) the projection induces a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism T_ℓA/ℓ^n T_ℓA ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep); (c) G_K acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA through its coordinatewise action on A[ℓ^n](K̄), the action map G_K × T_ℓA → T_ℓA is jointly continuous, and so (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) is an object of ContinuousRep G_K Z_ℓ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation) of rank 2g, with V_ℓA its coefficient extension to Q_ℓ; (d) the kernel of G_K → Aut(A[ℓ^n](K^sep)) is the open subgroup G_{K(A[ℓ^n])} fixing the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]) generated by the coordinates of the ℓ^n-torsion points, and ρ_{A,ℓ} factors through Gal(K(A[ℓ^∞])/K); (e) the construction is made for every algebraic closure of K, and a K-isomorphism ι : K̄ → K̄′ of algebraic closures induces the group isomorphism G_K ≅ Aut(K̄′/K), σ ↦ ισι^{−1}, and a Z_ℓ-isomorphism T_ℓA ≅ T′_ℓA intertwining the two actions; this isomorphism is not canonical: replacing ι by ι∘τ with τ ∈ G_K composes it with x ↦ τx and the group isomorphism with conjugation by τ, so (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) is determined up to the inner automorphisms of G_K. A choice of Z_ℓ-basis gives the framed form ρ_{A,ℓ} : G_K → GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (R01.1/framed-representation), well defined up to GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ)-conjugacy. The Tate module is covariant in A. It is not defined for ℓ = char K (there A[ℓ](K^sep) has order at most ℓ^g).
hypotheses: K any field; ℓ a prime different from char K (for ℓ = char K the construction is not made: A[ℓ](K^sep) has order ≤ ℓ^g)
A an abelian variety over K of dimension g in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety)
torsion points are taken over K^sep (equivalently K̄), never over K
G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K (automorphisms of AlgebraicClosure K) with the Krull topology
proofSteps: Order and étaleness: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 proves [n] finite locally free of rank n^{2g} and étale when n is invertible on the base; over K with ℓ ≠ char K, A[ℓ^n] is finite étale of order ℓ^{2gn}, so #A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = ℓ^{2gn} and the K^sep- and K̄-points agree (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).
Structure: applying the count to every m | ℓ^n and the structure theorem for finite abelian groups gives A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ (Z/ℓ^n)^{2g} (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).

Surjective transitions: [ℓ] : A → A is a finite étale surjective isogeny (A3), so every K^sep-point of A[ℓ^n] lifts to a K^sep-point of A[ℓ^{n+1}]; the inverse limit of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g along surjections reducing compatibly is free of rank 2g over Z_ℓ with T_ℓA/ℓ^n ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep) (Milne AV, Proposition 10.5, p. 45).

Galois action: σ ∈ G_K acts on A(K̄) through the functoriality of points along the K-automorphism σ (coordinates); it commutes with [ℓ^n], so preserves A[ℓ^n](K̄) and commutes with the transition maps; hence it acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA.

Continuity: each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is finite and pointwise defined over the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]), so the action on it factors through the finite quotient Gal(K(A[ℓ^n])/K) and is continuous for the discrete topology (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); joint continuity on the inverse limit follows level by level, and the module topology on the finite free Z_ℓ-module T_ℓA is its inverse-limit topology.

Independence of choices: an isomorphism of algebraic closures over K transports torsion points and Galois actions compatibly; this is the transport-of-structure argument of R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist applied to the isomorphism of profinite groups it induces.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve (g = 1) the construction recovers Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's T_ℓE, free of rank 2 (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).

For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, E[2](Q̄) = {O, (0,0), (1,0), (−1,0)} consists of rational points, so T_2E/2T_2E ≅ (Z/2)² with trivial G_Q-action, while ρ_{E,2} itself is nontrivial (its determinant is χ_2, node determinant-and-oddness).

The analogous construction for the multiplicative group, lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K^sep), is the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1) of R01.1/tate-twist, with G_K acting through the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter): this is the χ_ℓ example of the roadmap.

nodes.title: Finite torsion, the residual representation and rational cyclic isogenies
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) For every n ≥ 1 the G_K-module T_ℓA/ℓ^nT_ℓA is canonically isomorphic to A[ℓ^n](K^sep) with its pointwise action; in particular the residual representation ρ̄_{A,ℓ} := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} F_ℓ (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification) is the G_K-module A[ℓ](K^sep) of dimension 2g over F_ℓ. (b) For every G_K-stable Z_ℓ-lattice Λ ⊂ V_ℓA, (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ A[ℓ](K^sep)^ss as F_ℓ[G_K]-modules (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence). (c) Let E be an elliptic curve over K (Weierstrass, IsElliptic). The G_K-stable F_ℓ-lines L ⊂ E[ℓ](K^sep) are exactly the K-rational cyclic subgroups of order ℓ, i.e. the kernels of the cyclic K-rational isogenies of degree ℓ out of E (the quotient E → E/L of the Weierstrass curve by a finite Galois-stable subgroup of points, given by Vélu's formulas in Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1); so ρ̄_{E,ℓ} is reducible over F_ℓ iff E admits a K-rational isogeny of degree ℓ. On such a line G_K acts through a character ψ : G_K → F_ℓ^×, and on the quotient E[ℓ]/L through χ̄_ℓ ψ^{−1} (node determinant-and-oddness); For ℓ odd ψ need not be trivial, so reducibility of ρ̄_{E,ℓ} does not imply that E has a K-rational point of order ℓ. For ℓ = 2 the group F_2^× is trivial, so every G_K-stable line in E[2](K^sep) is generated by a K-rational point of order 2, and ρ̄_{E,2} is reducible iff E has a K-rational point of order 2.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
in (c), the line L is a subgroup of the K^sep-points; its K-rationality means stability under G_K, not pointwise rationality
in (c), the non-triviality of ψ is asserted for ℓ odd only; for ℓ = 2 every stable line is spanned by a K-rational point
proofSteps: (a) is part (b) of node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety, restated for consumers; n = 1 is the comparison of the residual representation with the existing pointwise action requested by the stage.
(b) Λ and T_ℓA are both G_K-stable lattices in V_ℓA; R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence gives (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ (T_ℓA/ℓT_ℓA)^ss, and (a) identifies the latter.

(c) E[ℓ](K̄) has ℓ² elements (already in the pinned library: TauCeti.Isogeny.card_ker_mulByIntIsogeny over the algebraically closed K̄, with mem_ker_mulByIntIsogeny_iff identifying the kernel of [ℓ] with the ℓ-torsion), and Layer 2 gives its structure (Z/ℓ)². A G_K-stable line L is a finite G_K-stable subgroup of E(K^sep); Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 constructs the quotient isogeny E → E/L by Vélu's formulas, defined over K, separable of degree ℓ with kernel L. Conversely an isogeny of degree ℓ defined over K is separable (ℓ ≠ char K) and its kernel is a subgroup of order ℓ of E(K^sep) stable under G_K (Layer 1), i.e. a G_K-stable line of E[ℓ](K^sep). The character ψ is the action on L ≅ F_ℓ; the quotient character follows from det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ (node determinant-and-oddness).

Non-triviality of ψ (ℓ odd): let L/K be a separable quadratic extension with quadratic character ε_L (Tau Ceti Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.quadraticCharacter) and E^L = WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist E L. Tau Ceti's quadraticTwistPointEquiv gives an additive isomorphism E^L(K̄) ≅ E(K̄), and quadraticTwistPointEquiv_map_eq_quadraticCharacter_smul_map says that it carries the action of σ ∈ G_K to ε_L(σ|_L)·σ. Restricting to ℓ-torsion: E^L[ℓ] ≅ E[ℓ] ⊗ ε_L, so E and E^L have the same stable lines and ψ is replaced by ψ·ε_L. A rational point of order ℓ on E (ψ = 1) gives ψ = ε_L ≠ 1 on E^L. For ℓ = 2 the character ε_L is trivial mod 2 and nothing changes. The library twists by a separable quadratic extension, in every characteristic, not by an element d.
acceptance: The curve 11a3, y² + y = x³ − x², has a rational point (0, 0) of order 5, so ρ̄_{E,5} has a stable line with trivial character ψ = 1 and quotient character χ̄_5 (Δ = −11).

Its quadratic twist by d = −1 still has a G_Q-stable line in E[5] (the twist of the same line) but its character is the nontrivial character ε_{−1} of Q(i)/Q, so the twisted curve has a rational 5-isogeny but no rational point of order 5 in that line.
For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, ρ̄_{E,2} is trivial (all of E[2] is rational) and every line in E[2] is G_Q-stable: three rational 2-isogenies.

nodes.title: Comparison with the Tate module of a Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, W a Weierstrass curve over K with [W.IsElliptic], E_W the elliptic curve it defines (the projective closure of W.toAffine, an abelian variety of dimension 1 whose L-points are W⁄L.Point functorially in the field L/K), and ℓ a prime ≠ char K. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2 constructs E[N] = Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point N ≃+ (ZMod N)² (the count #E[N] = N² over an algebraically closed field is already in the pinned library, TauCeti.Isogeny.card_ker_mulByIntIsogeny), the Weil pairing e_N valued in rootsOfUnity N K^sep, the Tate module T_ℓW := lim E[ℓ^n] with its continuous G_K-representation into Module.Aut Z_ℓ (T_ℓW) and det = χ_ℓ. Then the identification E_W(K^sep) = (W⁄K^sep).Point induces, for every n, a G_K-equivariant group isomorphism E_W[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point ℓ^n compatible with the transition maps, hence an isomorphism T_ℓ(E_W) ≅ T_ℓW of continuous Z_ℓ[G_K]-modules, under which: (i) the point map W₁(K^sep) → W₂(K^sep) of a Tau Ceti isogeny φ : TauCeti.Isogeny W₁ W₂ (a milestone of EllipticCurves Layer 1, named toPointHom there; the pinned library has the isogeny type, its degree and its kernel, but no point map yet) corresponds to T_ℓ of the induced homomorphism E_{W₁} → E_{W₂}; (ii) Tau Ceti's e_{ℓ^n} corresponds to the polarization pairing e^λ_{ℓ^n} of node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules for the canonical principal polarization λ = φ_{𝒪(O)} : E → E^∨, P ↦ t_P^*𝒪(O) ⊗ 𝒪(O)^{−1} = class of (O) − (P) (the opposite of the Abel–Jacobi identification P ↦ class of (P) − (O), which is φ of the inverse of an ample bundle and not a polarization). The sign is pinned by the formulas: with e_N(a, a′) = g/(g∘t_a) on geometric points (Milne AV §13, the normalisation requested from A3) and e_N(S, T) = g(X + S)/g(X) (AEC III.8.1, the normalisation of Layer 2), e^λ_N(S, T) = e_N(S, T) exactly, whereas e_N(S, class of (T) − (O)) = e_N(S, T)^{−1}; if either supplier pins the opposite normalisation the comparison lemma carries an inversion, and no other statement of this layer depends on the sign; (iii) the determinant theorem of Layer 2 and node determinant-and-oddness give the same character χ_ℓ. Consequently every statement of this layer about T_ℓA for abelian varieties applies to Tau Ceti's T_ℓW, and every Layer-2 statement about T_ℓW applies to T_ℓ(E_W).
hypotheses: W elliptic over a field K; ℓ ≠ char K

the identification of E_W with an abelian variety of dimension 1 together with E_W(L) = W⁄L.Point, natural in L, is imported from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1, whose stage text states the comparison of one-dimensional abelian schemes with elliptic curves through the Weierstrass presentation
proofSteps: Both inverse systems are built from the same groups: E_W(K^sep)[ℓ^n] and the ℓ^n-torsion submodule of (W⁄K^sep).Point coincide under the point identification, and multiplication by ℓ corresponds because the group laws coincide.

Galois equivariance: σ acts on both sides by acting on coordinates (Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ), so the identification is G_K-equivariant at each level and hence on the limits; continuity is level-wise on both sides.

Isogenies: a Tau Ceti isogeny is a coordinate-ring pullback; its point map (EllipticCurves Layer 1: ideal extension to the intermediate ring followed by the relative norm, additive by construction) is the map on points of the morphism of abelian varieties it defines under the identification of A1.

Weil pairing: over K^sep, let T ∈ E[N] and D = (T) − (O); choose f with div f = N·D and g with g^N = f ∘ [N], so that div g = [N]^*D. Milne's pairing (AV §13, the form of A3's pairing on geometric points) is e_N(S, class of D) = g/(g∘t_S) = g(X)/g(X + S), and the pairing of Tau Ceti Layer 2 (AEC III.8.1) is e_N(S, T) = g(X + S)/g(X); they are inverse to each other. Since λ(T) = class of (O) − (T) = −(class of D), bilinearity gives e^λ_N(S, T) = e_N(S, T). Compatibility in N passes this to the ℓ-adic pairings.
Determinant: both equal χ_ℓ since both pairings are perfect alternating and Galois-equivariant into Z_ℓ(1).
acceptance: For W : y² = x³ − x over Q, both constructions give the same mod-2 reduction: the four rational points O, (0,0), (±1,0), with trivial G_Q-action.

For the Tate curve E_q over a p-adic field with ℓ ≠ p, both constructions give the extension 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → Z_ℓ → 0 from Tau Ceti Layer 4's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) (node required-examples).

nodes.title: Functoriality: homomorphisms, products, isogenies and base change
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) Every homomorphism α : A → B of abelian varieties over K induces a Z_ℓ-linear G_K-equivariant map T_ℓα : T_ℓA → T_ℓB, (x_n) ↦ (α(x_n)); T_ℓ(id) = id, T_ℓ(βα) = T_ℓβ ∘ T_ℓα, T_ℓ(α + α′) = T_ℓα + T_ℓα′, so Hom_K(A, B) → Hom_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA, T_ℓB) is a group homomorphism and End_K(A) → End_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA) a ring homomorphism (End_K(A) is Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.End), which extends Z_ℓ-linearly to Hom_K(A, B) ⊗ Z_ℓ. (b) For the product A × B (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.prod), (T_ℓpr_1, T_ℓpr_2) : T_ℓ(A × B) → T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB is an isomorphism of continuous representations. (c) Let φ : A → B be an isogeny (finite surjective, Tau Ceti IsIsogeny) of degree d. Then T_ℓφ is injective and there is a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism coker(T_ℓφ) ≅ (ker φ)(K^sep)[ℓ^∞]; in particular #coker(T_ℓφ) = d_ℓ, the ℓ-part of d, and V_ℓφ : V_ℓA → V_ℓB is an isomorphism of Q_ℓ[G_K]-modules. If ℓ ∤ d, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and φ induces G_K-isomorphisms A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ B[ℓ^n](K^sep) for all n. If ψ : B → A satisfies ψφ = [m], then T_ℓψ ∘ T_ℓφ = m. (d) For a field extension L/K and a K-embedding j : K̄ → L̄ of algebraic closures, j induces bijections A[ℓ^n](K^sep) → A_L[ℓ^n](L^sep) (A[ℓ^n] is finite étale, so its geometric points do not change under an extension of separably closed fields), and the resulting Z_ℓ-isomorphism T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓ(A_L) intertwines ρ_{A_L,ℓ} with ρ_{A,ℓ} ∘ res_j, where res_j : G_L → G_K is restriction along j (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.baseChange). For L ⊆ K̄ algebraic over K this reads T_ℓ(A_L) = T_ℓA|_{G_L}; for a completion L = F_v of a number field F and an embedding j : F̄ → F̄_v, res_j is the embedding of G_{F_v} onto the decomposition group of the place of F̄ defined by j. (e) For a field isomorphism τ : K → K′ extended to τ̄ : K̄ → K̄′, transport of structure gives a Z_ℓ-isomorphism T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓ(A^τ) intertwining ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ) with ρ_{A^τ,ℓ}(τ̄στ̄^{−1}).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K
in (c) the degree d is the rank of the finite group scheme ker φ (its p-primary part may be infinitesimal in characteristic p; only its ℓ-primary part, which is étale, enters coker T_ℓφ)
in (d), Tau Ceti's AbelianVariety.baseChange takes L in the same universe as K; algebraic closures and completions of K satisfy this
proofSteps: (a) α commutes with [ℓ^n] and with the Galois action on coordinates; additivity holds level-wise because the group law on Hom(A, B) is pointwise (Milne AV, §10, p. 45).
(b) A × B represents the product functor on points, so (A × B)[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K^sep) × B[ℓ^n](K^sep) compatibly with transitions and Galois.

(c) Put G = ker φ, a finite K-group scheme of order d (A3). On K^sep-points, 0 → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → A[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → B[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → 0 is exact (φ is surjective on K̄-points; if φ(a) = b with b of ℓ-power order then a is torsion and its ℓ-primary component is again a preimage of b; ℓ-power torsion points are K^sep-rational; and A[ℓ^∞](K^sep) is divisible. Surjectivity of A(K^sep) → B(K^sep) itself fails for an inseparable isogeny over an imperfect field and is not used). Applying the snake lemma to multiplication by ℓ^n and passing to the limit (Hom(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ, −) is left exact and G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] is finite, so T_ℓG = 0) gives 0 → T_ℓA → T_ℓB → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → 0. The ℓ-primary part of G is étale since ℓ is invertible, so its order is d_ℓ (Milne AV, proof of Proposition 10.20, p. 52, uses exactly #Coker(T_ℓβ) = #Ker(β)(ℓ)).

The quasi-inverse: the kernel G of φ is killed by its order m = d (a finite commutative group scheme is killed by its order; "exponent" has no meaning for a non-étale G), so [m] factors through A/G ≅ B and ψ exists with ψφ = [m] (A3, isogenies and quotients); then T_ℓψ T_ℓφ = T_ℓ[m] = m; hence V_ℓφ is invertible (Milne AV Ch. IV, Corollary 3.6, p. 142).
(d) and (e) are transport of structure, using R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist for the restricted and conjugated representations.
acceptance: For the 5-isogeny φ : E = 11a3 → E′ with kernel the rational subgroup ⟨(0,0)⟩, T_5φ is injective with cokernel Z/5 and V_5φ is an isomorphism; for ℓ ≠ 5, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and E[ℓ] ≅ E′[ℓ] as G_Q-modules.
For [m] : A → A, coker T_ℓ[m] = T_ℓA/m T_ℓA ≅ A[m](K^sep)[ℓ^∞] has order m_ℓ^{2g} = (ℓ-part of deg [m] = m^{2g}).
For A = E_1 × E_2 a product of elliptic curves, T_ℓA = T_ℓE_1 ⊕ T_ℓE_2 has rank 4 and det = χ_ℓ² (node determinant-and-oddness).

nodes.title: The Weil pairing on Tate modules, polarization pairings and the similitude character
nodes.statement: Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let A^∨ be the dual abelian variety and Z_ℓ(1) = lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K̄) the Tate twist (R01.1/tate-twist; μ_{ℓ^n}(K̄) is Mathlib's rootsOfUnity (ℓ^n) K̄, and it lies in K^sep because ℓ ≠ char K), on which G_K acts through χ_ℓ = cyclotomicCharacter K̄ ℓ. From A3's perfect Weil pairings e_{ℓ^n} : A[ℓ^n] × A^∨[ℓ^n] → μ_{ℓ^n}, which satisfy e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′), define e_ℓ : T_ℓA × T_ℓA^∨ → Z_ℓ(1), e_ℓ((a_n), (a′_n)) := (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n))_n. Then e_ℓ is Z_ℓ-bilinear, perfect (it induces an isomorphism T_ℓA^∨ ≅ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(T_ℓA, Z_ℓ(1)) = (T_ℓA)^∨(1) of continuous representations, R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist) and Galois-equivariant: e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y) for σ ∈ G_K, writing Z_ℓ(1) additively. For a homomorphism λ : A → A^∨ put e^λ_ℓ(x, y) := e_ℓ(x, T_ℓλ(y)). Properties: (i) adjunction e_ℓ(x, T_ℓα^∨(y)) = e_ℓ(T_ℓα(x), y) for α : A → B, x ∈ T_ℓA, y ∈ T_ℓB^∨; (ii) if λ = φ_L for a line bundle L (in particular if λ is a polarization), e^λ_ℓ is alternating; (iii) for a polarization λ of degree d, e^λ_ℓ ⊗ Q_ℓ is nondegenerate, and e^λ_ℓ is perfect over Z_ℓ iff ℓ ∤ d (always when λ is principal); (iv) for α ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q and the Rosati involution α ↦ α^† of λ (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2/rosati-involution, which states this adjunction; it is cited, not planned again), e^λ_ℓ(αx, y) = e^λ_ℓ(x, α^†y) on V_ℓA; (v) for polarizations λ, μ of A, B, e^{λ×μ}_ℓ is the orthogonal sum on T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB; (vi) consequently every ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ) preserves e^λ_ℓ up to the scalar χ_ℓ(σ): e^λ_ℓ(ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ)x, ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ)y) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e^λ_ℓ(x, y) for all x, y in T_ℓA, and likewise on V_ℓA. So G_K acts on the nondegenerate alternating space (V_ℓA, e^λ_ℓ) by similitudes with similitude character (multiplier) χ_ℓ, and on the lattice T_ℓA, on which e^λ_ℓ is perfect exactly when ℓ ∤ deg λ (in particular for principal λ). Reducing mod ℓ^n recovers A3's pairings e_{ℓ^n} and e^λ_{ℓ^n}.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ char K

the dual abelian variety, φ_L and polarizations are imported from Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer E; the finite-level pairings e_{ℓ^n} and e^λ_{ℓ^n}, their compatibility in n, alternation and the perfectness criterion are AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3's; the Rosati involution is AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2/rosati-involution; this node passes to the limit on the Tate module of node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety and states the result for continuous representations
the target keeps the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1); it is never identified with Z_ℓ without a chosen compatible system of roots of unity
proofSteps: Compatibility of levels: e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′) (Milne AV Lemma 13.1, p. 57; A3 for the scheme-theoretic pairing), so the sequence (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n)) is an element of lim μ_{ℓ^n} = Z_ℓ(1).
Perfectness: each e_{ℓ^n} is perfect (A3, Cartier duality A^∨[n] = A[n]^D), and a compatible system of perfect pairings of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g gives a perfect pairing of the limits.

Galois equivariance: A3's pairing is a morphism of K-group schemes, so e_{ℓ^n}(σa, σa′) = σ(e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)) = e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} by Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.spec, whose instance hypothesis (K̄ has enough ℓ^i-th roots of unity for every i) is Mathlib's AlgebraicClosure.hasEnoughRootsOfUnity_pow, available because ℓ ≠ char K.

(i), (ii), (iv): Milne AV Proposition 13.2 (a)–(d), p. 58; (iv) is the adjunction stated by AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2/rosati-involution (from (i) and α^† = λ^{−1}α^∨λ: e(αx, λy) = e(x, α^∨λy) = e(x, λα^†y)). For (ii) at ℓ = 2: Proposition 13.2(d) gives a homomorphism to Hom(∧²T_ℓA, Z_ℓ(1)), i.e. e^L_ℓ(x, x) = 0; skew-symmetry alone gives 2e(x, x) = 0, which suffices because Z_ℓ(1) is torsion-free.
(iii): ker(T_ℓλ ⊗ Q_ℓ) = 0 because λ is an isogeny (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (c)); over Z_ℓ the discriminant of e^λ_ℓ is #coker T_ℓλ = d_ℓ.
(vi): from equivariance, e^λ_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ) e^λ_ℓ(x, y), which is the definition of a similitude with multiplier χ_ℓ(σ).

(v): under (A × B)^∨ = A^∨ × B^∨ the pairing e_ℓ of A × B is the orthogonal sum of those of A and B, by (i) applied to the two inclusions and the two projections; node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (b) identifies T_ℓ(A × B), and λ × μ is the product homomorphism.
acceptance: χ_ℓ example: for an elliptic curve, the polarization pairing e_ℓ : T_ℓE × T_ℓE → Z_ℓ(1) is perfect alternating, so ∧²T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ(1) and det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's determinant theorem).

For E : y² = x³ − x over Q and ℓ = 2, the mod-2 pairing on E[2] = {O, P_1, P_2, P_3} takes the value −1 on every pair of distinct nonzero points and 1 on the diagonal: it is alternating and nondegenerate on (Z/2)².
For a polarization λ = [ℓ]∘λ_0 (λ_0 principal), e^λ_ℓ = ℓ·e^{λ_0}_ℓ is nondegenerate over Q_ℓ but not perfect over Z_ℓ (discriminant divisible by ℓ^{2g}).
