nodes.title: Tensor induction from an open subgroup (Asai representation in index two)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ an open subgroup of index m, A a topological commutative ring and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep H A V of rank n. Choose a left transversal t_1,…,t_m of Γ/H and let Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m be the monomial homomorphism, g t_i = t_{π_g(i)} h_i(g) with h_i(g) ∈ H (ProfiniteCohomology layer 13, milestones 1–2). The tensor induction ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ is V^{⊗m} = ⨂_{i=1}^m V with g acting by g·(v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_m) = ⊗_i ρ(h_i(g)) v_{i} placed in slot π_g(i). It is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^m; a different transversal gives a canonically isomorphic representation; it is functorial, multiplicative (⊗-Ind(ρ ⊗ ρ′) ≅ ⊗-Ind ρ ⊗ ⊗-Ind ρ′), compatible with coefficient extension and transitive in towers. If H is normal, its restriction to H is ⊗_{i} ρ^{t_i} (with ρ^{t}(h) = ρ(t^{-1} h t)). Trace formula: for g ∈ Γ with cycles C_1,…,C_r of π_g on Γ/H, of lengths ℓ_j and starting coset t_{i_j}H, tr(⊗-Ind ρ)(g) = ∏_j tr ρ(t_{i_j}^{−1} g^{ℓ_j} t_{i_j}). Characteristic polynomial (V free of rank n): put B_j := ρ(t_{i_j}^{−1} g^{ℓ_j} t_{i_j}). Along the cycles V^{⊗m} = ⨂_j V^{⊗ℓ_j}, and (⊗-Ind ρ)(g) is the tensor product over j of the cyclically permuted operators of G7/charpoly-of-cyclically-permuted-tensor-product; hence det(X − (⊗-Ind ρ)(g)) is a universal polynomial in the coefficients of the det(X − B_j), whose roots are the products λ_1⋯λ_r with λ_j running over the roots of C_{n,ℓ_j}(c(B_j); X). For g in the intersection of the conjugates of H (all ℓ_j = 1) these are the products of one root of det(X − ρ(t_i^{−1}gt_i)) for each i. For m = 2: if g ∈ G_K, det(X − ρ(g)) = ∏_i (X − α_i) and det(X − ρ(σ^{−1}gσ)) = ∏_j (X − α′_j), then det(X − As(ρ)(g)) = ∏_{i,j}(X − α_iα′_j); if g ∉ G_K and det(X − ρ(g^2)) = ∏_i (X − β_i), then det(X − As(ρ)(g)) = ∏_i (X − β_i)·∏_{i<j}(X^2 − β_iβ_j). For m = 2, H = G_K ⊂ G_F = Γ (K/F quadratic), As(ρ) := ⊗-Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ is the Asai representation: As(ρ)|_{G_K} ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^σ, and As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} is a second extension of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ to G_F (the only other one, up to isomorphism, when A is a field and ρ ⊗ ρ^σ is absolutely irreducible).
hypotheses: H open (so of finite index); no invertibility hypothesis on A
the isomorphism class is independent of the transversal, the representation on a fixed model is not

As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} is a second extension of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ to G_F; when A is a field and ρ ⊗ ρ^σ is absolutely irreducible these are the only two up to isomorphism. They can be isomorphic (2 = 0 in A, or ρ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ for a character χ of G_K with χ ∘ Ver = η_{K/F}). Sources that do not distinguish them must say so.
proofSteps: Monomial homomorphism Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m and its continuity for open H: ProfiniteCohomology layer 13 milestones 1–2 (requested); the action of the permutation wreath product H^m ⋊ S_m on V^{⊗m} (factors permuted, H^m acting factorwise) is a group action because the place-permutation action of S_m on PiTensorProduct commutes appropriately with ⊗_i ρ(h_i).

Change of transversal: G7/tensor-induction-independent-of-transversal (the cocycle identity for the h_i, the intertwiner ⨂ρ(u_i)^{−1}, and its compatibility with composition, which makes the identification canonical).
Continuity: the matrix entries of ⊗-Ind ρ(g) are products of entries of ρ(h_i(g)), and g ↦ (h_i(g), π_g) is locally constant in π and continuous in h because H is open.

Restriction to normal H: compute Φ_t on H (π_h = id, h_i(h) = t_i^{−1}ht_i). Trace and characteristic polynomial: the cycles of π_g decompose V^{⊗m} as a tensor product over the cycles, and on the factor of a cycle (i, π_g(i), …) of length ℓ the operator (⊗-Ind ρ)(g) is the operator T of G7/charpoly-of-cyclically-permuted-tensor-product with the maps ρ(h_i(g)) along the cycle; their product along the cycle is ρ(t_i^{−1}g^ℓt_i), the element that also appears in Mathlib's cycle formula for the transfer (MonoidHom.transfer_eq_prod_quotient_orbitRel_zpowers_quot). Parts (1) and (2) of the lemma give the trace and characteristic polynomial on each factor, and part (4) those of the tensor product over the cycles.
Asai case m = 2: As(ρ)|_{G_K} = ρ ⊗ ρ^σ by the restriction formula; the action of a lift of σ is the swap composed with ρ(σ^2) in one factor, as in CG20's explicit realisation.
acceptance: CG20, proof of Example 4.11 (pp. 818–819): for K/Q imaginary quadratic, p > 2 and ρ : G_K → GL_2(F_p) with det ρ = ε^{1−k}, the symplectic induction r = Ind_K^Q ρ with similitude ν ∈ {ε^{1−k}, ε^{1−k}η_{K/Q}} (G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction) satisfies sp(r) ≅ Sym^2(r) ⊗ ν^{−1} ≅ As(ρ) ⊗ ν^{−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ), where As is the tensor induction of this node for the transversal {1, σ}: on V·σV ⊂ Sym^2(V ⊕ σV) the element σ sends v·σv′ to ρ(σ^2)v′·σv. CG20 print ad⁰(r̄) = As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰(ρ̄) and do not distinguish As from its quadratic twist; their ad⁰(r̄) is sp_4 (rank 10), not the trace kernel of gl_4. On As = V ⊗ V the swap composed with g ⊗ h, g = diag(x, x^{−1}), h = diag(y, y^{−1}), has eigenvalues xy, (xy)^{−1}, 1, −1.

BCGP21 §7.5.16 (characteristic ≠ 2): let G ⊂ Sp_4(k) be absolutely irreducible, H ⊂ G of index two with quadratic character χ, and W|_H = V ⊕ V^σ with the symplectic form non-degenerate on V (equivalently det V = 1; the source does not state this hypothesis, sourceIssues E720). Then Sym^2 W ≅ Ind_H^G(ad⁰ V) ⊕ As(V) and ∧^2 W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ.
Degenerate: for m = 1, ⊗-Ind_Γ^Γ ρ = ρ; for V = A the trivial rank-one representation, ⊗-Ind V is trivial; for a character ψ of H, ⊗-Ind ψ = ψ ∘ Ver_{Γ→H} (the transfer).

nodes.title: Tensor induction does not depend on the transversal
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a group, H ≤ Γ a subgroup of finite index, A a commutative ring and ρ : H → GL_A(V) a representation on an A-module V. For a left transversal t = (t_x)_{x ∈ Γ/H} (t_x ∈ x) write g·t_x = t_{gx}·h^t_x(g) with h^t_x(g) ∈ H, and let Ind^⊗_t ρ be the action of Γ on ⨂_{x ∈ Γ/H} V given on pure tensors by g·(⊗_x v_x) = ⊗_x w_x with w_{gx} = ρ(h^t_x(g))v_x. Then: (1) h^t_x(g′g) = h^t_{gx}(g′)·h^t_x(g), so Ind^⊗_t ρ is a representation of Γ. (2) For a second transversal t′_x = t_x u_x (u_x ∈ H) the A-linear automorphism T_{t,t′} := ⨂_x ρ(u_x)^{−1} of ⨂_x V satisfies T_{t,t′} ∘ (Ind^⊗_t ρ)(g) = (Ind^⊗_{t′} ρ)(g) ∘ T_{t,t′} for all g ∈ Γ. (3) T_{t,t} = id and T_{t′,t″} ∘ T_{t,t′} = T_{t,t″}. Hence the representations Ind^⊗_t ρ are identified by a compatible system of isomorphisms, and ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ is defined up to unique isomorphism. If Γ is profinite, H open and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep H A V, each T_{t,t′} is an isomorphism in ContinuousRep Γ A.
hypotheses: the tensor product is indexed by the cosets Γ/H, so that no ordering of the transversal is chosen
no hypothesis on A or V for (1)–(3); finite projective V and the module topology only for the last sentence
proofSteps: (1): g′g·t_x = g′·t_{gx}h^t_x(g) = t_{g′gx}·h^t_{gx}(g′)h^t_x(g); the action on pure tensors extends to ⨂_x V by PiTensorProduct.map composed with the reindexing along x ↦ gx, and (1) is the homomorphism property.

(2): g·t′_x = g·t_x u_x = t_{gx}h^t_x(g)u_x = t′_{gx}·u_{gx}^{−1}h^t_x(g)u_x, so h^{t′}_x(g) = u_{gx}^{−1}h^t_x(g)u_x. On a pure tensor, the gx-component of T_{t,t′}(g·_t ⊗v_x) is ρ(u_{gx})^{−1}ρ(h^t_x(g))v_x, and the gx-component of g·_{t′}T_{t,t′}(⊗v_x) is ρ(h^{t′}_x(g))ρ(u_x)^{−1}v_x = ρ(u_{gx}^{−1}h^t_x(g))v_x; they agree, and pure tensors span.
(3): the elements u_x for (t, t″) are the products of those for (t, t′) and (t′, t″), and ρ is a homomorphism.
Continuity: T_{t,t′} is A-linear between finite modules carrying the module topology, hence continuous (R01.1/continuous-representation).
acceptance: Index two, Γ = H ⊔ σH: for the transversals (1, σ) and (1, σh_0) the map id ⊗ ρ(h_0)^{−1} intertwines the two models of the Asai representation.

For a character ψ of H, T_{t,t′} is multiplication by ∏_x ψ(u_x)^{−1}, which commutes with everything: both models of ⊗-Ind ψ are the same character ψ ∘ Ver, the independence of the transfer from the transversal.
Index one (Γ = H), transversals (1) and (h_0): Ind^⊗_{(h_0)} ρ(g) = ρ(h_0^{−1}gh_0) and T = ρ(h_0)^{−1} intertwines ρ with it.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomials of tensor products and of cyclically permuted tensor products of linear maps
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, ℓ ≥ 1, V_1,…,V_ℓ free R-modules of the same finite rank n, and A_i : V_i → V_{i+1} (indices modulo ℓ) R-linear maps. Let T be the endomorphism of V_1 ⊗ … ⊗ V_ℓ with T(v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_ℓ) = A_ℓv_ℓ ⊗ A_1v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ A_{ℓ−1}v_{ℓ−1}, and let B = A_ℓ ∘ … ∘ A_1 ∈ End_R(V_1). Then (1) tr T = tr B. (2) There is a polynomial C_{n,ℓ} ∈ Z[c_1,…,c_n][X], monic of degree n^ℓ in X, with det(X − T) = C_{n,ℓ}(c_1(B),…,c_n(B); X), where det(X − B) = X^n − c_1(B)X^{n−1} + … ; it is characterised by C_{n,ℓ}(e_1(β),…,e_n(β); X) = ∏_O (X^{|O|} − β_O), the product over the orbits O of the cyclic shift on {1,…,n}^ℓ, with β_O = β_{j_1}⋯β_{j_d} for an orbit of size d containing (j_1,…,j_ℓ). In particular C_{n,1} = det(X − B) and C_{n,2}(e(β); X) = ∏_i (X − β_i)·∏_{i<j}(X^2 − β_iβ_j). (3) For V_1 = … = V_ℓ = V this is the characteristic polynomial of c ∘ (A_1 ⊗ … ⊗ A_ℓ), c the cyclic permutation v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_ℓ ↦ v_ℓ ⊗ v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_{ℓ−1} of V^{⊗ℓ}. (4) For free modules V, V′ of finite ranks n, n′ and endomorphisms A of V, A′ of V′: tr(A ⊗ A′) = tr A·tr A′ and det(X − A ⊗ A′) = P_{n,n′}(c(A), c(A′); X) for a polynomial P_{n,n′} with integer coefficients characterised by P_{n,n′}(e(α), e(α′); X) = ∏_{i,j}(X − α_iα′_j).
hypotheses: free modules of finite rank (LinearMap.charpoly and LinearMap.trace need a finite basis)
the A_i need not be invertible and B need not be diagonalisable; the identity is universal
proofSteps: Reduction to the generic case: both sides of (2) are polynomials with integer coefficients in the entries of the matrices of A_1,…,A_ℓ, so it suffices to prove (2) over an algebraically closed field Ω in which the A_i are invertible and B has n distinct eigenvalues β_1,…,β_n (the generic matrices over Z[x^{(i)}_{jk}] have this property over an algebraic closure of the fraction field: specialise A_2 = … = A_ℓ = 1 and A_1 diagonal with distinct entries), and then to specialise the entries of the matrices.

Adapted bases: let v_1,…,v_n be an eigenbasis of B, Bv_j = β_jv_j, and w^{(i)}_j = A_{i−1}⋯A_1v_j, a basis of V_i. Then A_iw^{(i)}_j = w^{(i+1)}_j for i < ℓ and A_ℓw^{(ℓ)}_j = β_jw^{(1)}_j, so on the basis e_j = w^{(1)}_{j_1} ⊗ … ⊗ w^{(ℓ)}_{j_ℓ} (j ∈ {1,…,n}^ℓ) one has Te_j = β_{j_ℓ}·e_{s(j)} with s(j) = (j_ℓ, j_1,…,j_{ℓ−1}).

T is a monomial matrix for the permutation s, so det(X − T) is the product over the orbits O of s of X^{|O|} − ∏_{j ∈ O} β_{j_ℓ}; for an orbit of size d the last coordinates of its d elements are j_1,…,j_d in some order. The trace is the sum over the fixed points j = (i,…,i), that is Σ_i β_i = tr B; (1) for arbitrary A_i follows by specialisation.
The right-hand side of (2) is symmetric in the β_i, hence a polynomial in the e_k(β) = c_k(B) (MvPolynomial.esymmAlgHom_fin_bijective).

(4): the same reduction to generic matrices; for A, A′ diagonalisable with eigenbases (v_i), (v′_j), the v_i ⊗ v′_j form an eigenbasis of A ⊗ A′ with eigenvalues α_iα′_j, and the product is symmetric in the α_i and in the α′_j separately.
acceptance: ℓ = 2, A_1 = A_2 = 1: T is the swap on V ⊗ V, with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^{n(n+1)/2}(X + 1)^{n(n−1)/2} and trace n.

ℓ = 2, n = 2, A_1 = g = diag(x, x^{−1}), A_2 = h = diag(y, y^{−1}) (CG20, proof of Example 4.11): B = hg has eigenvalues xy and (xy)^{−1}, and det(X − T) = (X − xy)(X − (xy)^{−1})(X^2 − 1): eigenvalues xy, (xy)^{−1}, 1, −1.
(4) for n = n′ = 2: det(X − A ⊗ A′) has constant term (det A)^2(det A′)^2 and the coefficient of X^3 is −tr A·tr A′.

sources.locator: §4, proof of Example 4.11, p. 15 (published text p. 819)
sources.match: CG20 compute the eigenvalues of the swap composed with g ⊗ h on V ⊗ V; this is the case ℓ = 2, n = 2 of the lemma.

nodes.title: Restriction of scalars of the coefficients
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a continuous homomorphism of topological commutative rings making B a finite projective A-module of constant rank r with the module topology (B's topology is the A-module topology), and let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ B M of rank n. The restriction of scalars Res_{B/A} ρ is M regarded as an A-module with the same action; it is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank rn. Characteristic polynomials (in the sense of R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial: Mathlib's LinearMap.charpoly when the module is free, and defined Zariski-locally on the coefficient ring in general, since LinearMap.charpoly takes Module.Free and Module.Finite as instance arguments): det_A(X − ρ(g) | M) = N_{B[X]/A[X]}(det_B(X − ρ(g) | M)). If B is étale over A and A → A′ splits B (B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_{σ ∈ Hom_A(B, A′)} A′), then (Res_{B/A} ρ) ⊗_A A′ ≅ ⊕_σ ρ ⊗_{B,σ} A′. For finite extensions E′/E of coefficient fields finite over Q_ℓ, Res_{E′/E} is the forgetful functor from E′-linear to E-linear continuous representations. Restriction of scalars along the base field (an abelian variety Res_{L/K} A) is not this construction: on Galois representations it is induction (R01.1/continuous-induction).
hypotheses: B finite projective over A with the A-module topology (true for finite extensions of complete DVRs and of finite fields)
the norm formula uses B[X] finite projective over A[X]
the splitting statement needs B étale over A
proofSteps: The A-module M is finite projective since B is finite projective over A. Topology (a lemma of this node): choose a B-linear surjection B^k → M; it is a quotient map for the B-module topology, B^k carries the A-module topology (finite products of B), and an A-linear surjection from a module with the A-module topology onto M induces the A-module topology on M (IsModuleTopology for quotients). Hence the B-module and A-module topologies on M agree and joint continuity is unchanged.

Norm formula: for B free over A and M free over B, Mathlib LinearMap.det_restrictScalars gives det_A(f) = N_{B/A}(det_B f); apply it to M[X] over B[X] over A[X] and f = X − ρ(g). In general localise at the primes of A: B becomes free and semilocal, and M, finite projective of constant rank over a semilocal ring, becomes free.
Splitting: B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_σ A′ gives M ⊗_A A′ ≅ M ⊗_B (B ⊗_A A′) ≅ ⊕_σ M ⊗_{B,σ} A′, Γ-equivariantly.
acceptance: For E′ = Q_ℓ(√u) unramified quadratic over E = Q_ℓ and a character ψ : Γ → E′^×, Res_{E′/E} ψ is two-dimensional with characteristic polynomial X^2 − Tr(ψ(g))X + N(ψ(g)), and after extending scalars to E′ it is ψ ⊕ ψ^{Frob}.
For A = B the construction is the identity; for B = A^r (r copies) Res is the direct sum of the r components.

uses.how: changing the coefficient field of a compatible system: an E′-valued member viewed over E
contrast: base-field Weil restriction corresponds to induction, supplied by R01.1/continuous-induction

nodes.title: The adjoint representation, the trace kernel and the quotient by scalars
nodes.statement: Let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank n ≥ 1. (i) ad ρ is End_A(M) with g·X = ρ(g) X ρ(g)^{−1} (Mathlib Representation.linHom ρ ρ), an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^2, canonically ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^∨. (ii) The scalars A·1 ⊂ ad ρ form a trivial subrepresentation; the quotient ad ρ / A·1 (the pgl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iii) The trace tr : ad ρ → A is the contraction: under the isomorphism M^∨ ⊗_A M ≅ End_A(M) of finite projective modules (Mathlib dualTensorHomEquiv) it is φ ⊗ m ↦ φ(m) (Mathlib contractLeft). For M free it is Mathlib's LinearMap.trace (LinearMap.trace_eq_contract); for M not free LinearMap.trace is not used, because it is 0 by definition on a module without a finite basis. tr is Γ-equivariant onto the trivial representation; ad⁰ ρ := ker tr (the sl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iv) The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on ad ρ is perfect and Γ-invariant, and induces a Γ-isomorphism ad⁰ ρ ≅ (ad ρ / A·1)^∨ for every A. (v) If n ∈ A^×, then ad ρ = A·1 ⊕ ad⁰ ρ, the composite ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ → ad ρ/A·1 is an isomorphism, and the trace pairing restricts to a perfect pairing on ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ is self-dual. (vi) If A is a field of characteristic p with p | n, then A·1 ⊂ ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ contains the trivial representation, ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ/A·1 has kernel and cokernel of rank one, and the trace pairing on ad⁰ ρ is degenerate with radical A·1. For an arbitrary A ≠ 0: A·1 ∩ ad⁰ ρ = A[n]·1 (A[n] the n-torsion of A), the natural map ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ/A·1 has kernel A[n]·1 and cokernel A/nA, and under (iv) it is the map ad⁰ ρ → (ad⁰ ρ)^∨ of the trace pairing restricted to ad⁰ ρ; so each of the three conclusions of (v) holds if and only if n ∈ A^×. For A = Z_p and p | n the map is injective with cokernel Z_p/nZ_p ≠ 0, and A·1 ⊕ ad⁰ ρ is a proper submodule of finite index in ad ρ. The three modules ad ρ, ad⁰ ρ and ad ρ/A·1 are kept distinct throughout. (vii) Lie-algebra form: when M = A^n these are gl_n, sl_n and pgl_n := gl_n/scalars with the adjoint action of GL_n(A) through ρ. (viii) For a Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) on V (R01.2), ad(r, N) := (ad r, [N, −]) on End(V), a Weil–Deligne representation.
hypotheses: M finite projective of constant rank n ≥ 1
no hypothesis on n for (i)–(iv); n ∈ A^× for (v)
in (viii) the Weil–Deligne relation for ad follows from that of (r, N)
proofSteps: Use Representation.linHom ρ ρ (Mathlib) for the action. The isomorphism ρ^∨ ⊗ ρ ≅ ad ρ is dualTensorHomEquiv (M finite projective), Γ-equivariant by Mathlib Representation.dualTensorHom_comm. Continuity of the action map as for ρ ⊗ ρ^∨ (G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers and R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist). Over a complete normed field ContRepresentation.linHom (Tau Ceti) is the continuous counterpart, and ContRepresentation.conj_linHom identifies it with Representation.linHom in finite dimension.

Equivariance of the trace: for the contraction, (ρ^∨(g)φ)(ρ(g)m) = φ(m). The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on End_A(M) is perfect by G7/trace-pairing-on-matrices-is-perfect (matrices: dual basis E_ij ↔ E_ji; finite projective M: localisation). TauCeti.traceBilinForm_nondegenerate is the weaker statement that both kernels vanish, which over a ring does not give perfectness.
Duality (iv): the annihilator of A·1 under the trace pairing is ker tr = ad⁰, so the perfect pairing on ad induces ad⁰ ≅ (ad/A·1)^∨.
Splitting (v): X ↦ (tr X / n)·1 is an equivariant projection onto A·1 with kernel ad⁰; nondegeneracy on ad⁰ follows from (iv) and ad⁰ ≅ ad/A·1.
(vi): tr(1) = n (the contraction of the identity of a module of constant rank n, computed locally) and n = 0 in A, so 1 ∈ ad⁰ and tr(1·Y) = tr Y = 0 for Y ∈ ad⁰.
(viii): if r(w) N r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)} N (R01.2 normalisation) then r(w)[N, X]r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)}[N, r(w)Xr(w)^{−1}], and [N, −] is nilpotent.
acceptance: For n = 2 and 2 ∈ A^×, ad⁰ ρ ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊗ det ρ^{−1}; this is the Galois side of the Gelbart–Jacquet relation Ad(π) = Sym^2(π) ⊗ ω_π^{−1} used by GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4.
For n = p = char k (e.g. n = 2, k = F_2), the identity matrix lies in sl_n(k), so H^0(H, ad⁰) ≠ 0 for every subgroup H; this is why ACC+ note that no subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous when p | n.
CHT08 §2.1: for 𝒢_n-valued r, ad extends to 𝒢_n on gl_n with ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx, and over Z[1/2] the 𝒢_n-invariants of gl_n vanish (G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group).

nodes.title: The trace pairing on matrices, and on endomorphisms of a finite projective module, is perfect
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring. (1) For n ≥ 0 the trace form M_n(A) × M_n(A) → A, (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) (Tau Ceti traceBilinForm A n) is a perfect pairing (Mathlib LinearMap.IsPerfPair): X ↦ tr(X·) is an isomorphism M_n(A) → Hom_A(M_n(A), A), and the basis dual to the matrix units (E_{ij}) is (E_{ji}). (2) For a finite projective A-module M let tr : End_A(M) → A be the contraction trace (φ ⊗ m ↦ φ(m) under dualTensorHomEquiv : M^∨ ⊗ M ≅ End_A(M)). Then (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) is a perfect pairing on End_A(M).
hypotheses: perfect means that both maps to the dual are bijective; TauCeti.traceBilinForm_nondegenerate gives injectivity only, and over a ring that is not a field injectivity does not give bijectivity (the form 2xy on ℤ)
in (2) M is finite projective, not necessarily free or of constant rank; Mathlib's LinearMap.trace is not used for non-free M, where it is 0 by definition
proofSteps: (1): TauCeti.traceBilinForm_single_single gives ⟨E_{ij}(a), E_{kl}(b)⟩ = ab if j = k and l = i, and 0 otherwise. So X ↦ tr(X·) sends the basis (E_{ij}) of M_n(A) to the family (E_{ji}^*) of the dual basis, a bijection of bases; hence it is an isomorphism, and the form is symmetric (TauCeti.traceBilinForm_isSymm), which gives both conditions of IsPerfPair.

(2): End_A(M) is finite projective, so Θ : End_A(M) → End_A(M)^∨, X ↦ tr(X·), is a linear map between finite projective modules; by Mathlib bijective_of_localized_maximal it is bijective if its localisation at every maximal ideal is. Localisation commutes with End, with duals and with the contraction trace for finite projective modules (dualTensorHomEquiv is compatible with base change), M localised at a maximal ideal is free, and there the contraction trace is LinearMap.trace (LinearMap.trace_eq_contract), so (1) applies.
acceptance: n = 1: the pairing (x, y) ↦ xy on A is perfect.
n = 2 over ℤ: in the basis E_11, E_12, E_21, E_22 the Gram matrix of tr(XY) is the permutation matrix exchanging E_12 and E_21, of determinant −1.

Contrast (the reason the statement is about gl_n and not sl_n): on sl_2(ℤ) with basis h = diag(1, −1), e, f the Gram matrix of tr(XY) is (2 0 0; 0 0 1; 0 1 0), of determinant −2, so the restricted pairing is perfect only when 2 is invertible, as G7/adjoint-representations (v) states for n = 2.

sources.match: BCG25 use gl_n^{*,ss} ≃ gl_n^{ss}; the trace pairing gives gl_n^* ≅ gl_n before semisimplification and over any coefficient ring, which is this lemma. In the passage g⁰_n is sp_n or so_n, and the parenthesis says that (g⁰_n)^* is a quotient of gl_n^*, a submodule only after semisimplification; it is not a statement about the trace-zero matrices.

nodes.title: Similitude groups GSp and GO of a perfect form, with multiplier
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M a finite projective R-module with a perfect bilinear form B : M × M → R that is ε-symmetric (B(x, y) = εB(y, x), ε ∈ {±1}; for ε = −1 require B alternating, B(x, x) = 0). The similitude group scheme GAut(M, B) over R has points GAut(M, B)(R′) = {(g, ν) ∈ GL(M ⊗ R′) × R′^× : B(gx, gy) = ν B(x, y)}; ν is a character (the multiplier); since B is perfect and M has positive rank, ν is determined by g. Write GSp(M, B) for ε = −1 and GO(M, B) for ε = +1, and Sp, O for the kernels of ν. Matrix forms: GSp_{2m} := GSp(R^{2m}, J_{2m}) with J_{2m} = (0, 1_m; −1_m, 0) (BLGGT §1.1), GO_n := GO(R^n, 1_n), and for GSp_4 the antidiagonal matrix J = (0, s; −s, 0), s = (0 1; 1 0), that is antidiag(1, 1, −1, −1), which BCGP21 (§2.1.1, condition gJᵗg = ν(g)J) and CG20 (§2.1, condition ᵗMJM = ν·J) both use: the two conditions define the same subgroup of GL_4 with the same ν because J^{−1} = −J, and P = diag(1_2, s) satisfies ᵗPJP = J_4, so g ↦ P^{−1}gP identifies it with GSp_4 for J_4; BCG25's G_n is GSp_n (n even, A_n = J_n) or GO_n (n odd, A_n = 1_n). Lie algebras: gsp/go = {X : B(Xx, y) + B(x, Xy) = c B(x, y), c ∈ R}, with sp/so the kernel of dν. If 2 ∈ R^×, gsp(M, B) = sp(M, B) ⊕ R·1, the scalar line being central with trivial adjoint action, and dν(1) = 2. A determinant constraint: g ∈ GSp_{2m}(R) has det g = ν(g)^m, and g ∈ GO_n(R) has (det g)^2 = ν(g)^n.
hypotheses: B perfect (the map M → M^∨, x ↦ B(x, −), is an isomorphism), not merely nondegenerate
alternating forms are required for the symplectic case so that characteristic 2 is covered; then rank M is even
the splitting gsp = sp ⊕ scalars needs 2 ∈ R^×
proofSteps: The functor of points is represented by a closed subgroup scheme of GL(M) × G_m: in a basis with Gram matrix G (B(x, y) = ᵗxGy) it is cut out by the entries of ᵗgGg − νG. Tau Ceti's ConstantForm construction uses the relation XCXᵀ − C, and XCXᵀ = tC is equivalent to ᵗXC^{−1}X = tC^{−1}; so GAut(M, B) is the group of the constant form C = G^{−1} with an extra G_m coordinate t (the Hopf ideal generated by the entries of XCXᵀ − tC in O(GL_n × G_m), TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.hopfIdealOrderIsoClosedSubgroup), extending the case ν = 1 (TauCeti.ConstantForm.groupScheme, TauCeti.Symplectic.groupScheme, TauCeti.Orthogonal.groupScheme). For G = J_{2m}, the antidiagonal J and 1_n one has G^{−1} = ±G, so gGᵗg = νG and ᵗgGg = νG define the same group; this is why BLGGT, CHT, BCGP21 and CG20 may put the transpose on either side.

Points: Sp_{2m}(R) is Mathlib's Matrix.symplecticGroup. Its J = fromBlocks 0 (−1) 1 0 is −J_{2m}, and AJAᵀ = J is the same equation for J and −J, so only the index types (Fin m ⊕ Fin m against Fin (2m)) have to be matched; O_n(R) is Matrix.orthogonalGroup (AAᵀ = 1).
Multiplier is a homomorphism and determined by g: perfectness of B.
Lie algebra splitting for 2 ∈ R^×: X ↦ X − (c/2)·1 (the computation recorded in sourceIssues E701); Ad(g) fixes scalars, and Ad(g) preserves c because ν(g) cancels.

det g = ν^m on GSp_{2m}: Mathlib SymplecticGroup.det_eq_one says that a matrix in Matrix.symplecticGroup l R (any commutative ring R) has determinant 1. For g with gJᵗg = νJ put D = diag(1_m, ν^{−1}·1_m); then DJᵗD = ν^{−1}J, so gD is symplectic and 1 = det(gD) = det(g)·ν^{−m}. For m = 1 this is Tau Ceti's Matrix.det_eq_of_transpose_mul_J_mul_eq_smul, and Matrix.transpose_mul_J_mul_eq_det_smul says that every 2 × 2 matrix scales J by its determinant. (det g)^2 = ν^n on GO_n by taking determinants of gᵗg = ν·1.
acceptance: GSp_2 = GL_2 with ν = det: every 2 × 2 matrix satisfies gJᵗg = det(g)J (Tau Ceti Matrix.transpose_mul_J_mul_eq_det_smul, in the form AᵀJA = det A • J for Mathlib's rank-two J).
For R = F_7 and n = 7, the form B_6 on Sym^6 F_7^2 of G7/symmetric-power-polarization is identified up to scalar with 1_7, so Sym^6 of a GL_2(F_7)-valued representation lands in GO_7(F_7).
For p > 2 and k a field of characteristic p, gsp_4(k) = sp_4(k) ⊕ k·1_4 has dimension 11 = 10 + 1 with trivial action on the scalar line (CG20, corrected).

nodes.title: Polarized representations: an actual pairing, a multiplier and a sign
nodes.statement: (a) Group-theoretic form. Let Γ be profinite, Δ ≤ Γ an open subgroup of index at most 2, A a topological commutative ring and (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Δ A M of rank n. For c ∈ Γ with c^2 = 1, and c ∉ Δ when Δ ≠ Γ, a polarization of ρ at c is a pair (μ, ⟨ , ⟩) of a continuous character μ : Γ → A^× and a perfect A-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : M × M → A such that ⟨ρ(σ)x, ρ(cσc)y⟩ = μ(σ)⟨x, y⟩ for all σ ∈ Δ, x, y ∈ M, and ⟨x, y⟩ = ε⟨y, x⟩ for a sign ε = ε_c ∈ {±1} (for ε = −1 the pairing is required to be alternating when 2 ∉ A^×; ε is a formal sign and the identity is read in A, so when 2 = 0 in A it holds for both signs and ε is part of the data; BLGGT impose no alternating condition). (b) Number fields (BLGGT §2.1). Let F be CM or totally real with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; for F imaginary (Mathlib NumberField.IsCMField) take Γ = G_{F⁺}, Δ = G_F: every complex conjugation c_v ∈ G_{F⁺} at a real place v of F⁺ (NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal) restricts on F to Mathlib's NumberField.IsCMField.complexConj F (NumberField.IsCMField.isConj_complexConj), so G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F is the set of elements restricting to complexConj F; for F = F⁺ take Δ = Γ = G_F (then cσc ∈ G_F). A polarized representation of G_F is (ρ, μ) with ρ ∈ ContinuousRep G_F A M and μ : G_{F⁺} → A^× continuous, together with, for some real place v of F⁺ and complex conjugation c_v ∈ G_{F⁺} at v, a sign ε_v and a pairing as in (a) at c = c_v; when F is imaginary one further requires ε_v = −μ(c_v). (c) CHT form: for any γ_0 ∈ Γ ∖ Δ (no condition γ_0^2 = 1), a triple (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) with μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ_0 δ γ_0^{−1})y⟩ for δ ∈ Δ and ⟨x, ρ(γ_0^2)y⟩ = −μ(γ_0)⟨y, x⟩; for γ_0 = c_v this is (b) with ε_v = −μ(c_v), provided −μ(c_v) is a sign and, when ε_v = −1 and 2 ∉ A^×, the pairing is alternating (the identity of CHT gives only 2⟨x, x⟩ = 0, which suffices when 2 is not a zero divisor in A; over Z/4, with Δ = 1, Γ = Z/2 and μ = 1, the perfect pairing with Gram matrix (2 1; −1 0) is a CHT triple, skew-symmetric and not alternating): μ(c_v)^2 = 1 always, and μ(c_v) = ±1 follows when A is a domain, or when 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A is connected, but not in general (A = F_2[t]/(t^2) with μ(c_v) = 1 + t; A = Q × Q with μ(c_v) = (1, −1)), and then a CHT triple is not a polarization in the sense of (a). The pair (ρ, μ) is a polarized pair in the sense of BLGGT if some v, ε_v and pairing exist (a property of the pair), and ρ is polarizable if some μ makes (ρ, μ) a polarized pair; essentially conjugate self-dual (ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ|_{G_F}) is the weaker condition with no pairing. A polarized representation is the data (ρ, μ, v, ⟨ , ⟩), not the property.
hypotheses: ⟨ , ⟩ perfect: the map M → M^∨ is an isomorphism (over a field, nondegenerate)
the coefficient ring is arbitrary (fields E/Q_ℓ, finite fields, complete local Noetherian rings, Q̄_ℓ), so the same definition serves l-adic, mod l and deformation-theoretic uses

for F imaginary the condition ε_v = −μ(c_v) is part of the definition; for F totally real it is not imposed, and when 2 ∈ A^× the representation ρ then factors through GSp or GO of the form ⟨x, ρ(c_v)y⟩_v according to μ(c_v) = −ε_v or μ(c_v) = ε_v; one of the two holds when Spec A is connected (BLGGT assert this for Q̄_l, and for F̄_l only when l > 2)
mod l with l = 2: alternating and symmetric pairings differ, so ε alone does not determine the type; the alternating requirement is recorded
proofSteps: Definition; nothing is proved. The change-of-place formula, and the independence of the place v when μ(c_v c_{v′}) = ±1 (always over a domain, or when 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A is connected; not over every ring), are G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (1), which is proved from this definition and is not used by it.

For F imaginary and γ_0 = c_v, (b) and (c) are the same data: with γ_0^2 = 1 the second identity of (c) reads ⟨x, y⟩ = −μ(c_v)⟨y, x⟩, i.e. ε_v = −μ(c_v). The dictionary with 𝒢_n-valued extensions (CHT08 Lemma 2.1.1) is G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group, which builds on this node.
Totally real case: ⟨x, y⟩′ := ⟨x, ρ(c_v)y⟩_v is G_F-equivariant up to μ and has symmetry εμ(c_v), giving the GSp/GO factorisation (BLGGT §2.1 bullet three).
acceptance: n = 1, F imaginary CM: a polarized character (ψ, μ) has ψ^c = ψ^{−1}μ|_{G_F}, and since a perfect pairing on a line is symmetric, ε_v = 1, so μ(c_v) = −1 (totally odd automatically).
n = 2, F imaginary quadratic, ρ the restriction to G_F of r : G_Q → GL_2(E) with det r(c) = −1: the pairing ⟨x, y⟩ = det(x, r(c)y) polarizes (ρ|_{G_F}, det r) with ε = +1.

F totally real, n = 2, 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A connected: any ρ is polarized by ⟨x, y⟩ = det(x, ρ(c_v)y) with μ = det ρ and ε_v = −det ρ(c_v), so ρ factors through GSp_2 = GL_2 (μ(c_v) = −ε_v). Without the two hypotheses det ρ(c_v) need not be a sign, and for ε_v = −1 the pairing need not be alternating: over Z/4 with ρ(c_v) = (1 2; 0 1), det(e_2, ρ(c_v)e_2) = −2 ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Sign, change of place, determinant and parity constraints of a polarization
nodes.statement: Let (ρ, μ) be polarized at a real place v of F⁺ with pairing ⟨ , ⟩_v and sign ε_v (G7/polarized-representation), ρ of rank n over A. (1) Change of place: for another real place v′, ⟨x, y⟩_{v′} := ⟨x, ρ(c_v c_{v′})y⟩_v satisfies the covariance identity at c_{v′} and ⟨y, x⟩_{v′} = μ(c_v c_{v′})ε_v⟨x, y⟩_{v′}. It polarizes (ρ, μ) at v′, with ε_{v′} = μ(c_v c_{v′})ε_v, when μ(c_v c_{v′}) ∈ {±1} (always when A is a domain, or when 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A is connected; in general only μ(c_v c_{v′})^2 = 1 and μ(c_v c_{v′})^n = 1 hold) and, if ε_{v′} = −1 and 2 ∉ A^×, when ⟨ , ⟩_{v′} is alternating (automatic if 2 is not a zero divisor in A); for F imaginary the condition ε_{v′} = −μ(c_{v′}) then holds at v′. Without the condition on μ(c_v c_{v′}) the place matters: for F imaginary, A = k × k with k a field of characteristic ≠ 2, χ a character of G_F and η a quadratic character of G_{F⁺} with η(c_v) = −1 and η(c_{v′}) = 1, the pair ρ = (χ ⊕ (χ^c)^{−1}, χ ⊕ (χ^c)^{−1}η|_{G_F}), μ = (δ_{F/F⁺}, η) is polarized at v by the hyperbolic symmetric pairing on each component (ε_v = 1 = −μ(c_v)) and is not polarized at v′, where −μ(c_{v′}) = (1, −1) is not a sign. (2) Determinant: det ρ(c_v σ c_v)·det ρ(σ) = μ(σ)^n for σ ∈ G_F; for F totally real (det ρ)^2 = μ^n, and if moreover ρ is symplectic, meaning that the form ⟨x, ρ(c_v)y⟩_v is alternating (this follows from μ(c_v) = −ε_v when 2 is not a zero divisor in A), then n is even and det ρ = μ^{n/2}. (3) Parity: if ⟨ , ⟩′ := ⟨ , ρ(c_v)·⟩ (F totally real) or the pairing itself (CHT, γ_0^2 = 1) is alternating and perfect on a free module over a nonzero ring, n is even. (4) Uniqueness and the intrinsic sign: if A = k is a field and ρ is absolutely irreducible with ρ^{c} ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ|_{G_F}, then a pairing satisfying the covariance identity exists, is unique up to k^×, and its symmetry sign is determined by (ρ, μ): ρ(γ^2)ᵗb_γ = ±μ(γ)b_γ with the sign −sgn(ρ, μ) independent of γ ∈ G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F; (ρ, μ) is polarized iff sgn(ρ, μ) = 1, and otherwise (ρ, μδ_{F/F⁺}) is (BLGGT §1.1, CHT Lemma 2.1.4). The homomorphisms r : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(k) with r|_{G_F} = (ρ, μ|_{G_F}) and r(G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F) ⊄ 𝒢_n^0(k), taken up to GL_n(k)-conjugacy, form a torsor under k^×/(k^×)^2 (α scales the GL_n-component of r(γ) for γ ∉ G_F), and all of them have the same multiplier ν ∘ r ∈ {μ, μδ_{F/F⁺}}. When char k = 2 the sign is not defined (1 = −1) and (ρ, μ) is always polarized. (5) Similitude ambiguity (GSp_4, BCGP21 Lemma 8.3.1): if ρ : G_K → GL_4(Q̄_p) is irreducible and preserves symplectic forms with similitude characters ν and νψ, ψ ≠ 1, then ψ has finite order and ρ is reducible over a quadratic subfield of the field cut out by ψ.
hypotheses: (4) requires absolute irreducibility; for reducible ρ the pairing need not be unique and the sign need not be defined

in (2) the symplectic conclusion det ρ = μ^{n/2} is the determinant constraint of G7/similitude-groups (proved there from Mathlib's SymplecticGroup.det_eq_one) and holds over any ring for an alternating form; (det ρ)^2 = μ^n alone does not determine det ρ
(5) is stated over Q̄_p for a number field K as in the source

(1): the transported pairing polarizes (ρ, μ) at v′ only when μ(c_v c_{v′}) ∈ {±1} in A; this holds when A is a domain, or when 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A is connected, and it can fail otherwise (over k × k with k a field of characteristic ≠ 2 the pair given in the statement is polarized at v and not at v′); BLGGT state the change of place for Q̄_l and F̄_l only
proofSteps: (1): direct computation using c_{v′} c_v ∈ G_F and the covariance identity; BLGGT §2.1 first bullet (stated there over Q̄_l and F̄_l, where μ(c_v c_{v′}) = ±1). Covariance at c_{v′}: with τ = c_v c_{v′} ∈ G_F one has τ·c_{v′}σc_{v′} = c_vσc_{v′} = (c_vσc_v)τ, so ⟨ρ(σ)x, ρ(c_{v′}σc_{v′})y⟩_{v′} = ⟨ρ(σ)x, ρ(c_vσc_v)ρ(τ)y⟩_v = μ(σ)⟨x, y⟩_{v′}. Symmetry: c_v τ^{−1} c_v = τ, so ⟨y, x⟩_{v′} = ε_v⟨ρ(τ)x, y⟩_v = ε_v μ(τ)⟨x, ρ(τ)y⟩_v = ε_v μ(τ)⟨x, y⟩_{v′}. The unit μ(τ) = μ(c_v)μ(c_{v′}) has square 1, and μ(τ)^n = 1 by (2) applied to σ = τ (c_vτc_v = τ^{−1}). It is ±1 when A is a domain, or when 2 ∈ A^× and Spec A is connected ((1 + μ(τ))/2 is then an idempotent), and it can differ from ±1 otherwise: (1, −1) in k × k, 1 + t in F_2[t]/(t^2), 3 in Z/8, and the class of x in Z[x]/(x^2 − 1), a ring with connected spectrum in which 2 is not a zero divisor.

(2): take determinants in the matrix form ᵗρ(σ) P ρ(cσc) = μ(σ) P of the covariance identity (P the Gram matrix); in the totally real case use G7/similitude-groups (det g = ν^m on GSp_{2m}, (det g)^2 = ν^n on GO_n).
(3): an alternating matrix of odd size has determinant 0 over any commutative ring.
(4): BLGGT §1.1 (Schur's lemma applied to ρ(γ^2δγ^{−2}) computed two ways) and CHT08 Lemma 2.1.4 (existence of the 𝒢_n-valued extension, and the k^×/(k^×)^2 classification by α ↦ r_α).
(5): BCGP21 Lemma 8.3.1: ν ⊕ νψ ⊂ Hom(V^*, V) gives V ≅ V(ψ), so ψ^4 = 1 by determinants, and a quadratic η with V ≅ V(η) makes V reducible over the fixed field of η by Schur.
acceptance: n = 1, F imaginary: (ψ, μ) polarized forces μ(c_v) = −1 at every v, consistent with (1) since μ(c_v c_{v′}) = 1.
F totally real, n = 2, symplectic: det ρ = μ (GSp_2 = GL_2).
BLGGT §1.1 rank-one example: for χ with χχ^{γ_0} = μ|_Δ and χ(γ_0^2) = −μ(γ_0), (χ, μ) is a 𝒢_1-valued homomorphism with ν = μ.

nodes.title: Operations on polarized representations: dual, twist, tensor, powers, restriction, coefficients
nodes.statement: Let F be CM with F⁺ ≠ F (imaginary case) and δ := δ_{F/F⁺} : G_{F⁺} → {±1} the quadratic character, so δ(c_v) = −1. For polarized (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩, ε) and (ρ′, μ′, ⟨ , ⟩′, ε′) of G_F over A at the same c_v (G7/polarized-representation) define: (1) dual: (ρ^∨, μ^{−1}) with the transported pairing ⟨φ^{−1}f, φ^{−1}g⟩ (φ : M → M^∨ the pairing map), sign ε; (2) twist by a continuous character χ : G_F → A^×: (ρ ⊗ χ, μ·(χ ∘ Ver)) with the same pairing, where Ver : G_{F⁺}^{ab} → G_F^{ab} is the transfer, so (χ ∘ Ver)|_{G_F} = χχ^c and (χ ∘ Ver)(c_v) = 1; sign ε; (3) tensor product: (ρ ⊗ ρ′, μμ′δ) with pairing ⟨x ⊗ x′, y ⊗ y′⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩⟨x′, y′⟩′, sign εε′; (4) exterior powers, k ≥ 1: (∧^k ρ, μ^k δ^{k−1}) with the determinant pairing ⟨x_1∧…∧x_k, y_1∧…∧y_k⟩ = det(⟨x_i, y_j⟩), sign ε^k, for every A; (5) symmetric powers, k ≥ 1, when k! ∈ A^×: (Sym^k ρ, μ^k δ^{k−1}) with the permanent pairing (1/k!)Σ_{s∈S_k}∏_i⟨x_i, y_{s(i)}⟩, sign ε^k; (6) direct sum of two polarizations with the same μ and ε at the same c_v: orthogonal sum; (7) restriction to a CM field L ⊃ F with L = L⁺F (L⁺ ⊃ F⁺ the maximal totally real subfield of L): (ρ|_{G_L}, μ|_{G_{L⁺}}) with the same pairing at the real place of L⁺ above v at which c_v is a complex conjugation; (8) coefficient extension along continuous A → B: (ρ ⊗_A B, μ ⊗ B, ⟨ , ⟩ ⊗ B). In each case the output satisfies the CM sign condition. For F totally real the same formulas hold with δ replaced by 1, with χ ∘ Ver replaced by χχ^{c_v} = χ^2 in (2) (the multiplier of ρ ⊗ χ is μχ^2), and with no sign condition; the type sign ε_vμ(c_v) of the form ⟨x, ρ(c_v)y⟩_v (−1: GSp, +1: GO, for 2 ∈ A^×) is multiplicative under ⊗ and is raised to the k-th power by ∧^k and Sym^k. The quadratic correction δ is invisible on G_F and is required at c_v.
hypotheses: F imaginary CM, both inputs polarized at the same c_v (use G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (1) to move places)
(5) needs k! ∈ A^×: for k ≥ char A the permanent pairing is degenerate (G7/symmetric-power-polarization)
(6): with different multipliers or signs the block pairing is not a polarization of one pair

(7): c_v fixes the totally real field L⁺, so c_v ∈ G_{L⁺}, and it is a complex conjugation at exactly one real place w of L⁺ above v; the pairing is kept at that w. The complex conjugations at the other real places of L⁺ above v are conjugate to c_v in G_{F⁺}, not in G_{L⁺} (conjugacy classes of complex conjugations in G_{L⁺} correspond to the real places of L⁺); to move to them use G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (1) over L

in the group-theoretic form (Δ ≤ Γ, c) of G7/polarized-representation (a) the new multipliers are characters of Γ determined by their values on Δ and at c: μχχ^c, μμ′, μ^k on Δ and μ(c), −μ(c)μ′(c), (−1)^{k−1}μ(c)^k at c ∉ Δ; such characters exist for Δ of index two (through the transfer and δ) and need not exist for a subgroup of larger index (Γ = S_4, Δ the Klein four-group, c = (12), ρ trivial of rank one with μ the sign character, χ a character of Δ with χ((12)(34)) = −1: the character χχ^c of Δ does not extend to S_4)
proofSteps: Each output pairing is perfect: (1) by transport; (3) tensor product of perfect pairings on finite projective modules; (4) ∧^k of a perfect pairing is perfect (∧^k M^∨ ≅ (∧^k M)^∨ for finite projective M); (5) perfect when k! ∈ A^× (symmetrisation is then a split projection).
Covariance: multiplicative in the factors; on G_F, δ is trivial, so the covariance multiplier is μμ′ (resp. μ^k).
Sign: transposition multiplies by εε′ (resp. ε^k by expanding det or perm of the transposed matrix).

CM sign condition: −(μμ′δ)(c_v) = −(−ε)(−ε′)(−1) = εε′; −(μ^kδ^{k−1})(c_v) = −(−ε)^k(−1)^{k−1} = ε^k; for twists, (χ ∘ Ver)(c_v) = χ(c_v^2) = 1 by the cycle formula for the transfer (Mathlib MonoidHom.transfer_eq_prod_quotient_orbitRel_zpowers_quot: c_v permutes the two cosets of G_F in one orbit of length 2).

Restriction and coefficient extension: immediate from the definitions; BLGGT §1.1 records the corresponding statements for 𝒢_n-valued maps (multiplier of r ⊗ r′ differs from μμ′ by the nontrivial character of Γ/Δ).
acceptance: Two totally odd inputs give a totally odd tensor product: ε = ε′ = 1 ⇒ εε′ = 1 (R24.5 consumer statement).

For ρ = ψ a polarized character (ε = 1, μ(c_v) = −1), ψ ⊗ ψ has multiplier μ^2δ with (μ^2δ)(c_v) = −1, again totally odd; without δ the multiplier μ^2 would have value +1 at c_v and violate the CM sign condition.
k = 0 convention: the unit representation A with pairing (a, b) ↦ ab and multiplier δ is polarized with sign +1, which is the value of μ^kδ^{k−1} at k = 0 because δ^{−1} = δ.

uses.how: duality, tensor (μμ′δ, εε′), ∧^k and Sym^k (μ^kδ^{k−1}, ε^k), twists, restriction

the ⊗ map (𝒢_n × 𝒢_m)^+ → 𝒢_{nm} is the 𝒢-valued form of (3)

nodes.title: Oddness at real places: polarized sign, similitude value and eigenspace balance
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and v a real place (Mathlib NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal; CM fields are NumberField.IsCMField); c_v ∈ G_F denotes a complex conjugation at v (the image of complex conjugation under G_ℝ → G_F for an embedding F̄ → ℂ extending v; its conjugacy class [c_v] depends only on v). (a) Polarized oddness (BLGGT §2.1): a polarized (ρ, μ) of G_F, F CM or totally real, is totally odd if ε_v = 1 in A for every real place v of F⁺, where ε_v := μ(c_{v_0}c_v)ε_{v_0} ∈ A for the place v_0 of the given polarization (the symmetry factor at v of G7/polarization-sign-and-determinant (1); it is an element of A with square 1, not always a sign). The equalities are read in A, as in BLGGT, and not for the formal sign of G7/polarized-representation (a): over a field of characteristic 2 (more generally a reduced ring with 2 = 0) every polarized pair is totally odd, whatever formal sign its polarization carries; over F_2[t]/(t^2) this fails (μ(c_v) can be 1 + t). When F is imaginary, totally odd is equivalent to μ(c_v) = −1 in A for all v | ∞ (ε_v = μ(c_{v_0})μ(c_v)·(−μ(c_{v_0})) = −μ(c_v)). (b) Group-valued oddness: a continuous r : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(A) with r^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(A)) = G_F (F imaginary) is totally odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 for all v; r : G_F → GSp_{2m}(A) (F totally real) is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 for all v; r : G_F → GO_n(A) is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = +1 for all v. (c) Rank one (ACC+ §1.2): a continuous character μ : G_K → A^× of a totally real K is totally odd if μ(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞; this is the predicate TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsTotallyOddChar of R01.4/odd-representation. (d) Unpolarized balance (CG18 §8.4, corrected): for V of dimension n over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, V is odd at a real place v in the sense of Calegari–Geraghty, here called balanced at v (predicate IsBalancedAt), if the (±1)-eigenspaces of ρ(c_v) have dimensions differing by at most one (no condition at complex places). In characteristic 0 this is Tr ρ(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}; in characteristic ℓ the trace criterion is equivalent to it exactly when ℓ > n + 1 (n even) or ℓ > n (n odd). (e) Rank two: for n = 2 and characteristic ≠ 2, (d) at v ⇔ det ρ(c_v) = −1 ⇔ (ρ, det ρ) is odd as a GSp_2-valued representation, which is R01.4/odd-representation. Oddness in dimension n is the sign condition (a)/(b), not the rank-two determinant test.
hypotheses: a polarization (or a similitude-group valued representation) is required for (a), (b); (d) is a separate unpolarized notion, used by CG18 for GL_n
characteristic ≠ 2 in (d) so that c_v is diagonalisable with eigenvalues ±1
in characteristic 2 the rank-two condition 'ρ̄(c) ≠ 1' is a different condition and is R01.4's
proofSteps: (a)⇔(μ(c_v) = −1) for F imaginary: ε_v = −μ(c_v) by definition.

Consequences (CHT08 Lemma 2.1.3): for r : Γ → 𝒢_n(k), char k ≠ 2, c ∈ Γ ∖ Δ with c^2 = 1, dim_k gl_n^{c=η} = n(n + ην(r(c)))/2; for totally odd r the c-invariants of ad have dimension n(n − 1)/2. For GSp_4 with ν(c) = −1 and p > 2, r(c) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, −1, −1) with isotropic eigenspaces and dim H^0(⟨c⟩, sp_4) = 4 (CG20, Proposition 4.9 use).

(d): if c_v has eigenspaces of dimensions a, b, then, for n = a + b ≥ 1, dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ V) = a^2 + b^2 − 1 (the centraliser of ρ(c_v) is gl_a × gl_b, on which the trace is non-zero), minimal exactly when |a − b| ≤ 1, which gives CG18's formula Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad⁰ V) = [F:Q] n(n−1)/2 + l_0; Tr ρ(c_v) = a − b computed in the field (sourceIssues E702).
(e): for n = 2 the eigenvalue multiset {1, −1} is the balanced case and has determinant −1; GSp_2 = GL_2 with ν = det.
acceptance: An odd ρ : G_Q → GL_2(E) restricted to an imaginary quadratic F is totally odd polarized with multiplier det ρ (pairing det(x, ρ(c)y)).
The cyclotomic character χ_ℓ of a totally real field is totally odd (χ_ℓ(c_v) = −1); the trivial character is not.
Non-example to the trace test (sourceIssues E702): over F_3 with n = 2 and ρ(c) = 1, Tr ρ(c) = 2 = −1 but the eigenspaces have dimensions 2 and 0, so V is not odd; similarly n = 4, F_5, ρ(c) = ±1.

api.name: TauCeti.GaloisRep.complexConj
api.statement: c_v ∈ G_F for a real place v and an extension of v to F̄, with conjugacy class independent of the extension: the element c_ι of R01.4/odd-representation (1), used here for the real places of F⁺.

api.name: TauCeti.PolarizedRep.IsTotallyOdd
api.statement: ε_v = 1 in A for all real v of F⁺, with ε_v = μ(c_{v_0}c_v)ε_{v_0} computed in A from the place v_0 of the polarization.

api.name: TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsBalancedAt
api.statement: The eigenspace-balance condition (d) at a real place v: |dim V^{c_v = 1} − dim V^{c_v = −1}| ≤ 1 (field of characteristic ≠ 2). It is not R01.4's IsOddAt (det ρ(c_v) = −1), with which it agrees only for n = 2.

api.name: TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBalancedAt_iff_trace
api.statement: In characteristic 0, or ℓ > n + 1 (n even), ℓ > n (n odd): IsBalancedAt ⇔ Tr ρ(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}.

api.name: TauCeti.GaloisRep.dim_invariants_adZero_complexConj
api.statement: dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ V) = a^2 + b^2 − 1 for eigenspace dimensions a + b = n ≥ 1 (for n = 0 the left side is 0); its minimum n^2/2 − 1 (n even) or (n^2 + 1)/2 − 1 (n odd) is attained exactly when V is balanced at v.

nodes.title: The group scheme 𝒢_n and the dictionary with polarized triples
nodes.statement: 𝒢_n is the group scheme over Z given as the semidirect product of 𝒢_n^0 = GL_n × GL_1 by {1, j}, with j(g, μ)j^{−1} = (μ ᵗg^{−1}, μ); the multiplier ν : 𝒢_n → GL_1 sends (g, μ) ↦ μ and j ↦ −1; 𝒢_n^0 is the identity component. The adjoint action on gl_n = Lie GL_n ⊂ Lie 𝒢_n is ad(g, μ)(x) = gxg^{−1}, ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx. Dictionary (CHT08 Lemma 2.1.1): for a group Γ with an index-two subgroup Δ (open if Γ is topological), a ring R and γ_0 ∈ Γ ∖ Δ, homomorphisms r : Γ → 𝒢_n(R) inducing Γ/Δ ≅ 𝒢_n/𝒢_n^0 correspond bijectively to triples (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) with ρ : Δ → GL_n(R), μ : Γ → R^×, ⟨ , ⟩ perfect on R^n, ⟨x, ρ(γ_0^2)y⟩ = −μ(γ_0)⟨y, x⟩ and μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ_0δγ_0^{−1})y⟩; here μ = ν ∘ r, ⟨x, y⟩ = ᵗx A^{−1} y where r(γ_0) = (A, −μ(γ_0))j, and continuous r correspond to continuous ρ. Auxiliary maps: ⊗ : (𝒢_n × 𝒢_m)^+ → 𝒢_{nm}, (g, a) × (g′, a′) ↦ (g ⊗ g′, aa′), j × j ↦ j; I : 𝒢_n → GSp_{2n}; for a similitude group G_n with form matrix A_n (G7/similitude-groups) the injection G_n × {±1} → 𝒢_n, (g, 1) ↦ (g, ν(g)), (g, −1) ↦ (g, ν(g))·(A_n^{−1}, (−1)^{n+1})j, with ν(r((g, s))) = ν(g)s^n, and hence r_ψ : G_Q → 𝒢_n(R) for ψ : G_Q → G_n(R) and an imaginary quadratic F (BCG25 (2.1.2)); the rank-one maps (χ, μ) : Γ → 𝒢_1(R); and CHT's induction: for Γ′ ⊂ Γ of finite index not contained in Δ, Δ′ = Δ ∩ Γ′, χ : Γ → R^×, γ_0 ∈ Γ′ ∖ Δ′ and r′ : Γ′ → 𝒢_n(R) with ν ∘ r′ = χ|_{Γ′} and Δ′ = (r′)^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(R)), corresponding to the triple (ρ′, χ|_{Γ′}, ⟨ , ⟩′), the homomorphism Ind^{Γ,Δ,χ}_{Γ′,Δ′} r′ : Γ → 𝒢_{n[Γ:Γ′]}(R) corresponds to (ρ, χ, ⟨ , ⟩), where ρ is right translation on the functions f : Δ → R^n with f(δ′δ) = ρ′(δ′)f(δ) for δ′ ∈ Δ′, and ⟨f, f′⟩ = Σ_{δ ∈ Δ′∖Δ} χ(δ)^{−1}⟨f(δ), f′(γ_0δγ_0^{−1})⟩′; it is independent of γ_0 and has multiplier χ (CHT08 pp. 8–9).
hypotheses: Γ/Δ ≅ 𝒢_n/𝒢_n^0 is part of the hypothesis on r (r(Δ) ⊂ 𝒢_n^0 and r(Γ ∖ Δ) ⊂ 𝒢_n^0 j)
the convention for GSp/GO is gA_nᵗg = ν(g)A_n; with ᵗgA_ng = νA_n the same group results
𝒢_n-invariants of gl_n vanish only over Z[1/2]
proofSteps: Group-scheme structure: the semidirect product of two affine group schemes by an automorphism of order 2 (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 0 functor of points; product and constant group {1, j}).

Lemma 2.1.1 (CHT08 p. 7): write r(γ_0) = (A, −μ(γ_0))j; the relation r(γ_0)r(δ)r(γ_0)^{−1} = r(γ_0δγ_0^{−1}) is the covariance identity for ⟨x, y⟩ = ᵗxA^{−1}y, and r(γ_0)^2 = r(γ_0^2) is the symmetry identity; conversely define r(γ_0) from the Gram matrix.

The map (2.1.2) of BCG25 agrees with r̂_Δ of BLGGT §1.1 and with CHT Lemma 2.1.2 (r(γ) = (ρ(γ)J^{−1}, (−1)^a μ(γ))j, ν ∘ r = δ_{Γ/Δ}^{a+1}μ): (g, ν(g))·(A_n^{−1}, (−1)^{n+1})j = (gA_n^{−1}, (−1)^{n+1}ν(g))j, which is (gJ_n^{−1}, −ν(g))j for n even and (g, ν(g))j for n odd. It is a homomorphism: with e = (−1)^{n+1}, the element z = (A_n^{−1}, e)j satisfies z^2 = (e·A_n^{−1}ᵗA_n, e^2) = 1 (A_n = 1_n and e = 1, or A_n = J_n, ᵗJ_n = −J_n and e = −1), and z(g, ν(g))z^{−1} = (ν(g)A_n^{−1}ᵗg^{−1}A_n, ν(g)) = (g, ν(g)) because ᵗgA_ng = ν(g)A_n. Finally ν(z) = e·ν(j) = (−1)^n, so ν(r((g, s))) = ν(g)s^n.
⊗ and I are homomorphisms by direct computation (BLGGT §1.1); (χ, μ) is a homomorphism by BLGGT's displayed verification.
Polarized dictionary over CM fields: Γ = G_{F⁺}, Δ = G_F, γ_0 = c_v gives G7/polarized-representation (b) with ε_v = −μ(c_v).

nodes.title: Polarization of symmetric powers of a rank-two symplectic representation
nodes.statement: Let F be a field in universe 0 (F : Type, as Sym[F]^d requires), d ≥ 1 with d! ∈ F^× and 2 ∈ F^×, n = d + 1, V = F^2 with an alternating perfect form h, and r : Γ → GL(V) with h(r(g)x, r(g)y) = μ(g)h(x, y), μ = det r. The normalized symmetrization B_d(u_1⋯u_d, w_1⋯w_d) = (1/d!)Σ_{s∈S_d}∏_j h(u_j, w_{s(j)}) is a well-defined perfect bilinear form on Sym^d V with B_d(Sym^d r(g)u, Sym^d r(g)w) = μ(g)^d B_d(u, w) and B_d(w, u) = (−1)^d B_d(u, w). In a basis x, y with h(x, y) = 1 and v_i = x^{d−i}y^i, B_d(v_i, v_j) = 0 unless i + j = d and B_d(v_i, v_{d−i}) = (−1)^i / binom(d, i). Hence Sym^d r takes values in GSp(Sym^d V, B_d) for d odd (n even) and GO(Sym^d V, B_d) for d even (n odd), with multiplier μ^d. Identification with G_n (G7/similitude-groups): for n even there is P with ᵗP B_d P = J_n; for n odd and F finite of odd characteristic there are P and c ∈ F^× with ᵗP B_d P = c·1_n (scale to match the discriminant square class, then use the classification of nondegenerate quadratic forms over finite fields); over a general field the odd case is an extra hypothesis. When d! ∉ F^× (char F = p ≤ d) the form B_d is not defined and the d!-scaled antidiagonal form (−1)^i i!(d−i)! is degenerate; whether Sym^d r still preserves a perfect form then depends on d and on the image. It does not for p = 7 and d = 7: the space of SL_2(F_7)-invariant bilinear forms on Sym^7 F_7^2 is one-dimensional and spanned by a form of rank 6. It does for d = 2p − 1, where Sym^d of the standard representation of SL_2 is irreducible (for p = 3, 5, 7 a direct computation with SL_2(F_p) finds an invariant form of full rank d + 1).
hypotheses: 2 and d! invertible in F (in characteristic p: n ≤ p)
r preserves an alternating perfect form with multiplier det r (automatic for GL_2)
the symmetric identification with 1_n is asserted only over finite fields of odd characteristic (or algebraically closed fields)
proofSteps: Symmetrization is invariant under permuting each argument separately, so B_d descends from V^{⊗d} × V^{⊗d} to Sym^d V × Sym^d V (on the existing Sym^d of G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers: the action is Representation.symmetricPower r d on Sym[F]^d V, and the monomials v_i = x^{d−i}y^i are the basis Module.Basis.symmetricPower of the basis x, y); equivariance multiplies each of the d factors h by μ(g).

Monomial computation: B_d(v_i, v_j) counts matchings of i copies of y and d − i copies of x on the left with the right factors; only i + j = d contributes, with value (−1)^i i!(d−i)!/d!. All binomial coefficients are units when d! is, so the antidiagonal Gram matrix is invertible; transposition multiplies by (−1)^d.

Identification: alternating perfect forms have symplectic bases; symmetric forms over finite fields of odd characteristic are classified by rank and discriminant, and scaling by c changes the discriminant by c^n, n odd.

Degenerate and exceptional cases for d ≥ p: solving ᵗgBg = B for the two elementary generators of SL_2(F_p) on Sym^d F_p^2 shows that the invariant bilinear forms form a line for p = 7, d = 5, 6, 7, 8, of rank 6, 7, 6, 5, and for p = 5, d = 3, 4, 5, of rank 4, 5, 4; the d!-scaled antidiagonal form with entries (−1)^i i!(d−i)! spans it, and its rank is the number of i with p ∤ i!(d−i)!. For d = 2p − 1 and p = 3, 5, 7 the same computation gives a space of invariant forms of dimension 3, 2, 2 containing a form of full rank.
acceptance: d = p − 2 = 5, p = 7 (n = 6): B_5 is alternating of rank 6 and invariant under SL_2(F_7): Sym^5 r lands in GSp_6(F_7) with multiplier μ^5.

d = p − 1 = 6, p = 7 (n = 7): B_6 is symmetric of rank 7; its d!-scaled Gram matrix has all antidiagonal entries −1 (Wilson's theorem), so Sym^6 r lands in GO_7(F_7) with multiplier μ^6 (BCG25 Theorem 3.1 uses n = p with multiplier ε̄^{(1−k)(p−1)} = 1).
d = p = 7: no nondegenerate invariant form exists (rank 6 < 8), so no GSp_8 conclusion; BCG25's multiplier bookkeeping ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄^∨ε̄^{1−n} for n = p − 1, p − 2.

Over F = ℝ with d = 2, B_2 has signature (1, 2) (Gram matrix antidiag(1, −1/2, 1) in the basis x^2, xy, y^2), so it is not a scalar multiple of 1_3 up to isometry: keep GO(B_2) unless an identification is supplied.

nodes.title: GSp_4-valued representations: oddness, adjoint modules, and symplectic induction from index two
nodes.statement: Let A be a topological commutative ring with 2 ∈ A^× and F a number field (in the sources totally real or Q). (i) A GSp_4-valued representation is a continuous r : G_F → GSp_4(A) (G7/similitude-groups; BCGP21 and CG20 use the same antidiagonal J, which the permutation matrix diag(1_2, (0 1; 1 0)) carries to J_4), with similitude character ν ∘ r; it is odd if ν(r(c_v)) = −1 at every real v. For A a field and r odd, r(c_v) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, −1, −1) with Lagrangian eigenspaces and dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ r) = 4. (ii) Adjoint modules of the GSp_4-valued r; they are submodules of End_A(A^4) = ad(std ∘ r) of G7/adjoint-representations, whose trace kernel (rank 15) is a different module from sp_4: ad r := gsp_4 with Ad ∘ r (rank 11); ad⁰ r := sp_4 (rank 10) = Lie(Sp_4) = Lie(PGSp_4) = asp⁰ r for 2 ∈ A^×; ad r = ad⁰ r ⊕ A with trivial action on the scalar line A·1_4 (not ⊕ ν); ad⁰ r ≅ Sym^2(r) ⊗ (ν ∘ r)^{−1} and ad⁰ r is self-dual via the trace form. (iii) Symplectic induction (BCGP21 §2.2): let K/F be quadratic with nontrivial character η_{K/F}, σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_K, ρ : G_K → GL(V), V free of rank 2 over a field L, with det ρ = χ|_{G_K} for a character χ of G_F. On W = V ⊕ σV (a model of Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ, R01.1/continuous-induction) choose a nondegenerate alternating form on V, make V ⊥ σV, and set ⟨σv_1, σv_2⟩ = ±χ(σ)⟨v_1, v_2⟩; the two signs give ρ_1, ρ_2 : G_F → GSp(W) with similitude characters χ and χη_{K/F}, and ∧^2 Ind ρ contains χ and χη_{K/F}. In BCGP21's J, the image of {(A, B) ∈ GL_2 × GL_2 : det A = det B} is the set of g ∈ GSp_4 with zero pattern rows (∗,0,0,∗), (0,∗,∗,0), (0,∗,∗,0), (∗,0,0,∗). For ρ with det ρ = ε^{−1}, Ind ρ denotes the symplectic induction with similitude ε^{−1}; for an elliptic curve E/K it is the dual Tate module of Res_{K/F} E with its Weil-pairing polarization. (iv) ad⁰ of an induction (characteristic ≠ 2): ad⁰(Ind ρ)|_{G_K} ≅ (ρ ⊗ ρ^σ) ⊗ χ^{−1} ⊕ ad⁰ ρ ⊕ ad⁰ ρ^σ and ad⁰(Ind ρ) ≅ As(ρ) ⊗ ν^{−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰ ρ for the symplectic induction with similitude ν ∈ {χ, χη_{K/F}}, where As(ρ) is the tensor induction of G7/tensor-induction for the transversal {1, σ}: the summand V·σV of Sym^2(V ⊕ σV) is As(ρ) itself (σ sends v·σv′ to ρ(σ^2)v′·σv), and V∧σV ⊂ ∧^2(V ⊕ σV) is As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F}.
hypotheses: 2 ∈ A^× (for ad = ad⁰ ⊕ A and for sp_4 = Lie PGSp_4)
in (iii) det ρ must extend to G_F; the two polarizations differ by η_{K/F}
the Weil-pairing statement is a comparison with R01.6/AbelianSchemes (A3, A6) and is recorded as a use, not proved here
proofSteps: (i): ⟨cv, cw⟩ = ν(c)⟨v, w⟩ = −⟨v, w⟩ makes both eigenspaces isotropic, hence Lagrangian; the centraliser of diag(1,1,−1,−1) in sp_4 is the Siegel Levi gl_2 (CG20 proof of Proposition 4.9).

(ii): G7/similitude-groups (gsp = sp ⊕ scalars for 2 invertible, scalars trivial under Ad); the printed '⊕ ν' (CG20 p. 813) is corrected (sourceIssues E701). Sym^2 W ⊗ ν^{−1} ≅ sp(W) via x·y ↦ (z ↦ ⟨x, z⟩y + ⟨y, z⟩x)/ν, Γ-equivariant up to the multiplier.

(iii): BCGP21 §2.2; consistency of the definition of the form on σV uses σ^2 ∈ G_K and det ρ(σ^2) = χ(σ)^2; equivariance under G_K and σ is a direct check; the block description by writing W = V ⊕ σV in the basis adapted to J.
(iv): compute over G_K using ρ^∨ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ^{−1} (rank two) and descend with G7/tensor-induction (As) and Mackey (R01.1/mackey-decomposition) (CG20 Example 4.11; BCGP21 §7.5.16).
acceptance: BCGP21: for K/F a quadratic extension of number fields and E/K an elliptic curve, Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} of the dual p-adic Tate module of E is GSp_4-valued with similitude ε^{−1}, and is the dual Tate module of Res_{K/F}E.

CG20 Example 4.11: for K/Q imaginary quadratic and ρ̄ : G_K → GL_2(F_p), p > 2, with det ρ̄ = ε^{1−k}, the symplectic induction r̄ = Ind ρ̄ whose similitude character ν ∈ {ε^{1−k}, ε^{1−k}η_{K/Q}} has ν(c) = −1 (ν = ε^{1−k} for k even, ε^{1−k}η_{K/Q} for k odd) is odd GSp_4-valued, and ad⁰(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ν^{−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰(ρ̄); CG20 print As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} and leave the quadratic twist of As open.
dim gsp_4 = 11, dim sp_4 = 10, and over F_p, p > 2, the scalar line in gsp_4 is a trivial summand.

nodes.title: Semisimple GSp_4-valued representations are determined by GL_4 × GL_1 (characteristic ≠ 2)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a group and L an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2. Two semisimple representations r, r′ : Γ → GSp_4(L) are GSp_4(L)-conjugate if and only if their composites Γ → GSp_4(L) → GL_4(L) × GL_1(L) (underlying representation and similitude character) are GL_4(L) × GL_1(L)-conjugate, i.e. the underlying GL_4-representations are isomorphic and ν ∘ r = ν ∘ r′. In characteristic 2 the statement is false.
hypotheses: L algebraically closed, char L ≠ 2 (BCGP21 states no characteristic hypothesis; sourceIssues E703)
semisimple means semisimple as a GL_4-representation; for char ≠ 2 this is equivalent to GSp_4-complete reducibility
proofSteps: Let V = L^4 with two Γ-invariant-up-to-ν alternating perfect forms B, B′ (the second transported by an isomorphism of GL_4-representations). Decompose V = ⊕_W W ⊗ Hom_Γ(W, V) into isotypic parts; a form with multiplier ν pairs the W-isotypic part with the (W^∨ ⊗ ν)-isotypic part.

For W ≇ W^∨ ⊗ ν the form is determined, up to the action of GL of the multiplicity spaces, by an isomorphism of multiplicity spaces; for W ≅ W^∨ ⊗ ν, with W carrying a unique (Schur) invariant form of sign s_W, the form on the isotypic part is s_W ⊗ (form of sign −s_W on the multiplicity space); over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2 nondegenerate symmetric and alternating forms of a given rank are unique up to isometry.
Hence (V, B) ≅ (V, B′) Γ-equivariantly, i.e. r′ = g r g^{−1} with g ∈ GSp_4(L) (indeed Sp-similar); BCGP21 refer to the proof of Gan–Takeda Lemma 6.1 (gap).

Characteristic 2 counterexample (sourceIssues E703): Γ = SL_2(F_2), W its two-dimensional representation with the alternating form B_W, V = W ⊗ L^2 with the forms B_W ⊗ S for S = (0 1; 1 0) and for S = 1_2. Both are alternating on V (B_W is), Γ-invariant and perfect, so they give two Sp_4-valued representations with the same underlying GL_4-representation and trivial similitude. An element of GL_4(L) commuting with Γ is 1 ⊗ z with z ∈ GL_2(L) (W is absolutely irreducible), and it carries B_W ⊗ S to B_W ⊗ ᵗzSz; no z and scalar c give ᵗz(0 1; 1 0)z = c·1_2, because the left side is alternating and 1_2 is not. So the two are not GSp_4(L)-conjugate.
acceptance: Two GSp_4-valued representations Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ with similitude χ and with χη_{K/F} (G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction) have isomorphic GL_4-representations but different similitude characters, so the lemma does not identify them, as it must not.
For r = ρ_1 ⊕ ρ_2 with ρ_i : Γ → GL_2(L) semisimple and det ρ_1 = det ρ_2 = ν (orthogonal sum), any GSp_4-valued r′ with the same GL_4-representation and similitude ν is GSp_4-conjugate to r.

nodes.title: Strongly irreducible representations
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ K V with K a field (a finite extension of Q_ℓ, Q̄_ℓ, or a finite field). ρ is strongly irreducible if ρ|_{Γ′} is irreducible for every open subgroup Γ′ ≤ Γ. For Γ = G_F, F a field, this says ρ|_{G_L} is irreducible for every finite separable extension L/F inside F^sep; for Γ = G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} the quantifier runs over finite extensions of F(ζ_{p^∞}). Absolutely strongly irreducible: ρ ⊗_K K̄ strongly irreducible. For K of characteristic 0 and ρ semisimple, ρ ⊗ K̄ is strongly irreducible iff the identity component G_ρ^0 of the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ) acts irreducibly on V ⊗ K̄ (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups).
hypotheses: the quantifier is over all open subgroups (all finite extensions), not only over the given group
irreducible, not absolutely irreducible, unless stated; the absolute variant is a separate predicate
proofSteps: Definition. Characterisation via G^0 (characteristic 0): Γ^0 := ρ^{−1}(G_ρ^0(K̄)) is open of finite index; for open Γ′ the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ′ ∩ Γ^0) is G_ρ^0 (finite-index subgroups of a connected group's dense subgroup are dense: [Bor91, Ch. I §1.2]), and a subspace is ρ(Γ′ ∩ Γ^0)-stable iff it is G_ρ^0-stable; conversely every open Γ′ contains an open subgroup of Γ^0.
acceptance: Non-example: for K/F quadratic and ψ a character of G_K with ψ ≠ ψ^σ, Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ψ is irreducible but not strongly irreducible (its restriction to G_K is ψ ⊕ ψ^σ).

Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F with CM by an imaginary quadratic K ⊄ F. Over Q̄_p, V_pE ⊗ Q̄_p is irreducible over G_F and reducible over G_{FK} (it is the sum of two characters): not absolutely strongly irreducible. Over Q_p the answer depends on p: if p splits in K, V_pE is reducible over G_{FK}; if p is inert or ramified in K, V_pE is a line over the field K ⊗ Q_p on which every open subgroup of G_{FK} acts through a character with open image, so V_pE is irreducible on every open subgroup: strongly irreducible but not absolutely strongly irreducible. For E/Q without CM, V_pE is absolutely strongly irreducible (Serre's open image theorem gives G_ρ^0 = GL_2).

NT26: for F totally real and π a non-CM RAESDC representation of GL_2(𝔸_F), r_{π,ι} is strongly irreducible ([NT23, Example 2.29], cited by NT26 p. 10; the automorphic input belongs to the roadmap that owns r_{π,ι}).

nodes.title: Zariski closures of subgroups and the monodromy group of a representation
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, G an affine group scheme of finite type over K and Σ ⊂ G(K) a subgroup. The Zariski closure Σ̄ ⊂ G is the closed subgroup scheme defined by the Hopf ideal I(Σ) = {f ∈ O(G) : f(σ) = 0 for all σ ∈ Σ} (Tau Ceti's Hopf-ideal/closed-subgroup classification); it is reduced, Σ ⊂ Σ̄(K), and it is the smallest closed subgroup scheme whose K-points contain Σ. For a field K with an algebraically closed extension Ω, closures are formed over Ω and Σ̄_Ω = (Σ̄)_Ω. For (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ K V the monodromy group G_ρ is the Zariski closure of ρ(Γ) in GL(V), with identity component G_ρ^0 (formed after base change to an algebraic closure, TauCeti identityComponent), component group π_0(G_ρ) and Γ^0 := ρ^{−1}(G_ρ^0(K̄)), an open normal subgroup of finite index; for Γ = G_F the field F_ρ^0 := (F^sep)^{Γ^0} is finite Galois over F with Gal(F_ρ^0/F) ≅ ρ(Γ)/(ρ(Γ) ∩ G_ρ^0(K̄)) ≅ π_0(G_ρ)(K̄) (ρ(Γ) is Zariski dense, so it meets every connected component). Facts ([Bor91, Ch. I §§1–2]): (a) for a homomorphism α : H → H′ of affine algebraic groups over an algebraically closed field Ω and a subgroup Σ ⊂ H(Ω), the closure of α(Σ) is α(Σ̄); (b) the closure of the commutator subgroup [Σ, Σ] is the derived group D(Σ̄) ([Bor91, Ch. I §2.4]); (c) in characteristic 0, if ρ is semisimple then G_ρ^0 is reductive (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 6: faithful semisimple representation); (d) in characteristic 0 a connected reductive subgroup of GL_2 acting irreducibly is SL_2 or GL_2, and its image in PGL_2 is PGL_2; (e) for Ω algebraically closed of characteristic 0, a closed subgroup G ⊂ PGL_2 × PGL_2 whose two projections are surjective is either PGL_2 × PGL_2 or the graph of an automorphism φ of the algebraic group PGL_2: by G7/simplicity-of-pgl2-over-an-algebraically-closed-field (3) the group G(Ω) is everything or the graph of an abstract automorphism; in the second case the first projection G → PGL_2 is bijective on Ω-points, and a homomorphism of algebraic groups in characteristic 0 that is bijective on Ω-points is an isomorphism (gap). The differential dφ is then a linear automorphism of Lie(PGL_2) = sl_2 with dφ ∘ Ad(a) = Ad(φ(a)) ∘ dφ for all a. Consequently a subgroup Σ ⊂ PGL_2(Ω) × PGL_2(Ω) with Zariski dense projections is either Zariski dense or contained in the graph of such a φ, and in the second case the representations Ad ∘ pr_1 and Ad ∘ pr_2 of Σ on sl_2 are isomorphic. That φ is inner is true and is not used.
hypotheses: closures are defined for subgroups of K-points; for Γ profinite and ρ continuous the closure ignores the topology of Γ
the identity component is geometric (after base change to an algebraically closed field), as in Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 3
(c)–(e) are characteristic-0 statements; (a) holds over any algebraically closed field
proofSteps: I(Σ) is a Hopf ideal: if f vanishes on Σ then Δf vanishes on Σ × Σ, and the map O(G)/I ⊗ O(G)/I → Fun(Σ × Σ, K) is injective (tensor product of injections into function spaces), so Δf ∈ I ⊗ O + O ⊗ I; S(f) and ε(f) similarly. Then Tau Ceti hopfIdealOrderIsoClosedSubgroup gives the closed subgroup scheme.
Base change: I(Σ) ⊗ Ω = I_Ω(Σ) by linear algebra (functions on Σ with values in K vs Ω).

Γ^0 open of finite index: G_ρ^0 has finite index in G_ρ (π_0 finite, Tau Ceti component group results) and ρ(Γ) ∩ G_ρ^0(K̄) is a finite-index subgroup closed in ρ(Γ), hence open since ρ(Γ) is compact.

(a), (b): [Bor91, Ch. I §2.1(f) and §2.4], as cited by NT26. (a): α(Σ̄) is closed (the image of a homomorphism of algebraic groups is closed) and contains α(Σ); conversely the preimage under α of the closure of α(Σ) is a closed subgroup containing Σ. (b): the commutator map is continuous, so [Σ̄, Σ̄] lies in the closure of [Σ, Σ], which is a subgroup; conversely D(Σ̄) is closed and contains [Σ, Σ]. The two inputs, closedness of images and of derived groups, are recorded in the gap on Borel.
(c): a faithful semisimple representation in characteristic 0 forces trivial unipotent radical (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 6, linearly reductive characterisation).

(d): ReductiveGroups layer 6 (requested). (e): G7/simplicity-of-pgl2-over-an-algebraically-closed-field (3) (Mathlib Subgroup.goursat with the simplicity of PGL_2(Ω)) gives the alternative on Ω-points. In the graph case the first projection is a bijective homomorphism of algebraic groups, an isomorphism in characteristic 0 (gap), so φ = pr_2 ∘ pr_1^{−1} is an automorphism of the algebraic group PGL_2, and the adjoint representation is functorial for isomorphisms of algebraic groups (ReductiveGroups layer 2, requested): dφ ∘ Ad(a) = Ad(φ(a)) ∘ dφ.
acceptance: For ρ = 1 ⊕ χ_ℓ (χ_ℓ the cyclotomic character of G_Q, ℓ-adic), G_ρ = {diag(1, t)} ≅ G_m and G_ρ^0 = G_ρ; for ρ of finite image, G_ρ is the finite constant group ρ(Γ) and G_ρ^0 = 1, F_ρ^0 the field cut out by ρ.
NT26 Lemma 2.2: for ρ strongly irreducible G_F → GL_2(Q̄_p), the closure of Proj ρ(G_F) is PGL_2.
Non-example: over K = F_q, the closure of GL_2(F_q) ⊂ GL_2 is the finite constant group scheme, not GL_2; the dense-subgroup statements (d), (e) are for infinite images in characteristic 0.

nodes.title: PGL_2 of an algebraically closed field is a simple group
nodes.statement: Let Ω be an algebraically closed field. (1) The composite SL_2(Ω) → GL_2(Ω) → PGL_2(Ω) = GL_2(Ω)/Ω^× is surjective with kernel {±1}; so PGL_2(Ω) ≅ PSL_2(Ω). (2) PGL_2(Ω) is a simple group. More generally PSL_2(K) is simple for every field K with more than three elements. (3) Consequently, a subgroup G of PGL_2(Ω) × PGL_2(Ω) whose two projections are surjective is either the whole product or the graph of an automorphism of the abstract group PGL_2(Ω).
hypotheses: Ω algebraically closed for (1) (square roots of determinants) and to have more than three elements; (2) is a statement about abstract groups, no topology or algebraic structure
PSL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 and PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4 are not simple
proofSteps: (1): for g ∈ GL_2(Ω) choose λ with λ^2 = det g; λ^{−1}g ∈ SL_2(Ω) has the same class. A scalar of determinant 1 is ±1.

(2), Iwasawa's criterion (Mathlib MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup): PSL_2(K) acts faithfully on the projective line P^1(K), and doubly transitively, hence primitively (so quasi-primitively). For a line L let T(L) be the image of the group of transvections 1 + N with N^2 = 0 and image L; it is commutative, T(gL) = gT(L)g^{−1}, and the T(L) generate, because SL_2(K) is generated by the elementary matrices (transvections). SL_2(K) is perfect when K has more than three elements: for a ∈ K with a^2 ≠ 0, 1 the commutator of diag(a, a^{−1}) with the elementary matrix u(b) is u((a^2 − 1)b), so every elementary matrix is a commutator. The criterion gives simplicity.

(3): Goursat's lemma (Mathlib Subgroup.goursat) presents G through normal subgroups N_1, N_2 of the two factors and an isomorphism PGL_2(Ω)/N_1 ≅ PGL_2(Ω)/N_2 whose graph is the image of G; by (2) each N_i is trivial or everything, and N_1 is everything exactly when N_2 is.
acceptance: PSL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 and PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4 have proper non-trivial normal subgroups: the bound |K| > 3 is sharp.
In PGL_2(ℂ) the normal subgroup generated by the class of diag(1, −1) is everything.
For the diagonal G = {(g, g)} ⊂ PGL_2(Ω)^2 the alternative in (3) is the graph of the identity; for G = PGL_2(Ω)^2 it is the whole product.

nodes.title: Tensor products of symmetric powers with unequal Hodge–Tate differences are strongly irreducible after cyclotomic restriction
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime, and ρ, ρ′ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_p) continuous and strongly irreducible. Suppose there is an embedding τ : F → Q̄_p inducing a place v | p such that ρ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ′|_{G_{F_v}} are Hodge–Tate with HT_τ(ρ) = {a, b}, HT_τ(ρ′) = {a′, b′} and a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′). Then (i) the Zariski closure of the image of Proj ρ × Proj ρ′ : G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_p) × PGL_2(Q̄_p) is PGL_2 × PGL_2; (ii) for all m, m′ ≥ 1, (Sym^m ρ ⊗ Sym^{m′} ρ′)|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}} is strongly irreducible.
hypotheses: both representations strongly irreducible (not merely irreducible)
the weight condition a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′) at one embedding τ; equal differences allow ρ′ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ, where (i) fails
the condition a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′) does not depend on the sign convention for Hodge–Tate weights (HT(χ_p) = +1 in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention)
proofSteps: Closure of Proj ρ(G_F) is PGL_2: G_ρ is reductive (faithful irreducible representation), G_ρ^0 acts irreducibly (strong irreducibility, G7/strong-irreducibility), so G_ρ^0 ∈ {SL_2, GL_2} (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups (c), (d)); image in PGL_2 is PGL_2 by fact (a).

Let G be the closure of the image of Proj ρ × Proj ρ′; its two projections are surjective by step 0 and fact (a). By G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups (e), either G = PGL_2 × PGL_2, or G is the graph of an automorphism φ of the algebraic group PGL_2. In the second case Proj ρ′ = φ ∘ Proj ρ, and since ad⁰ ρ = Ad ∘ Proj ρ on sl_2 (G7/adjoint-representations), dφ is an isomorphism ad⁰ ρ ≅ ad⁰ ρ′ of representations of G_F; so their Hodge–Tate weights {a − b, 0, b − a} and {a′ − b′, 0, b′ − a′} at τ agree (weights of ad⁰ from PadicHodgeTheory R06.2: ⊗ and duals), contradicting the hypothesis. NT26 pass through 'every automorphism of PGL_2 is inner'; functoriality of Ad is enough.

Cyclotomic restriction: Gal(F(ζ_{p^∞})/F) is abelian, so the image of G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} under ρ × ρ′ contains the commutator subgroup of (ρ × ρ′)(G_F); its closure contains the derived group of the closure of (ρ × ρ′)(G_F) (fact (b); NT26's printed product of images is the image of ρ × ρ′, sourceIssues E704), which contains SL_2 × SL_2 because the latter closure surjects onto PGL_2 × PGL_2.

The same holds for every open subgroup of G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})} (finite-index subgroups have the same identity component), and Sym^m ⊗ Sym^{m′} is irreducible for SL_2 × SL_2 in characteristic 0; G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers supplies the representations.
acceptance: NT26 application: ρ = r_{π,ι}, ρ′ = r_{σ,ι} attached to non-CM Hilbert eigenforms of different weights (parallel weight 2 and parallel weight 3 differ: a − b = 1 vs 2), so Sym^m r_π ⊗ Sym^{m′} r_σ is strongly irreducible over F(ζ_{p^∞}).
Failure without the weight hypothesis: ρ′ = ρ ⊗ χ for a character χ has equal weight differences, and Sym^1 ρ ⊗ Sym^1 ρ′ ≅ (Sym^2 ρ ⊕ det ρ) ⊗ χ is reducible.

nodes.title: Lifting projective Galois representations through central torus quotients (Tate's theorem)
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and ℓ a prime. (1) (Tate; Conrad) Every continuous P : G_F → PGL_n(Q̄_ℓ) lifts to a continuous ρ : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ); more generally, for a surjection H′ → H of linear algebraic groups over Q̄_ℓ with kernel a central torus, every continuous G_F → H(Q̄_ℓ) lifts to a continuous G_F → H′(Q̄_ℓ). (2) Any two lifts to GL_n differ by a continuous character G_F → Q̄_ℓ^×. (3) If P is unramified at all but finitely many places, so is every lift. The only arithmetic input is Tate's theorem H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4); no p-adic Hodge theory is used. Lifts with control of Hodge–Tate weights are G7/lifting-projective-representations-hodge-tate.
hypotheses: F a number field. The vanishing is not special to global fields: H^2(G_K, Q/Z) = 0 also for K a finite extension of Q_p and for K = ℝ, ℂ (the proof of Patrikis Theorem 2.1.1 starts from the completions; by local duality H^2(G_K, Z/n) is dual to μ_n(K), the transition maps for n | n′ are dual to x ↦ x^{n′/n} : μ_{n′}(K) → μ_n(K), and the limit vanishes because μ(K) is finite), so (1) and (2) hold for G_K as well, and Patrikis Remark 2.1.7 uses (1) for K/Q_ℓ finite. What can be obstructed, for local and global fields alike, is lifting through an isogeny, or lifting without enlarging the coefficient field (Patrikis Example 2.1.2, Remark 2.1.5). Only the global case is stated here
coefficients Q̄_ℓ with its ℓ-adic topology; enlarging the coefficient field is essential (Patrikis Remark 2.1.5): a representation valued in H(E) lifts in general only over E(μ_n) for n large
(3) is about places not dividing ℓ as well as those dividing ℓ: unramified at all but finitely many places
proofSteps: (1): Patrikis Proposition 2.1.4 (Conrad [Con11, Prop. 5.3]). Reduce to kernel G_m; choose an isogeny complement H′_1 ⊂ H′ with H′_1 ∩ G_m = μ_{n_0}, and for n_0 | n put H′_n = H′_1·μ_n, an isogeny onto H with kernel μ_n. The image of G_F lies in H(E) for a finite E/Q_ℓ (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field), and the central extension by μ_n pulled back to G_F is a topological central extension of a profinite group by a finite group, with a class c_n ∈ H^2(G_F, Z/n) (ProfiniteCohomology layer 10, requested); the c_n are compatible for n | n′, and lim_n H^2(G_F, Z/n) = H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0 (Tate; requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4), so c_n = 0 for n large, which gives a continuous lift to H′_n(Q̄_ℓ) ⊂ H′(Q̄_ℓ).

(2): for two lifts ρ_1, ρ_2 the matrix ρ_1(g)^{−1}ρ_2(g) is a scalar χ(g) depending continuously on g, and χ is a character because scalars are central: ρ_2 = ρ_1 ⊗ χ (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist).

(3): let ρ be a lift. Its image is compact and lies in GL_n(E) for a finite E/Q_ℓ (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field), so after conjugation in GL_n(O_E); let U = 1 + ℓ^2 M_n(O_E), an open torsion-free subgroup, and F″ the finite extension of F cut out by ρ^{−1}(U). A continuous character χ : G_F → Q̄_ℓ^× is unramified almost everywhere: for v ∤ ℓ the group χ(I_v) is finite (R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence in dimension one: N = 0), and for v unramified in the finite extension cut out by χ^{−1}(1 + ℓ^2 O_E) it lies in a torsion-free group, hence is trivial. Now let v ∤ ℓ be a place at which P and the character det ρ are unramified and which is unramified in F″. Then ρ(I_v) consists of scalar matrices ψ_v(g)·1, with ψ_v^n = det ρ|_{I_v} = 1; so ρ(I_v) is a finite subgroup of U, hence trivial. (Patrikis quotes a lemma of Conrad for this, as [Con11, Lemma 5.2] in Remark 2.1.5 and as Lemma 5.3 in the proof of Lemma 2.7.4; it is not needed.)
acceptance: n = 2, projective image dihedral: P = Proj Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} θ lifts to Ind θ, and every other lift is Ind θ ⊗ χ.

Finite-group non-example: the projective representation (Z/2)^2 → PGL_2(Q̄_ℓ) sending the generators to the classes of diag(1, −1) and (0 1; 1 0) does not lift to a homomorphism (Z/2)^2 → GL_2(Q̄_ℓ) (any lifts anticommute); for a Galois group G_F of a number field surjecting onto (Z/2)^2 the inflated projective representation does lift, by (1), with larger image.

Coefficients: the projectivisation of the Tate module of an elliptic curve over a totally real field does not lift to SL_2(Q̄_ℓ), because the cyclotomic character has no square root (Patrikis Example 2.1.2); it lifts to GL_2, as (1) says.
